Consumers that require live Rust protocol callbacks can compose the existing stream parsers with Tokio process pipes. This language-specific API distinction is recorded rather than claiming identical callbacks.\n\n## Root causes and fixes\n\n### Catalogue drift and incompatible native flags\n\nThe two bindings embedded separate, older model maps. Hive Mind moved to a centralized catalogue with live exact IDs; the dependency continued to publish older aliases/defaults. The replay compares all 206 entries against the pinned catalogue. JavaScript now shares one generated catalogue; Rust maps are generated from the same data. Legacy keys absent from the source remain accepted. Unknown exact IDs continue through unchanged, leaving validation and capability discovery to the caller.\n\nClaude's old inline `--prompt` path did not match native print invocation, and JSON commands did not always request print/verbose output. Builders now use native `-p` and add `--verbose` when stream JSON is selected. Resuming Gemini was dropped by the common builder; OpenCode used a different backend's `--resume` flag; Agent advertised no resume despite Hive Mind using `--resume ... --no-fork`. All six common resume paths now map to the native contract.\n\n### Snapshots, final totals and cache accounting\n\nA single “sum every usage object” strategy double-counted Claude/Qwen final totals and repeated snapshots. OpenCode's native usage lives in `part.tokens`, while Gemini often reports `result.stats.models[*].tokens`. Rust's controller dropped Qwen/Gemini usage entirely. Codex's inclusive input concealed cached reads, making its output incompatible with Hive Mind's fresh-input accounting.\n\nThe parsers now select final totals when present, otherwise deduplicate identified snapshots; Agent/OpenCode sum native steps. Codex reports fresh input and cache reads separately, with nested cache/reasoning vocabulary retained. This is a deliberate documented semantic change. The simple fixture `input=100, cached=80` changes from input 100 to input 20 plus cache reads 80. Reasoning may already belong to native output totals and must not be added again for billing.\n\n### Process status and session status\n\nExit code zero does not prove an agent completed its turn. An interrupted JSON stream previously passed even after init/turn-started events; signal exits with no numeric status were also treated as zero in JavaScript. The new state tracker follows the last native turn. Direct JSON controllers also reject empty or unrecognized output without completion evidence. Plain/generic command execution retains exit semantics when no native lifecycle is observed.\n\nA terminal success supersedes earlier recoverable transport errors and quoted usage-limit text; errors emitted after it still fail. Claude events with `parent_tool_use_id` are diagnostics for a subagent and cannot replace the parent's verdict, summary or totals. Those raw events remain available, and actual native Task/Agent/collaboration records are exposed separately. This follows the main-thread boundary fixed upstream in PR #2302; it does not automatically implement Hive Mind's background-task continuation policy.\n\n### Framing, deadlocks and shell transport\n\nCombining stderr with stdout before JSON parsing let a diagnostic JSON line change session identity, usage or success. Both bindings now parse stdout independently. Raw output still includes diagnostics for callers' investigations. JavaScript uses incremental UTF-8 decoding so chunk boundaries cannot corrupt multibyte characters.\n\nRust previously waited/read in an order that could deadlock when stderr filled its pipe before stdout closed. Reader tasks now start immediately and drain both pipes concurrently, with attached writes and byte-preserving collection. The finite regression emits 128 KiB to stderr then `done` to stdout; a five-second test bound makes the old deadlock reproducible without exhausting memory. Cancelling signals the direct Unix process group, waits for readers and cleans up prompts. Unregistering a Rust signal handler no longer invokes its cleanup callback.\n\nThe previous safe-word heuristic left shell metacharacters unquoted when no spaces were present. A narrow safe-character allowlist and proper quoting of the working directory preserve arguments such as `one;two'&three|four` and paths with spaces. Prompt files continue to keep large user text out of command strings.\n\n## Timeline and experimental evidence\n\n| Stage on 2026-10-07              | Observation and action                                                                                                                                 |\n| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| Initial research                 | Read issue/PR context and contributing rules; collect current Hive Mind tree/adapter/catalogue and merged work; verify native documentation            |\n| First reproduction               | Add minimum fixture tests before changes; both languages fail native usage, catalogue and session cases; bounded Rust stderr probe times out           |\n| First implementation             | Synchronize catalogues, fix native parsing/usage/headless flags, concurrent process reads, quoting and cancellation                                    |\n| Compatibility validation         | Full suites expose stale model/Claude prompt assertions; update expectations while retaining pinned aliases                                            |\n| Consumer audit                   | Five new reproductions expose scoped results, recovered errors, missing subagent records and empty success; fix both bindings                          |\n| Native resume and usage audit    | Reproduce OpenCode/Agent resume and alternate nested usage fields; implement backend-specific flags and field vocabulary                               |\n| Runtime and packaging validation | Deno's controller tests require write permission; add it to script/CI. Its turn events provide a native completion boundary. Model capability selection remains the consumer's job.\n- [Claude Code headless documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless) describes print mode, stream JSON with verbose output, session continuation and final result fields. This supports the native flags and result-total handling.\n- [Gemini headless documentation](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/headless/) describes text, single JSON and streaming JSON outputs, result statistics, error records and process status. These facts motivate nonzero signal status and Unix group cancellation.\n- [Tokio process documentation](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/process/) covers asynchronous process management and `kill_on_drop`. Concurrent readers avoid pipe backpressure while waiting for the child.\n\nRecent upstream work directly relevant to the dependency:\n\n| Merged Hive Mind PR                                            | General execution implication                                                                                               |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [#1044](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/1044) | Existing experimental dependency adapter for all six tools; fixes:\n75\t\n76\t- **Model catalogue** synced to v2.39.5: Claude 5.5 family, Codex `sol`/`luna`/`astra`, the Kilo default for Agent, OpenCode `big-pickle`, the Qwen catalogue (`4367abf`, `0f729b9`). Both parsers now read multi-line and back-to-back records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`). A shared JSON-lines parser and model mapper replaced the per-tool copies first (`872657e`).\n78\t- **Agent fatal errors on stderr.** The agent 0.26.15 source (`src/cli/output.ts`) prints only fatal errors, such as an unknown model, to stderr, so the metadata said only \"Process exited with code 1\". A failed exit with no error event on stdout now uses the last JSON error record of the output (`6ec13f1`, reproduced by [experiments/agent-stderr-error.mjs](../../../experiments/agent-stderr-error.mjs)).\n79\t- **Rust generic-tool quoting.** `build_tool_command` used a single-quote escape inside double quotes, so bash expanded `$`, backticks and `\"`. It now uses `escape_arg` like JS (`05d7264`).\n80\t- **Rust detached process group.** `execute_detached` left the child in the caller's process group, so Ctrl+C to the caller also stopped the agent. Node's `detached: true` makes the child \"the leader of a new process group and session\". The Rust helper now sets `process_group(0)`. `test_execute_detached_leads_its_own_process_group` failed before the fix (pgid 425119 ≠ pid 425409) and passes after it (`3851352`).\n81\t\n82\t### Hive Mind policy left to the caller\n83\t\n84\tThe following stay in Hive Mind, passed through `extraArgs` / `extraEnv` or derived from the metadata:\n85\t\n86\t- pricing tiers and context windows (`service_tier`, `model_context_window`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT`);\n87\t- Codex `features.goals` and memory overrides;\n88\t- Formal AI pricing and attribution;\n89\t- OOM, disk and container recovery, and the Codex trace-file routing;\n90\t- retry and auto-resume decisions, and close-timeout values;\n91\t- loop reports and version probes;\n92\t- prompts, GitHub, Telegram and queues.\n93\t\n94\tCopying any of these into agent-commander would duplicate Hive Mind's policy state (see section (c) of the delta analysis).\n95\t\n96\t## Dependency updates\n97\t\n98\tAll packages were checked on 2026-10-21 against npm, crates.io, GitHub releases and the pre-commit hook repositories ([dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md)).\n99\t\n100\t- **npm** (`62a4a1a`): @changesets/cli 3, ESLint and @eslint/js 10, jscpd 5, lint-staged 17, prettier 3.9.10 and eslint-plugin-prettier 5.5.7. These exactly match Hive Mind v2.39.5's devDependencies.\n101\t  - jscpd 5 validates `format` strictly. The old `[\"console\"]` value had made jscpd 4 scan zero files, so duplicate detection now actually runs.\n102\t  - command-stream was already `^2.4.0`, the latest, and the version Hive Mind pins.\n103\t- **crates.io** (`fbf2222`): command-stream 0.13.1 → 1.9.0 (three source-breaking struct changes in `tui.rs`), tokio 1.54, serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.154, thiserror 2.0.21, tempfile 3.27 and tokio-test 0.4.6.\n104\t- **CI** (`4082d59`): checkout v7, setup-node v7, cache v6, and Node 24 in every workflow. The e2e workflows were still on Node 20, which the Node >= 22 engine requirement no longer allows. Also crates-io-auth-action v1.0.6 (SHA-pinned) and pre-commit-hooks v6.0.0.\n105\t\n106\t## command-stream adoption\n107\t\n108\t[command-stream-analysis.md](data/command-stream-analysis.md) reviews The exported `quoteForContext` gives the same output.\n134\t\n135\t## Timeline and experimental evidence\n136\t\n137\t1. **Dependencies first** (`62a4a1a`, `fbf2222`). The Rust command-stream upgrade broke three struct literals in `tui.rs`, which were fixed in the same commit. jscpd 5's validation exposed that duplicate detection had never run.\n138\t2. **Shared parsing, then the catalogue** (`872657e`, `4367abf`). Without parsing the agent's pretty-printed records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`), the agent default output ended as `incomplete_stream`.\n139\t3. **Classification port** (`d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b`). Each of C1–C6, X1, X2, X4 and A1–A3 started as a probe against `buildNormalizedResultMetadata`, then became a shared fixture. One example: a Codex failure whose tool output quoted a limit reported `limitReached: true` with a reset time full of JSON.\n140\t4. **Process lifetime** (`d83b799`, `b487dcc`, `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a`). A finite fixture forks a grandchild that holds stdout, then exits the wrapper. Before the fix `stop()` waited for the grandchild, and after it the group is terminated and draining is bounded.\n141\t5. **Sandbox finding.** In the test sandbox, PID 1 never reaps zombies, so a killed process group stays visible to `kill -0`. [experiments/process-group-reap.mjs](../../../experiments/process-group-reap.mjs) shows this. The group tests therefore check for live, non-zombie members with `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` instead of `kill -0`.\n142\t6. **Session files, env, aliases** (`c41770c`, `0219c31`, `97be2dc`, `2c1e397`, `36087a3`, `c7066de`). These use synthetic `CODEX_HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trees in temporary directories, so no credentials are read.\n143\t7. **command-stream features and quoting** (`decbeba`, `5e479d0`, `05d7264`), the **agent stderr error** (`6ec13f1`), and the **Rust detached process group** (`3851352`). The last one was found while writing #232.\n144\t8. **CI-only failures** (`d6b4591`, `55d2c74`). Two failures appeared only in the CI matrix:\n145\t   - Deno on all three OSes: `NotCapable: Requires sys access to \"homedir\"`. The session-file helpers called `os.homedir()` as a default parameter even when `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` was set. This also affected Deno consumers. The home directory is now read lazily, with a `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` fallback. The failure was reproduced locally with the CI's `deno test` flags (7 failed), and passes after the fix.\n146\t   - Rust on macOS: `File exists (os error 17)` in `gemini_controller_collects_formatted_json`. Prompt temp directories were named `agent-commander-{pid}-{nanos}`, and parallel tests on macOS's coarse clock got the same name. Names now carry a per-process sequence, and existing names are skipped. `prompt_dirs_are_unique_within_one_clock_tick` creates two directories with the same clock value, which failed under the old naming.\n147\t\n148\t### Known limits\n149\t\n150\t- **TUI env removal.** command-stream's Rust terminal capture cannot remove an inherited variable, so TUI launches with `unset_env` run through `env -u` (#229). The TUI tests check this argv.\n151\t- **No live provider inference.** No live inference was run against provider CLIs, because that needs paid credentials. Native shapes come from Hive Mind's fixtures and the vendors' documentation. The e2e workflows stay credential-gated as before.\n152\t- **Kilo gateway.** That the Kilo gateway still serves `nemotron-3-super-free` was checked only in the agent package source.\n153\t\n154\t## Primary-source research\n155\t\n156\t| Source                                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\n157\t| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n158\t| [Node.js `child_process`](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)                                                                         | \"On non-Windows platforms, if `options.detached` is set to true, the child process will be made the leader of a new process group and session.\" `unref()` lets the parent exit independently. This is the behavior the Rust `execute_detached` now matches.                                                                      |\n159\t| [Bash manual, Exit Status](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Exit-Status.html)                                              | \"When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.\" The `bash -c` wrapper turns signals into exit codes, which is why X3 maps 128+N back to a signal.                                                                                                                 |\n160\t| [Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)                                                                        | `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and the last line is a `result` message. SIGTERM gives exit 143. Background work is stopped after an idle wait that is configurable with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (C8–C10). `system/api_retry` carries `error: rate_limit` (C3). `parent_tool_use_id` marks subagent messages. |\n161\t| [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (redirect from developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive) | \"Event types include `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.*`, and `error`.\" Progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout (X2, X4). `codex exec resume --last` / `<SESSION_ID>` resumes a run (X6).                                                                           |\n162\t| npm registry, crates.io API, GitHub releases                                                                                                 | Every version in [dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md), and the command-stream release timeline in section 6 of the analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n163\t| `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.12–0.26.15 package source (read only)                                                                           | `src/cli/output.ts` sends only fatal errors to stderr; `src/provider/kilo.ts` defines `nemotron-3-super-free` (A4).                                                                                                                                                                                                              |\n164\t\n165\t## Existing components and libraries\n166\t\n167\t- **command-stream** gives terminal capture, frame and recording modes, and quoting, all adopted. Its process runners were evaluated in full, and the blockers were filed (see above).\n168\t- **Node `child_process` and Tokio `process`** stay the executor base. Process-group termination uses `process.kill(-pid)` in JS and a `kill -TERM -- -pid` shell-out in Rust, because the crate forbids `unsafe`, so `libc::kill` is not an option.\n169\t- **Hive Mind's own libraries** (`claude.usage-limit-sources.lib.mjs`, `codex-rollout-usage-limit.lib.mjs`, `agent-error-events.lib.mjs` and the others) were ported for their general logic rather than imported. Importing them would make the dependency depend on its consumer.\n170\t- **The `@link-assistant/agent` CLI** already defines the Kilo model, so no overlay was added.\n171\t\n172\t## Consumer migration\n173\t\n174\tEvery new field and option is additive. Hive Mind's existing `agent({...})`, `start({ attached, onOutput })` and `metadata.success` / `limitReached` / `limitResetTime` handling work unchanged. To benefit fully, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` should:\n175\t\n176\t1. copy the new metadata fields (`signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `limitSource`, `apiError*`, `observedModels` and the background-task fields) in `summarizeAgentCommanderResult`;\n177\t2. pass `null` env values through instead of dropping them;\n178\t3. replace its own `isRecoverableAgentToolError` fallback with the metadata verdict;\n179\t4. call `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` with its own timeout values.\n180\t\n181\thive-mind [#3690](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3690) tracks this. Future syncs should start from Hive Mind `5a7cb68b7` and repeat the same diff-and-classify method.\n182\t\n183\t## Validation\n184\t\n185\t```bash\n186\tcd js && npm run check && npm test\n187\tcd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\n188\t```\n189\t\n190\tLocal results on 2026-10-21: `npm run check` clean and `npm test` 362 of 362 passing (Bun 362 of 362, and Deno 355 passing with 7 skipped); `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo doc` clean, and `cargo test` 358 of 358 passing. CI on the PR head is recorded in PR #56.\n191\t"

`FREE_MODELS`, so injecting an overlay would only mask the CLI's own definition.                                 | analysis only        |\n| M1  | Only `opus` was a rolling alias. `sonnet` and `haiku` were pinned, and `--fallback-model` was always mapped.                                      | `opus`, `sonnet` and `haiku` pass through for Claude execution and fallback, matching                                                                                                   | Aliases are matched case-insensitively and trimmed.                                                                                                                                                          | `c7066de`            |\n\nThe sync also found more general fixes:\n\n- **Model catalogue** synced to v2.39.5: Claude 5.5 family, Codex `sol`/`luna`/`astra`, the Kilo default for Agent, OpenCode `big-pickle`, the Qwen catalogue (`4367abf`, `0f729b9`). The withdrawn `openai/formal-ai` aliases were removed in Rust as well (`24e0014`).\n- **JSON records.** Agent's default output is pretty-printed or concatenated JSON rather than NDJSON. Both parsers now read multi-line and back-to-back records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`). A shared JSON-lines parser and model mapper replaced the per-tool copies first (`872657e`).\n- **Agent fatal errors on stderr.** The agent 0.26.15 source (`src/cli/output.ts`) prints only fatal errors, such as an unknown model, to stderr, so the metadata said only \"Process exited with code 1\". A failed exit with no error event on stdout now uses the last JSON error record of the output (`6ec13f1`, reproduced by [experiments/agent-stderr-error.mjs](../../../experiments/agent-stderr-error.mjs)).\n- **Rust generic-tool quoting.** `build_tool_command` used a single-quote escape inside double quotes, so bash expanded `$`, backticks and `\"`. It now uses `escape_arg` like JS (`05d7264`).\n- **Rust detached process group.** `execute_detached` left the child in the caller's process group, so Ctrl+C to the caller also stopped the agent. Node's `detached: true` makes the child \"the leader of a new process group and session\". The Rust helper now sets `process_group(0)`. `test_execute_detached_leads_its_own_process_group` failed before the fix (pgid 425119 ≠ pid 425409) and passes after it (`3851352`).\n\n### Hive Mind policy left to the caller\n\nThe following stay in Hive Mind, passed through `extraArgs` / `extraEnv` or derived from the metadata:\n\n- pricing tiers and context windows (`service_tier`, `model_context_window`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT`);\n- Codex `features.goals` and memory overrides;\n- Formal AI pricing and attribution;\n- OOM, disk and container recovery, and the Codex trace-file routing;\n- retry and auto-resume decisions, and close-timeout values;\n- loop reports and version probes;\n- prompts, GitHub, Telegram and queues.\n\nCopying any of these into agent-commander would duplicate Hive Mind's policy state (see section (c) of the delta analysis).\n\n## Dependency updates\n\nAll packages were checked on 2026-10-21 against npm, crates.io, GitHub releases and the pre-commit hook repositories ([dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md)).\n\n- **npm** (`62a4a1a`): @changesets/cli 3, ESLint and @eslint/js 10, jscpd 5, lint-staged 17, prettier 3.9.10 and eslint-plugin-prettier 5.5.7. The Rust command-stream upgrade broke three struct literals in `tui.rs`, which were fixed in the same commit. jscpd 5's validation exposed that duplicate detection had never run.\n2. **Shared parsing, then the catalogue** (`872657e`, `4367abf`). Without parsing the agent's pretty-printed records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`), the agent default output ended as `incomplete_stream`.\n3. **Classification port** (`d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b`). Each of C1–C6, X1, X2, X4 and A1–A3 started as a probe against `buildNormalizedResultMetadata`, then became a shared fixture. One example: a Codex failure whose tool output quoted a limit reported `limitReached: true` with a reset time full of JSON.\n4. **Process lifetime** (`d83b799`, `b487dcc`, `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a`). A finite fixture forks a grandchild that holds stdout, then exits the wrapper. Before the fix `stop()` waited for the grandchild, and after it the group is terminated and draining is bounded.\n5. **Sandbox finding.** In the test sandbox, PID 1 never reaps zombies, so a killed process group stays visible to `kill -0`. [experiments/process-group-reap.mjs](../../../experiments/process-group-reap.mjs) shows this. The group tests therefore check for live, non-zombie members with `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` instead of `kill -0`.\n6. **Session files, env, aliases** (`c41770c`, `0219c31`, `97be2dc`, `2c1e397`, `36087a3`, `c7066de`). These use synthetic `CODEX_HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trees in temporary directories, so no credentials are read.\n7. **command-stream features and quoting** (`decbeba`, `5e479d0`, `05d7264`), the **agent stderr error** (`6ec13f1`), and the **Rust detached process group** (`3851352`). The last one was found while writing #232.\n8. **CI-only failures** (`d6b4591`, `55d2c74`). Two failures appeared only in the CI matrix:\n   - Deno on all three OSes: `NotCapable: Requires sys access to \"homedir\"`. The session-file helpers called `os.homedir()` as a default parameter even when `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` was set. This also affected Deno consumers. The home directory is now read lazily, with a `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` fallback. The failure was reproduced locally with the CI's `deno test` flags (7 failed), and passes after the fix.\n   - Rust on macOS: `File exists (os error 17)` in `gemini_controller_collects_formatted_json`. Prompt temp directories were named `agent-commander-{pid}-{nanos}`, and parallel tests on macOS's coarse clock got the same name. Names now carry a per-process sequence, and existing names are skipped. `prompt_dirs_are_unique_within_one_clock_tick` creates two directories with the same clock value, which failed under the old naming.\n\n### Known limits\n\n- **TUI env removal.** command-stream's Rust terminal capture cannot remove an inherited variable, so TUI launches with `unset_env` run through `env -u` (#229). The TUI tests check this argv.\n- **No live provider inference.** No live inference was run against provider CLIs, because that needs paid credentials. Native shapes come from Hive Mind's fixtures and the vendors' documentation. The e2e workflows stay credential-gated as before.\n- **Kilo gateway.** That the Kilo gateway still serves `nemotron-3-super-free` was checked only in the agent package source.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| Source                                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [Node.js `child_process`](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)                                                                         | \"On non-Windows platforms, if `options.detached` is set to true, the child process will be made the leader of a new process group and session.\" `unref()` lets the parent exit independently. This is the behavior the Rust `execute_detached` now matches.                                                                      |\n| [Bash manual, Exit Status](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Exit-Status.html)                                              | \"When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.\" The `bash -c` wrapper turns signals into exit codes, which is why X3 maps 128+N back to a signal.                                                                                                                 |\n| [Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)                                                                        | `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and the last line is a `result` message. SIGTERM gives exit 143. Background work is stopped after an idle wait that is configurable with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (C8–C10). `system/api_retry` carries `error: rate_limit` (C3). `parent_tool_use_id` marks subagent messages. |\n| [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (redirect from developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive) | \"Event types include `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.*`, and `error`.\" Progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout (X2, X4). `codex exec resume --last` / `<SESSION_ID>` resumes a run (X6).                                                                           |\n| npm registry, crates.io API, GitHub releases                                                                                                 | Every version in [dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md), and the command-stream release timeline in section 6 of the analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n| `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.12–0.26.15 package source (read only)                                                                           | `src/cli/output.ts` sends only fatal errors to stderr; `src/provider/kilo.ts` defines `nemotron-3-super-free` (A4).                                                                                                                                                                                                              |\n\n## Existing components and libraries\n\n- **command-stream** gives terminal capture, frame and recording modes, and quoting, all adopted. Its process runners were evaluated in full, and the blockers were filed (see above).\n- **Node `child_process` and Tokio `process`** stay the executor base. Process-group termination uses `process.kill(-pid)` in JS and a `kill -TERM -- -pid` shell-out in Rust, because the crate forbids `unsafe`, so `libc::kill` is not an option.\n- **Hive Mind's own libraries** (`claude.usage-limit-sources.lib.mjs`, `codex-rollout-usage-limit.lib.mjs`, `agent-error-events.lib.mjs` and the others) were ported for their general logic rather than imported. Importing them would make the dependency depend on its consumer.\n- **The `@link-assistant/agent` CLI** already defines the Kilo model, so no overlay was added.\n\n## Consumer migration\n\nEvery new field and option is additive. Hive Mind's existing `agent({...})`, `start({ attached, onOutput })` and `metadata.success` / `limitReached` / `limitResetTime` handling work unchanged. To benefit fully, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` should:\n\n1. copy the new metadata fields (`signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `limitSource`, `apiError*`, `observedModels` and the background-task fields) in `summarizeAgentCommanderResult`;\n2. pass `null` env values through instead of dropping them;\n3. replace its own `isRecoverableAgentToolError` fallback with the metadata verdict;\n4. call `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` with its own timeout values.\n\nhive-mind [#3690](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3690) tracks this. Future syncs should start from Hive Mind `5a7cb68b7` and repeat the same diff-and-classify method.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run check && npm test\ncd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\n```\n\nLocal results on 2026-10-21: `npm run check` clean and `npm test` 362 of 362 passing (Bun 362 of 362, and Deno 355 passing with 7 skipped); `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo doc` clean, and `cargo test` 358 of 358 passing. Task agents and scheduling\\n\\n**Scheduler.** `scheduling/Scheduler.ts`\\n- One `Effect.sleep(\\\"5 seconds\\\")` loop that runs forever.\\n- Each source has its own `Semaphore.make(1)` with `withPermitsIfAvailable(1)`, so a source never overlaps itself.\\n\\n**Task agents.** `packages/tasks-contracts/src/v1/agents.ts`\\n- Triggers: `startStatuses`, `startTags`, `startRunStatuses (failed|interrupted|blocked)`.\\n- Config: `{role, modelSelection, runtimeMode, interactionMode, tools, skills, instructions}`.\\n\\n**Agent service.** `packages/tasks-server/src/agents/TaskAgentService.ts`\\n- At most one active run per task and agent.\\n- `thread.create` with `sidebarHidden: true`, then `sendToThread` (L1006-1046).\\n- L167-168: `PENDING_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 2*60*1000`.\\n\\n**Retries and result parsing.**\\n- `retryOperational.ts`: capped exponential backoff from 100 ms to 5 s.\\n- `TaskAgentResultParser.ts`: parses a fenced `task_agent_result` or json block containing `{status, summary, blocker, events[]}`.\\n\\n**Scheduled tasks.**\\n- `scheduledTasks/Schedule.ts`: interval, fixed_time (HH:MM plus weekdays) or webhook. `MISSED_FIXED_TIME_GRACE_MS = 10 min`.\\n- `ScheduledTaskService.ts`:\\n  - Uses an idempotent `commandId` of the form `scheduled-task:${id}:${ms}:${trigger}` and runs with `concurrency: 1`.\\n  - Recovers rows stuck in `running` at startup.\\n  - Delivers with `sendToThread` `mode: \\\"queue\\\"`.\\n  - Supports webhook verification and templates.\\n\\n**MCP tools exposing scheduling** (`mcp/toolkits/orchestrator/tools.ts` L117-160): `schedule_task`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `update_scheduled_task`, `delete_scheduled_task`.\\n\\n## 5. Checkpointing\\n\\n- **Ref format** (`checkpointing/Utils.ts`): `refs/t3/checkpoints/${Base64Url(threadId)}/turn/${turnCount}`.\\n- **Durable writes** (`vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts` L786-791): `-c core.fsync=objects,reference -c core.fsyncMethod=fsync`, because \\\"an unclean restart can leave 0-byte files under refs/t3/**\\\".\\n- **Capture:** a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` `t3-checkpoint-index-${uuid}` (L804), then `write-tree`, then `commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD -m \\\"t3 checkpoint ref=...\\\"` (L1025-1037), then `update-ref` (L1054).\\n- **Restore:** `restore --source <oid> --worktree --staged -- .`, then `clean -fd -- .`, then `reset --quiet -- .`.\\n- **Diff:** `diff --patch|--numstat -z --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv [--ignore-all-space]`.\\n- **Callers:** `orchestration-v2/CheckpointService.ts` L287 and L398 (capture), L523 (restore), L551 (delete).\\n\\n## 6. Event logging and observability\\n\\n**Per-thread NDJSON provider log.** `provider/EventNdjsonLogger.ts`\\n- Three streams: `native`, `canonical`, `orchestration`, labelled `NTIVE`/`CANON`/`ORCH` (around L179-181). Files are `${prefix}${threadSegment}.log`, and `_global` is used when there is no thread.\\n- Limits (L29-39):\\n  - Rotation and retention: `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 10 MiB`, `MAX_FILES = 10`, `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 MiB`, `MAX_AGE_MS = 14 days`.\\n  - Buffering: batch window 1 s, buffer 1 MiB or 512 records.\\n  - Per record: `MAX_RECORD_CHARACTERS = 64 KiB`, 1024 fields, depth 16.\\n- Token-delta noise is dropped (L45-64): `content.delta`, `item/agentMessage/delta`, `agent_message_chunk` and similar. 4] = [\n        (\n            launch.reasoning_effort.is_some(),\n            |c| c.reasoning_effort,\n            \"reasoning effort (--reasoning-effort)\",\n        ),\n        (\n            launch.mcp_config.is_some(),\n            |c| c.mcp_config,\n            \"MCP server configuration (--mcp-config)\",\n        ),\n        (\n            launch.strict_mcp_config,\n            |c| c.strict_mcp_config,\n            \"strict MCP configuration (--strict-mcp-config)\",\n        ),\n        (\n            !launch.additional_directories.is_empty(),\n            |c| c.additional_directories,\n            \"additional directories (--add-dir)\",\n        ),\n    ];\n    let capabilities = launch_capabilities(tool);\n    for (requested, pick, label) in checks {\n        if requested && !pick(&capabilities) {\n            let supporting: Vec<&str> = TOOLS\n                .iter()\n                .copied()\n                .filter(|name| pick(&launch_capabilities(name)))\n                .collect();\n            return Err(format!(\n                \"Tool \\\"{}\\\" does not support {}. Choose one of: {}; or omit the option.\",\n                tool,\n                label,\n                supporting.join(\", \")\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Validate a reasoning effort / variant name.\n///\n/// # Panics\n/// Panics when the level contains characters other than `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.\npub fn normalize_reasoning_effort(reasoning_effort: &str) -> String {\n    assert!(\n        !reasoning_effort.is_empty()\n            && reasoning_effort\n                .chars()\n                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '-'),\n        \"Invalid reasoning effort \\\"{}\\\". Use a level name such as low, medium or high.\",\n        reasoning_effort\n    );\n    reasoning_effort.to_string()\n}\n\n/// Push `flag value` for each extra directory.\npub fn push_directories(args: &mut Vec<String>, flag: &str, directories: &[String]) {\n    for dir in directories {\n        assert!(!dir.is_empty(), \"additional directories must not be empty\");\n        args.push(flag.to_string());\n        args.push(dir.clone());\n    }\n}\n\n/// Encode a TOML key segment (bare when possible, quoted otherwise).\nfn toml_key(key: &str) -> String {\n    if !key.is_empty()\n        && key\n            .chars()\n            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '-')\n    {\n        key.to_string()\n    } else {\n        Value::String(key.to_string()).to_string()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Encode a JSON value as an inline TOML value. JSON string escapes are a\n/// subset of TOML basic-string escapes, so strings reuse JSON encoding.\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error for `null` at the top level.\npub fn to_toml_value(value: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {\n    match value {\n        Value::String(_) | Value::Number(_) | Value::Bool(_) => Ok(value.to_string()),\n        Value::Array(items) => {\n            let parts: Result<Vec<String>, String> = items.iter().map(to_toml_value).collect();\n            Ok(format!(\"[{}]\", parts?.join(\", \")))\n        }\n        Value::Object(map) => {\n            let mut parts = Vec::new();\n            for (key, item) in map.iter().filter(|(_, item)| !item.is_null()) {\n                parts.push(format!(\"{} = {}\", toml_key(key), to_toml_value(item)?));\n            }\n            Ok(format!(\"{{{}}}\", parts.join(\", \")))\n        }\n        Value::Null => Err(\"Cannot encode null as a TOML value\".to_string()),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Translate a Claude-style `{\"mcpServers\": {...}}` JSON document into one\n/// Codex `-c mcp_servers={...}` override. `headers` becomes `http_headers`\n/// and the transport `type` is dropped (Codex infers it from `command` or\n/// `url`). Codex merges the table into the servers from `config.toml`.\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error for a file path, invalid JSON or a missing `mcpServers`.\npub fn codex_mcp_servers_override(mcp_config: &str) -> Result<String, String> {\n    if !mcp_config.trim_start().starts_with('{') {\n        return Err(\"Tool \\\"codex\\\" takes MCP servers as config overrides, not a file path. Pass mcpConfig as inline JSON.\".to_string());\n    }\n    let config: Value =\n        serde_json::from_str(mcp_config).map_err(|error| format!(\"Invalid mcpConfig JSON: {error}\"))?;\n    let servers = config\n        .get(\"mcpServers\")\n        .and_then(Value::as_object)\n        .ok_or_else(|| \"mcpConfig must contain an mcpServers object\".to_string())?;\n    let mut table = serde_json::Map::new();\n    for (name, server) in servers {\n        let mut server = server\n            .as_object()\n            .cloned()\n            .ok_or_else(|| format!(\"MCP server \\\"{name}\\\" must be an object\"))?;\n        server.remove(\"type\");\n        if let Some(headers) = server.remove(\"headers\") {\n            server.insert(\"http_headers\".to_string(), headers);\n        }\n        table.insert(name.clone(), Value::Object(server));\n    }\n    Ok(format!(\"mcp_servers={}\", to_toml_value(&Value::Object(table))?))\n}\n"

Options\n * @param {string} options.tool - Tool name\n * @param {string} [options.executable] - Executable path/name override\n * @returns {string} Shell command (stderr is merged into stdout)\n */\nexport function buildVersionCommand({ tool, executable }) {\n  const binary = executable || getTool({ toolName: tool }).executable;\n  return `${escapeArg(binary)} --version 2>&1`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Extract the first semantic version from `--version` output, such as\n * `2.1.308 (Claude Code)` or `codex-cli 0.163.0`.\n * @param {string} output - Command output\n * @returns {string|null} Version without a leading `v`\n */\nexport function parseToolVersion(output) {\n  return VERSION_PATTERN.exec(String(output || ''))?.[1] || null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Split a version into numeric parts and an optional prerelease tag.\n * @param {string} version - Version\n * @returns {{parts: number[], prerelease: string|null}} Parsed version\n */\nfunction splitVersion(version) {\n  const match = /^v?(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)(?:-([0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?/.exec(\n    String(version).trim()\n  );\n  if (!match) {\n    throw new Error(`Invalid version \"${version}\"`);\n  }\n  return { parts: match[1].split('.').map(Number), prerelease: match[2] || null };\n}\n\n/**\n * Compare two versions numerically; a prerelease sorts before its release.\n * Missing parts count as zero, so `1.2` equals `1.2.0`.\n * @param {string} a - First version\n * @param {string} b - Second version\n * @returns {number} -1, 0 or 1\n */\nexport function compareVersions(a, b) {\n  const left = splitVersion(a);\n  const right = splitVersion(b);\n  const length = Math.max(left.parts.length, right.parts.length);\n  for (let index = 0; index < length; index++) {\n    const diff = (left.parts[index] || 0) - Options\n * @param {string} options.tool - Tool name\n * @param {number} options.exitCode - Probe exit code\n * @param {string} [options.output] - Probe output\n * @param {string} [options.minimumVersion] - Lowest accepted version\n * @returns {{tool: string, installed: boolean, version: string|null, raw: string, meetsMinimum: boolean|null}}\n */\nexport function toolVersionFromOutput({\n  tool,\n  exitCode,\n  output = '',\n  minimumVersion,\n}) {\n  const raw = String(output).trim();\n  const installed = !NOT_FOUND_EXIT_CODES.has(exitCode);\n  const version = exitCode === 0 ? parseToolVersion(raw) : null;\n  const meetsMinimum =\n    minimumVersion === undefined || minimumVersion === null\n      ? null\n      : version !== null && compareVersions(version, minimumVersion) >= 0;\n  return { tool, installed, version, raw, meetsMinimum };\n}\n\n/**\n * Run `<tool> --version` and report the installed version.\n * @param {Object} options - Errors\n/// Returns an error for an unknown tool.\npub fn build_version_command(tool: &str, executable: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, String> {\n    let binary = match executable {\n        Some(path) if !path.is_empty() => path.to_string(),\n        _ => get_tool(tool)?.executable().to_string(),\n    };\n    Ok(format!(\"{} --version 2>&1\", escape_arg(&binary)))\n}\n\n/// Extract the first semantic version from `--version` output, such as\n/// `2.1.308 (Claude Code)` or `codex-cli 0.163.0`.\npub fn parse_tool_version(output: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    version_pattern()\n        .captures(output)\n        .map(|captures| captures[1].to_string())\n}\n\nfn split_version(version: &str) -> Result<(Vec<u64>, Option<String>), String> {\n    let trimmed = version.trim();\n    let trimmed = trimmed.strip_prefix('v').unwrap_or(trimmed);\n    let (numbers, prerelease) = match trimmed.split_once('-') {\n        Some((numbers, tag)) => (numbers, Some(tag.to_string())),\n        None => (trimmed, None),\n    };\n    let parts: Result<Vec<u64>, _> = numbers.split('.').map(str::parse::<u64>).collect();\n    parts\n        .map(|parts| (parts, prerelease))\n        .map_err(|_| format!(\"Invalid version \\\"{version}\\\"\"))\n}\n\n/// Compare two versions numerically; a prerelease sorts before its release.\n/// Missing parts count as zero, so `1.2` equals `1.2.0`.\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error when either side is not a dotted numeric version.\npub fn compare_versions(a: &str, b: &str) -> Result<Ordering, String> {\n    let (left, left_pre) = split_version(a)?;\n    let (right, right_pre) = split_version(b)?;\n    for index in 0..left.len().max(right.len()) {\n        let order = left\n            .get(index)\n            .unwrap_or(&0)\n            .cmp(right.get(index).unwrap_or(&0));\n        if order != Ordering::Equal {\n            return Ok(order);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(match (left_pre, right_pre) {\n        (None, None) => Ordering::Equal,\n        (Some(_), None) => Ordering::Less,\n        (None, Some(_)) => Ordering::Greater,\n        (Some(l), Some(r)) => l.cmp(&r),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Interpret a finished `--version` probe.\npub fn tool_version_from_output(\n    tool: &str,\n    exit_code: i32,\n    output: &str,\n    minimum_version: Option<&str>,\n) -> ToolVersion {\n    let raw = output.trim().to_string();\n    let version = if exit_code == 0 {\n        parse_tool_version(&raw)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    let meets_minimum = minimum_version.map(|minimum| {\n        version\n            .as_deref()\n            .and_then(|found| compare_versions(found, minimum).ok())\n            .is_some_and(|order| order != Ordering::Less)\n    });\n    ToolVersion {\n        tool: tool.to_string(),\n        installed: exit_code != 126 && exit_code != 127,\n        version,\n        raw,\n        meets_minimum,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run `<tool> --version` and report the installed version.\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error for an unknown tool.\npub fn build_version_command(tool: &str, executable: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, String> {\n    let binary = match executable {\n        Some(path) if !path.is_empty() => path.to_string(),\n        _ => get_tool(tool)?.executable().to_string(),\n    };\n    Ok(format!(\"{} --version 2>&1\", escape_arg(&binary)))\n}\n\n/// Extract the first semantic version from `--version` output, such as\n/// `2.1.308 (Claude Code)` or `codex-cli 0.163.0`.\npub fn parse_tool_version(output: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    version_pattern()\n        .captures(output)\n        .map(|captures| captures[1].to_string())\n}\n\nfn split_version(version: &str) -> Result<(Vec<u64>, Option<String>), String> {\n    let trimmed = version.trim();\n    let trimmed = trimmed.strip_prefix('v').unwrap_or(trimmed);\n    let (numbers, prerelease) = match trimmed.split_once('-') {\n        Some((numbers, tag)) => (numbers, Some(tag.to_string())),\n        None => (trimmed, None),\n    };\n    let parts: Result<Vec<u64>, _> = numbers.split('.').map(str::parse::<u64>).collect();\n    parts\n        .map(|parts| (parts, prerelease))\n        .map_err(|_| format!(\"Invalid version \\\"{version}\\\"\"))\n}\n\n/// Compare two versions numerically; a prerelease sorts before its release.\n/// Missing parts count as zero, so `1.2` equals `1.2.0`.\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error when either side is not a dotted numeric version.\npub fn compare_versions(a: &str, b: &str) -> Result<Ordering, String> {\n    let (left, left_pre) = split_version(a)?;\n    let (right, right_pre) = split_version(b)?;\n    for index in 0..left.len().max(right.len()) {\n        let order = left\n            .get(index)\n            .unwrap_or(&0)\n            .cmp(right.get(index).unwrap_or(&0));\n        if order != Ordering::Equal {\n            return Ok(order);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(match (left_pre, right_pre) {\n        (None, None) => Ordering::Equal,\n        (Some(_), None) => Ordering::Less,\n        (None, Some(_)) => Ordering::Greater,\n        (Some(l), Some(r)) => l.cmp(&r),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Interpret a finished `--version` probe.\npub fn tool_version_from_output(\n    tool: &str,\n    exit_code: i32,\n    output: &str,\n    minimum_version: Option<&str>,\n) -> ToolVersion {\n    let raw = output.trim().to_string();\n    let version = if exit_code == 0 {\n        parse_tool_version(&raw)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    let meets_minimum = minimum_version.map(|minimum| {\n        version\n            .as_deref()\n            .and_then(|found| compare_versions(found, minimum).ok())\n            .is_some_and(|order| order != Ordering::Less)\n    });\n    ToolVersion {\n        tool: tool.to_string(),\n        installed: exit_code != 126 && exit_code != 127,\n        version,\n        raw,\n        meets_minimum,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run `<tool> --version` and report the installed version.\n///\n/// # Errors\n/// Returns an error for an unknown tool or when `bash` cannot be spawned.\npub async fn get_tool_version(\n    tool: &str,\n    executable: Option<&str>,\n    minimum_version: Option<&str>,\n) -> io::Result<ToolVersion> {\n    let command = build_version_command(tool, executable)\n        .map_err(|error| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, error))?;\n    let result = execute_command(&command, false, false).await?;\n    Ok(tool_version_from_output(\n        tool,\n        result.exit_code,\n        &result.stdout,\n        minimum_version,\n    ))\n}\n"

window.resetsAt,\n        mins,\n      })\n    );\n  }\n  return windows;\n}\n\n/**\n * Merge a partial update into known windows by `id`; windows the update\n * omits are kept (Claude names one window per event).\n * @param {Object[]} windows - Known windows\n * @param {Object[]} update - New windows\n * @returns {Object[]} Merged windows, sorted by kind then id\n */\nexport function mergeUsageWindows(windows = [], update = []) {\n  const byId = new Map(windows.map((window) => [window.id, window]));\n  for (const window of update) {\n    const previous = byId.get(window.id);\n    byId.set(window.id, {\n      ...window,\n      resetsAt: window.resetsAt ?? previous?.resetsAt ?? null,\n    });\n  }\n  return [...byId.values()].sort(\n    (a, b) =>\n      USAGE_WINDOW_KINDS.indexOf(a.kind) - USAGE_WINDOW_KINDS.indexOf(b.kind) ||\n      (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ?  \"session\"\n    }\n}\n\nfn either<'a>(value: &'a Value, snake: &str, camel: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {\n    value\n        .get(snake)\n        .filter(|item| !item.is_null())\n        .or_else(|| Per-tool mapping:\n     - **claude:** `--add-dir` (repeated), `--mcp-config <value>`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--effort <level>` (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). These are emitted before `--model` so the variadic flags are terminated by the next option.\n     - **codex:**\n       - `exec --sandbox ... --add-dir <dir> [resume ID] -c model_reasoning_effort=<lvl> -c mcp_servers={...TOML inline table...} --json --skip-git-repo-check ...`.\n       - `headers` is mapped to `http_headers` and `type` is dropped.\n       - `strictMcpConfig` is unsupported, because overrides merge with the user's servers.\n       - Documented efforts: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh.\n     - **opencode:** `--variant <level>` (provider-specific; `reasoningEfforts: null`). No MCP, strict, or add-dir support.\n     - **gemini:** `--include-directories <dir>` only.\n     - **qwen:** `--include-directories` (merged with its existing `includeDirectories` option) and `--mcp-config`. No effort or strict support.\n     - **agent:** none of these are supported.\n   - Planned remaining features:\n     - E: live input `sendMessage`/`endInput` for stream-input tools (claude, agent).\n     - F: tool version probe (`buildVersionCommand`, `parseToolVersion`, `compareVersions`, `getToolVersion`/`checkToolVersion({minimumVersion})`).\n     - G: normalized `usageWindows` metadata `{id, kind: session|weekly|monthly|other, label, usedPercent, resetsAt, windowDurationMins}`.\n       - From Claude `rate_limit_event`: utilization×100; five_hour→session (300 min); seven_day→weekly (10080 min).\n       - From Codex rate_limits primary/secondary: plan free/go means monthly; ignore limitId other than codex.\n     - H (maybe): contextUsage/contextWindow.\n     - D (optional): image attachments \n\n=========\n\nThis session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The metadata object gives callers a stable summary without tool-specific output parsing:\n\n- `success`, `exitCode`, `signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `errorDuringExecution`, `errorType`, and `errorMessage`. `errorType` includes `rate_limited` (a transient server throttle: retry it), `incomplete_stream` (the process exited before the native completion event) and `background_tasks_stopped`. A process that `stop()` ends after its completed result is not a failure.\n- `sessionId`\n- `limitReached`, `limitResetTime`, `limitTimezone`, `limitResetsAt` (epoch seconds, from structured sources) and `limitWindow` (`5-hour`, `weekly`, ...)\n- `limitSource`: set when the limit was found outside the output, as `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (see below)\n- `apiError`, `apiErrorStatus`, `terminalReason`, and `requestId` (Claude API failure details)\n- `resultSummary`\n- `anthropicTotalCostUSD`, `publicPricingEstimate`, and `pricingInfo`\n- `resultModelUsage`, `streamTokenUsage`, `subAgentCalls`, `observedModels`, and `observedModel` (the models that actually answered)\n- `runningBackgroundTasks`, `backgroundTasksStopped`, `stoppedBackgroundTasks`, and `printWaitCeilingSeconds`\n\n#### Usage limits that only the session files report\n\n`codex exec --json` and `claude -p` do not always print a usage limit when they fail on one. For a failed run that ended on its own, without a signal and without a limit in its output, `stop()` checks the session file the CLI wrote:\n\n- **Codex**: the last turn of `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*-<thread id>.jsonl`. It uses a `token_count` `rate_limits` window at 100% with a `resets_at`, or an `error` event with `usage_limit_exceeded`.\n- **Claude**: `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects/<working-directory slug>/<session id>.jsonl`, when its last conversation entry is an `isApiErrorMessage` usage-limit message.\n\nA `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` passed in `toolOptions.extraEnv` is honoured. Only the last turn or entry is read, so a limit the session recovered from is not reported. The same checks are exported for callers that run the CLIs themselves: `applyCodexRolloutUsageLimit`, `detectCodexRolloutUsageLimit`, `canResumeCodexSession` (a missing rollout means `codex exec resume` cannot work, so start a new session), `applyClaudeTranscriptUsageLimit` and `readClaudeTranscriptApiError`. Hive Mind's text classifiers are exported too: `detectUsageLimitSources`, `isUsageLimitText`, `extractResetTime` and `isRecoverableToolError`.\n\n### Using Different Tools\n\n## API Reference\n\n### `agent(options)`\n\nCreates an agent controller.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `options.tool` (string, required) - CLI tool to use ('claude', 'codex', 'opencode', 'qwen', 'gemini', 'agent')\n- `options.workingDirectory` (string, required) - Working directory\n- `options.prompt` (string, optional) - Prompt for the agent\n- `options.systemPrompt` (string, optional) - System prompt\n- `options.promptFile` (string, optional) - File containing prompt input for stdin-based tools\n- `options.model` (string, optional) - Model alias or full ID\n- `options.json` (boolean, optional) - Enable JSON output mode\n- `options.resume` (string, optional) - Resume session ID (tool-specific)\n- `options.readOnly` (boolean, optional) - Enforce native read-only/planning mode\n- `options.planOnly` (boolean, optional) - Enforce native planning mode; the `agent` tool maps it to `--permission-mode plan` while other tools treat it like `readOnly`\n- `options.isolation` (string, optional) - 'none', 'screen', or 'docker' (default: 'none')\n- `options.screenName` (string, optional) - Screen session name (required for screen isolation)\n- `options.containerName` (string, optional) - Container name (required for docker isolation)\n- `options.toolOptions` (object, optional) - Additional tool-specific options\n  - `executable` (string, optional) - Override the native executable path/name for any supported tool\n  - `extraEnv` (object or `KEY=VALUE` / `[key, value]` array, optional) - Environment variables applied to the native tool process. A `null` value unsets an inherited variable (`env -u`), for example `{ ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: null }`.\n  - `extraArgs` (string array, optional) - Raw native tool arguments appended after typed agent-commander arguments\n  - `skipDefaultSafetyFlags` (boolean, optional) - Do not add default autonomous safety bypass flags such as Claude/Codex bypass flags or Qwen/Gemini `--yolo`\n  - `permissionMode` (string, optional) - Explicit permission mode for Claude or `agent` (agent: `auto` | `plan` | `readonly` | `ask`)\n  - `permission` (string, optional) - OpenCode-compatible `--permission` JSON policy for the `agent` tool\n  - `sandboxMode` (string, optional) - Explicit Codex sandbox mode\n  - `approvalMode` (string, optional) - Explicit Codex approval mode\n\n**Returns:** Agent controller object with `start()`, `stop()`, `cancel()`, `getSessionId()`, `getMessages()`, and `getToolConfig()` methods\n\n### `controller.start(startOptions)`\n\nStarts the agent (non-blocking - returns immediately after starting the process).\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `startOptions.dryRun` (boolean, optional) - Preview command without executing\n- `startOptions.detached` (boolean, optional) - Run in detached mode\n- `startOptions.attached` (boolean, optional) - Stream output (default: true)\n- `startOptions.onMessage` (function, optional) - Callback for JSON messages\n- `startOptions.onOutput` (function, optional) - Callback for raw output chunks\n\n**Returns:** Promise resolving to `void` (or prints command in dry-run mode)\n\n### `controller.stop(stopOptions)`\n\nStops the agent and collects output.\n\nFor `isolation: 'none'`: Waits for process to exit and collects all output.\nFor `isolation: 'screen'` or `'docker'`: Sends stop command to the isolated environment.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `stopOptions.dryRun` (boolean, optional) - Preview command without executing\n- `stopOptions.closeTimeoutMs` (number, optional) - Stop a process that stays alive this long after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang). The whole process group is stopped.\n- `stopOptions.backgroundWaitMs` (number, optional) - Extra time allowed while the result reports background tasks that are still running\n\n**Returns:** Promise resolving to:\n\n```javascript\n{\n  exitCode: number,\n  output: {\n    plain: string,      // Raw text output (stdout + stderr)\n    parsed: Array|null  // JSON-parsed messages (if tool supports it)\n  },\n  sessionId: string|null,  // Session ID for resuming\n  usage: Object|null,      // Token usage statistics\n  metadata: Object         // Normalized result metadata (see above)\n}\n```\n\n### `createJsonInputStream(options)`",

Empty or unfinished streams return `incomplete_stream`; Agent's default NDJSON mode uses the same check. Protocol parsing and usage use stdout, while `plain_output` retains stderr diagnostics. Parent session metadata excludes Claude subagent-scoped results.\n\n`stop()` waits for a direct process to finish. `AgentStopOptions { close_timeout, background_wait, .. }` ends a process that stays alive after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang, hive-mind#1280), allowing `background_wait` more while the result reports running background tasks. Such a run keeps `success` with `terminated_after_result`. `controller.cancel().await?` interrupts it and collects the final result. Unix cancellation signals the process group; Windows cancellation signals the immediate child. A native CLI that ignores SIGTERM needs a caller-managed termination policy. Process pipes drain concurrently from start, including when attached output is disabled. Set `AGENT_COMMANDER_DEBUG=1` for cancellation diagnostics.\n\nWhen a failed Codex or Claude run did not print its usage limit, `stop()` reads the last turn of the Codex rollout or the last entry of the Claude transcript and sets `limit_source` to `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (hive-mind#3570). A `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in `extra_env` is honoured. The checks are public: `apply_codex_rollout_usage_limit`, `detect_codex_rollout_usage_limit`, `can_resume_codex_session` (hive-mind#2888), `apply_claude_transcript_usage_limit` and `read_claude_transcript_api_error`, with `CodexRolloutOptions` and `ClaudeTranscriptOptions`. `detect_usage_limit_sources` and `is_recoverable_tool_error` are Hive Mind's classifiers.\n\nUsage preserves native final totals without adding repeated assistant snapshots. Codex `input_tokens` now counts fresh input; add `cache_read_tokens` to recover inclusive input. Serializable usage structs expose cache and reasoning fields, and Qwen/Gemini results now include `usage` too.\n\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) for the feature matrix and regression evidence.\n\n## Shared Behavior\n\nJavaScript and Rust expose the same core concepts:\n\n- Tool selection and model alias mapping\n- `none`, `screen`, and `docker` isolation modes\n- Dry-run command preview\n- JSON/NDJSON output parsing for tools that support it\n- Read-only planning mode for tools with enforceable native restrictions\n- Per-command approval (ask mode) with a normalized `permission_request`/`permission_response` relay for tools with a drivable native handshake\n\nSee [shared concepts](../docs/common-concepts.md) for behavior that should stay aligned across both packages, including the [per-command approval parity table](../docs/common-concepts.md#per-command-approval-ask-mode).\n\n## Release Flow",

The packages should keep the same user-facing behavior for common agent orchestration concepts, even when language-specific APIs differ.\n\n## Tools\n\nBoth packages support these tool names:\n\n| Tool       | Purpose                   | Read-only mode                                        |\n| ---------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |\n| `claude`   | Anthropic Claude Code CLI | `--permission-mode plan`                              |\n| `codex`    | OpenAI Codex CLI          | `--sandbox read-only`                                 |\n| `opencode` | OpenCode CLI              | permission deny rules                                 |\n| `qwen`     | Qwen Code CLI             | `--approval-mode plan`                                |\n| `gemini`   | Gemini CLI                | `--approval-mode plan`                                |\n| `agent`    | @link-assistant/agent     | `--permission-mode readonly` (`--plan-only` → `plan`) |\n\nUnsupported tools can still be executed through the generic command builder, but read-only planning mode is rejected unless the tool has an enforceable native restriction.\n\n## Per-command approval (ask mode)\n\nBoth packages support a uniform `--approve-each` flag (alias: `--permission-mode ask`) that asks the consumer to approve each command the agent wants to run, mapping to the backend's native per-command approval mechanism. When the backend exposes a drivable JSON handshake, each native permission request is relayed to the consumer as a normalized `permission_request` NDJSON event (with an opaque `id`, the `tool`, the resolved `command`/`pattern`, a `title`, and a `scope`); the consumer answers with a normalized `permission_response` carrying a decision of `once`, `always`, or `reject`, which is forwarded back to the native CLI in its own wire format.\n\n`scope` documents what an `always`/allow decision attaches to — it deliberately differs per backend, so consumers should not assume a session-wide grant everywhere.\n\n| Tool       | Native mechanism                                         | Scope              | Relay | Notes                                                                                                                  |\n| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `agent`    | `--permission-mode ask` (+ `--input-format stream-json`) | `session`          | ✅    | Native JSON `permission_request`/`permission_response` protocol; `once` \\| `always` \\| `reject` map 1:1.               |\n| `claude`   | `--permission-mode default` (stream-json `can_use_tool`) | `tool-input`       | ✅    | `control_request`/`control_response` handshake; no session-wide `always`, so `once` and `always` both allow this call. |\n| `codex`    | `--ask-for-approval` (coupled with `--sandbox`)          | `sandbox-coupled`  | ❌    | Approval is coupled with the sandbox policy and not exposed as a tool-agnostic JSON request/response stream.           |\n| `qwen`     | `--approval-mode default`                                | `interactive-only` | ❌    | Headless mode has no relayable per-command JSON approval handshake.                                                    |\n| `gemini`   | `--approval-mode default`                                | `interactive-only` | ❌    | No JSON stdin channel (prompt is passed via `-p`), so approvals cannot be relayed.                                     |\n| `opencode` | `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` (static `{edit,bash,task}` policy) | `static-policy`    | ❌    | Only a static up-front policy is available; there is no per-command request/response relay.                            |\n\nOnly `agent` and `claude` can drive the handshake (`relay = ✅`). For every other tool, `--approve-each` is rejected up front with a clear error — the same pattern `--read-only` uses for tools without an enforceable native restriction.\n\n## Isolation\n\nThe shared isolation modes are:\n\n- `none`: run the command directly in the working directory.\n- `screen`: wrap the command in a named GNU Screen session.\n- `docker`: run the command in a container with the working directory mounted.\n\n`--dry-run` should print the command that would be executed without starting a process.\n\n## Prompt Input\n\nBoth packages accept `--prompt <text>` / `prompt` for short prompts and `--prompt-file <path>` / `promptFile` / `prompt_file` for prompt content already stored on disk.\n\nFor `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agent`, `qwen`, and `gemini`, the controllers also write in-memory prompts to temporary files at execution time and pipe those files into stdin. This keeps large generated prompts out of nested shell command strings while preserving the public API used by hive-mind and similar orchestrators.\n\nFor `codex`, `opencode`, `agent`, `qwen`, and `gemini`, the temporary file contains the system prompt followed by a blank line and then the user prompt. For `claude`, the temporary file contains the user prompt and the system prompt remains a Claude CLI system-prompt argument.\n\n## Native Tool Passthrough\n\nBoth packages expose raw passthrough controls for the native commands for all six tools. These controls cover fast-moving upstream features without forcing every native CLI option into agent-commander's typed API:\n\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.executable` / Rust `AgentOptions.executable` / CLI `--tool-executable`\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.extraEnv` / Rust `AgentOptions.extra_env` / CLI `--tool-env KEY=VALUE`\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.extraArgs` / Rust `AgentOptions.extra_args` / CLI `--tool-arg`\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.skipDefaultSafetyFlags` / Rust `AgentOptions.skip_default_safety_flags` / CLI `--skip-default-safety-flags`\n\nPassthrough environment variables are attached to the native tool side of prompt pipelines, so `cat prompt.txt | env KEY=value codex exec ...` applies `KEY` to `codex` without altering prompt-file reads. Raw arguments are appended after typed arguments, allowing callers to override or extend native CLI behavior such as MCP config, reasoning config, permission modes, sandbox modes, approval modes, and custom config paths.\n\nClaude and Codex builders also expose typed `permissionMode` / `permission_mode`, `sandboxMode` / `sandbox_mode`, and `approvalMode` / `approval_mode` fields for callers that build commands directly. The `agent` builder exposes typed `permissionMode` / `permission_mode` (`auto` | `plan` | `readonly` | `ask`) and an OpenCode-compatible `permission` / `permission` JSON policy. `--read-only` maps to `readonly` and `--plan-only` maps to `plan` for `agent`.\n\n## Claude Options\n\nBoth packages expose Claude-specific options for model fallback, session management, prompt appending, verbose mode, and replaying user messages:\n\n- `appendSystemPrompt` / `append_system_prompt`\n- `fallbackModel` / `fallback_model`\n- `sessionId` / `session_id`\n- `forkSession` / `fork_session`\n- `verbose`\n- `replayUserMessages` / `replay_user_messages`\n\nThe CLI spellings are kebab-case: `--append-system-prompt`, `--fallback-model`, `--session-id`, `--fork-session`, `--verbose`, and `--replay-user-messages`.\n\n## Releases\n\nThe repository publishes separate language packages from one codebase:\n\n- JavaScript releases use Changesets, npm, `js_` tags, and `[JavaScript] vX.Y.Z` release names.\n- Rust releases use changelog fragments, crates.io, `rust_` tags, and `[Rust] vX.Y.Z` release names.\n\nRoot documentation should link to the language README files. Package README files should include registry version badges so npm and crates.io package pages show the current package status.\n\n## Dependency result contract\n\nAll six tools expose session IDs, usage and normalized metadata. 'Return a short implementation plan',\n  model: 'sonnet',\n  readOnly: true,\n});\n\nawait controller.start({ attached: false });\nconst result = await controller.stop();\n\nconsole.log(result.exitCode);\nconsole.log(result.output.plain);\nconsole.log(result.metadata);\n```\n\n`result.metadata` is a normalized summary for all six supported tools. It includes success and error classification, session ID, usage-limit reset details, result summary, cost estimates, stream token usage, optional model usage, and sub-agent call summaries.\n\n### Completion, usage and cancellation\n\nFor direct JSON runs, `metadata.success` requires a native terminal event and a successful process exit. Empty or unfinished streams report `incomplete_stream`; stderr stays in `output.plain` while parsed events, session IDs and usage come from stdout. Agent's default NDJSON mode uses the same check. Parent session metadata excludes Claude subagent-scoped results.\n\n`stop()` waits for a direct process to finish. Use `await controller.cancel()` to interrupt it and collect the final result. Unix cancellation signals the process group; Windows cancellation signals the immediate child. A native CLI that ignores SIGTERM needs a caller-managed termination policy.\n\n`stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` ends a process that stays alive after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang, hive-mind#1280). It allows `backgroundWaitMs` more while the result reports running background tasks. Such a run keeps `success: true` with `terminatedAfterResult: true`. `metadata` also reports `signal`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `apiError`, `apiErrorStatus`, `terminalReason`, `requestId`, `observedModels`, and the background-task fields.\n\nWhen a failed Codex or Claude run did not print its usage limit, `stop()` reads the last turn of the Codex rollout or the last entry of the Claude transcript and sets `limitSource` to `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (hive-mind#3570). `canResumeCodexSession({ threadId, codexHome })` tells whether `codex exec resume` can find a thread (hive-mind#2888). `detectUsageLimitSources` and `isRecoverableToolError` are Hive Mind's classifiers.\n\nUsage preserves native final totals without adding repeated assistant snapshots. Codex `inputTokens` means fresh input; inclusive input is `inputTokens + cacheReadTokens`. Cache and reasoning fields are reported when supplied. Gemini and Qwen expose token usage and native model usage through the same result contract.\n\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) and [dependency example](../examples/hive-mind-dependency.mjs), which can run against a credential-free fixture for any tool.\n\n### Real TUI capture\n\nUse `captureAgentTui()` when a test must exercise the same interactive terminal\ninterface a person sees. 'Return a short implementation plan',\n  model: 'sonnet',\n  readOnly: true,\n});\n\nawait controller.start({ attached: false });\nconst result = await controller.stop();\n\nconsole.log(result.exitCode);\nconsole.log(result.output.plain);\nconsole.log(result.metadata);\n```\n\n`result.metadata` is a normalized summary for all six supported tools. It includes success and error classification, session ID, usage-limit reset details, result summary, cost estimates, stream token usage, optional model usage, and sub-agent call summaries.\n\n### Completion, usage and cancellation\n\nFor direct JSON runs, `metadata.success` requires a native terminal event and a successful process exit. Empty or unfinished streams report `incomplete_stream`; stderr stays in `output.plain` while parsed events, session IDs and usage come from stdout. Agent's default NDJSON mode uses the same check. Parent session metadata excludes Claude subagent-scoped results.\n\n`stop()` waits for a direct process to finish. Use `await controller.cancel()` to interrupt it and collect the final result. Unix cancellation signals the process group; Windows cancellation signals the immediate child. A native CLI that ignores SIGTERM needs a caller-managed termination policy.\n\n`stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` ends a process that stays alive after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang, hive-mind#1280). It allows `backgroundWaitMs` more while the result reports running background tasks. Such a run keeps `success: true` with `terminatedAfterResult: true`. `metadata` also reports `signal`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `apiError`, `apiErrorStatus`, `terminalReason`, `requestId`, `observedModels`, and the background-task fields.\n\nWhen a failed Codex or Claude run did not print its usage limit, `stop()` reads the last turn of the Codex rollout or the last entry of the Claude transcript and sets `limitSource` to `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (hive-mind#3570). `canResumeCodexSession({ threadId, codexHome })` tells whether `codex exec resume` can find a thread (hive-mind#2888). `detectUsageLimitSources` and `isRecoverableToolError` are Hive Mind's classifiers.\n\nUsage preserves native final totals without adding repeated assistant snapshots. Codex `inputTokens` means fresh input; inclusive input is `inputTokens + cacheReadTokens`. Cache and reasoning fields are reported when supplied. Gemini and Qwen expose token usage and native model usage through the same result contract.\n\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) and [dependency example](../examples/hive-mind-dependency.mjs), which can run against a credential-free fixture for any tool.\n\n### Real TUI capture\n\nUse `captureAgentTui()` when a test must exercise the same interactive terminal\ninterface a person sees. It supports `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agent`,\n`gemini`, and `qwen` without switching them to their JSON/headless modes:",
