Codex receives the servers as one TOML `-c mcp_servers={...}` override: `headers` becomes `http_headers` and the transport `type` is implied by `command` or `url`. The TOML encoder in Rust writes keys in sorted order. Attachment paths that are relative resolve against the working directory; each path gets its own flag, because both native flags take several values.\n\n## Tool version probe\n\n`getToolVersion({ tool, executable, minimumVersion })` / `get_tool_version(tool, executable, minimum_version)` run `<tool> --version` (`buildVersionCommand` / `build_version_command`) and return `{ tool, installed, version, raw, meetsMinimum }`. `installed` is false when the shell cannot find or run the executable (exit 126 or 127). `version` is the first `x.y.z` in the output without a leading `v`. `meetsMinimum` is `null` / `None` when no minimum was asked for. `compareVersions` / `compare_versions` order versions, with a pre-release lower than its release.\n\n## Usage windows and context usage\n\nResult metadata carries two normalized views next to the token totals:\n\n- `usageWindows` / `usage_windows`: subscription windows as `{ id, kind, label, usedPercent, resetsAt, windowDurationMins }`, where `kind` is `session`, `weekly`, `monthly` or `other`, `usedPercent` is 0-100 and `resetsAt` is in epoch seconds. Claude streams them as `rate_limit_event` messages (`five_hour` is the session window, every `seven_day*` type is weekly). Codex writes `rate_limits.primary` / `secondary` to its rollout `token_count` events, which `stop()` reads after the run because `codex exec --json` does not print them. App-server `account/rateLimits/*` notifications are recognized too.\n- `contextUsage` / `context_usage`: how full the context window is, as `{ usedTokens, peakTokens, maxTokens, usedPercent, model, compactions }`. For Claude and Qwen a request fills input + cache writes + cache reads + output tokens. Sub-agent messages (`parent_tool_use_id`) are skipped, and `maxTokens` comes from the result's `modelUsage[model].contextWindow`. For Codex, `stop()` reads `last_token_usage.total_tokens` and `model_context_window` from the rollout. `compactions` counts `compact_boundary` messages. The value is `null` / `None` when the run reported no token usage.\n\nThe extractors are public for callers that read the streams themselves: `extractUsageWindows`, `usageWindowsFromMessage`, `mergeUsageWindows`, `extractContextUsage` and `contextReadingFromMessage` (snake_case in Rust).\n\n## Live input\n\n`liveInput: true` / `live_input: true` keeps the tool's stdin open as a stream-json channel for an attached run without isolation. The prompt becomes the first frame and JSON output is forced.\n\n| Tool     | `sendMessage` / `send_message`       | `interrupt`                        | Notes                                                                        |\n| -------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `claude` | text or content blocks (text, image) | `control_request` `interrupt`      | Claude can read a queued message during the running turn.                    |\n| `qwen`   | text or content blocks               | `control_request` `interrupt`      | Qwen turns non-text blocks into JSON text.                                   |\n| `agent`  | text                                 | ❌ (stop the agent instead)        | The message runs after the current turn.                                     |\n| others   | ❌                                   | ❌                                 | `codex`, `opencode` and `gemini` read a plain prompt, so `liveInput` throws. |\n\n`endInput()` / `end_input()` closes stdin so the tool finishes the queued input and exits; `stop()` and `cancel()` also close it. In JavaScript, a run that also relays permission requests keeps stdin open until the last turn reports its result.\n\n\"\"\"\ns=s.replace(\"## Isolation\\n\", section+\"## Isolation\\n\",1)\ns=s.replace(\"The [issue #50 audit](case-studies/issue-50/README.md) records\",\"The [issue #57 case study](case-studies/issue-57/README.md) covers the launch options, version probe, usage windows, context usage and live input added for hive-mind and upcomputer. It includes success and error classification, session ID, usage-limit reset details, result summary, cost estimates, stream token usage, optional model usage, and sub-agent call summaries.\n\n### Completion, usage and cancellation\n\nFor direct JSON runs, `metadata.success` requires a native terminal event and a successful process exit. Empty or unfinished streams report `incomplete_stream`; stderr stays in `output.plain` while parsed events, session IDs and usage come from stdout. Agent's default NDJSON mode uses the same check. Parent session metadata excludes Claude subagent-scoped results.\n\n`stop()` waits for a direct process to finish. Use `await controller.cancel()` to interrupt it and collect the final result. Unix cancellation signals the process group; Windows cancellation signals the immediate child. A native CLI that ignores SIGTERM needs a caller-managed termination policy.\n\n`stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` ends a process that stays alive after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang, hive-mind#1280). It allows `backgroundWaitMs` more while the result reports running background tasks. Such a run keeps `success: true` with `terminatedAfterResult: true`. `metadata` also reports `signal`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `apiError`, `apiErrorStatus`, `terminalReason`, `requestId`, `observedModels`, and the background-task fields.\n\nWhen a failed Codex or Claude run did not print its usage limit, `stop()` reads the last turn of the Codex rollout or the last entry of the Claude transcript and sets `limitSource` to `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (hive-mind#3570). `canResumeCodexSession({ threadId, codexHome })` tells whether `codex exec resume` can find a thread (hive-mind#2888). `detectUsageLimitSources` and `isRecoverableToolError` are Hive Mind's classifiers.\n\nUsage preserves native final totals without adding repeated assistant snapshots. Codex `inputTokens` means fresh input; inclusive input is `inputTokens + cacheReadTokens`. Cache and reasoning fields are reported when supplied. Gemini and Qwen expose token usage and native model usage through the same result contract.\n\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) and [dependency example](../examples/hive-mind-dependency.mjs), which can run against a credential-free fixture for any tool.\n\n### Real TUI capture\n\nUse `captureAgentTui()` when a test must exercise the same interactive terminal\ninterface a person sees. It supports `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agent`,\n`gemini`, and `qwen` without switching them to their JSON/headless modes:\n\n    approvalMode: 'never',\n  },\n});\n```\n\n## Shared Behavior\n\nJavaScript and Rust expose the same core concepts:\n\n- Tool selection and model alias mapping\n- `none`, `screen`, and `docker` isolation modes\n- Dry-run command preview\n- JSON/NDJSON output parsing for tools that support it\n- Read-only planning mode for tools with enforceable native restrictions\n- Per-command approval (ask mode) with a normalized `permission_request`/`permission_response` relay for tools with a drivable native handshake\n\nSee [shared concepts](../docs/common-concepts.md) for behavior that should stay aligned across both packages, including the [per-command approval parity table](../docs/common-concepts.md#per-command-approval-ask-mode).\n\n## Release Flow\n\nJavaScript releases use Changesets:\n1:# agent-commander\n10:## Install\n22:## CLI\n56:## Library\n61:#[tokio::main]\n113:## Completion, usage and cancellation\n127:## Shared Behavior\n140:## Release Flow\n149:### Fixed\n156:## Test\n164:## Interactive Terminal Capture\n187:# Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())",

Empty or unfinished streams return `incomplete_stream`; Agent's default NDJSON mode uses the same check. Protocol parsing and usage use stdout, while `plain_output` retains stderr diagnostics. Parent session metadata excludes Claude subagent-scoped results.\n\n`stop()` waits for a direct process to finish. `AgentStopOptions { close_timeout, background_wait, .. }` ends a process that stays alive after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang, hive-mind#1280), allowing `background_wait` more while the result reports running background tasks. Such a run keeps `success` with `terminated_after_result`. `controller.cancel().await?` interrupts it and collects the final result. Unix cancellation signals the process group; Windows cancellation signals the immediate child. A native CLI that ignores SIGTERM needs a caller-managed termination policy. Process pipes drain concurrently from start, including when attached output is disabled. Set `AGENT_COMMANDER_DEBUG=1` for cancellation diagnostics.\n\nWhen a failed Codex or Claude run did not print its usage limit, `stop()` reads the last turn of the Codex rollout or the last entry of the Claude transcript and sets `limit_source` to `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (hive-mind#3570). A `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in `extra_env` is honoured. The checks are public: `apply_codex_rollout_usage_limit`, `detect_codex_rollout_usage_limit`, `can_resume_codex_session` (hive-mind#2888), `apply_claude_transcript_usage_limit` and `read_claude_transcript_api_error`, with `CodexRolloutOptions` and `ClaudeTranscriptOptions`. `detect_usage_limit_sources` and `is_recoverable_tool_error` are Hive Mind's classifiers.\n\nUsage preserves native final totals without adding repeated assistant snapshots. Codex `input_tokens` now counts fresh input; add `cache_read_tokens` to recover inclusive input. Serializable usage structs expose cache and reasoning fields, and Qwen/Gemini results now include `usage` too.\n\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) for the feature matrix and regression evidence.\n\n## Shared Behavior\n\nJavaScript and Rust expose the same core concepts:\n\n- Tool selection and model alias mapping\n- `none`, `screen`, and `docker` isolation modes\n- Dry-run command It includes success and error classification, session ID, usage-limit reset details, result summary, cost estimates, stream token usage, optional model usage, and sub-agent call summaries. `result.usage` exposes the aggregated stream token usage as JSON for parity with the JavaScript package.\n\nFor large generated prompts, set `prompt_file` or let the controller create a temporary prompt file automatically for `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agent`, `qwen`, and `gemini`.\n\nFor parity with fast-moving native CLIs, set raw executable, environment, and argument overrides for any supported tool on `AgentOptions`:\n\n```rust\nlet mut controller = agent(AgentOptions {\n    tool: \"claude\".to_string(),\n    working_directory: \"/tmp/project\".to_string(),\n    prompt_file: Some(\"/tmp/agent-prompt.txt\".to_string()),\n    executable: Some(\"/opt/claude-code/bin/claude\".to_string()),\n    extra_env: vec![(\"MCP_TIMEOUT\".to_string(), \"10000\".to_string())],\n    // Inherited variables removed from the tool's environment\n    unset_env: vec![\"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\".to_string()],\n    extra_args: vec![\n        \"--mcp-config\".to_string(),\n        \"/tmp/mcp.json\".to_string(),\n        \"--permission-mode\".to_string(),\n        \"default\".to_string(),\n    ],\n    skip_default_safety_flags: true,\n    ..Default::default()\n})?;\n```\n\n## Completion, usage and cancellation\n\nFor direct JSON runs, `metadata.success` requires native completion and a successful process exit. Empty or unfinished streams return `incomplete_stream`; Agent's default NDJSON mode uses the same check. Protocol parsing and usage use stdout, while `plain_output` retains stderr diagnostics. Parent session metadata excludes Claude subagent-scoped results.\n\n`stop()` waits for a direct process to finish. `AgentStopOptions { close_timeout, background_wait, .. }` ends a process that stays alive after its final result (the Claude print-mode hang, hive-mind#1280), allowing `background_wait` more while the result reports running background tasks. Such a run keeps `success` with `terminated_after_result`. `controller.cancel().await?` interrupts it and collects the final result. Unix cancellation signals the process group; Windows cancellation signals the immediate child. A native CLI that ignores SIGTERM needs a caller-managed termination policy. Process pipes drain concurrently from start, including when attached output is disabled. Set `AGENT_COMMANDER_DEBUG=1` for cancellation diagnostics.\n\nWhen a failed Codex or Claude run did not print its usage limit, `stop()` reads the last turn of the Codex rollout or the last entry of the Claude transcript and sets `limit_source` to `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (hive-mind#3570). A `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in `extra_env` is honoured. The checks are public: `apply_codex_rollout_usage_limit`, `detect_codex_rollout_usage_limit`, `can_resume_codex_session` (hive-mind#2888), `apply_claude_transcript_usage_limit` and `read_claude_transcript_api_error`, with `CodexRolloutOptions` and `ClaudeTranscriptOptions`. `detect_usage_limit_sources` and `is_recoverable_tool_error` are Hive Mind's classifiers.\n\nUsage preserves native final totals without adding repeated assistant snapshots. Codex `input_tokens` now counts fresh input; add `cache_read_tokens` to recover inclusive input. Serializable usage structs expose cache and reasoning fields, and Qwen/Gemini results now include `usage` too.\n\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) for the feature matrix and regression evidence.\n\n## Shared Behavior\n\nJavaScript and Rust expose the same core concepts:\n\n- Tool selection and model alias mapping\n- `none`, `screen`, and `docker` isolation modes\n- Dry-run command preview\n- JSON/NDJSON output parsing for tools that support it\n- Read-only planning mode for tools with enforceable native restrictions\n- Per-command approval (ask mode) with a normalized `permission_request`/`permission_response` relay for tools with a drivable native handshake\n\nSee [shared concepts](../docs/common-concepts.md) for behavior that should stay aligned across both packages, including the [per-command approval parity table](../docs/common-concepts.md#per-command-approval-ask-mode).\n\n## Release Flow\nrust/src/tool_version.rs:126:pub async fn Task agents and scheduling\n\n**Scheduler.** `scheduling/Scheduler.ts`\n- One `Effect.sleep(\"5 seconds\")` loop that runs forever.\n- Each source has its own `Semaphore.make(1)` with `withPermitsIfAvailable(1)`, so a source never overlaps itself.\n\n**Task agents.** `packages/tasks-contracts/src/v1/agents.ts`\n- Triggers: `startStatuses`, `startTags`, `startRunStatuses (failed|interrupted|blocked)`.\n- Config: `{role, modelSelection, runtimeMode, interactionMode, tools, skills, instructions}`.\n\n**Agent service.** `packages/tasks-server/src/agents/TaskAgentService.ts`\n- At most one active run per task and agent.\n- `thread.create` with `sidebarHidden: true`, then `sendToThread` (L1006-1046).\n- L167-168: `PENDING_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 2*60*1000`.\n\n**Retries and result parsing.**\n- `retryOperational.ts`: capped exponential backoff from 100 ms to 5 s.\n- `TaskAgentResultParser.ts`: parses a fenced `task_agent_result` or json block containing `{status, summary, blocker, events[]}`.\n\n**Scheduled tasks.**\n- `scheduledTasks/Schedule.ts`: interval, fixed_time (HH:MM plus weekdays) or webhook. `MISSED_FIXED_TIME_GRACE_MS = 10 min`.\n- `ScheduledTaskService.ts`:\n  - Uses an idempotent `commandId` of the form `scheduled-task:${id}:${ms}:${trigger}` and runs with `concurrency: 1`.\n  - Recovers rows stuck in `running` at startup.\n  - Delivers with `sendToThread` `mode: \"queue\"`.\n  - Supports webhook verification and templates.\n\n**MCP tools exposing scheduling** (`mcp/toolkits/orchestrator/tools.ts` L117-160): `schedule_task`, `list_scheduled_tasks`, `update_scheduled_task`, `delete_scheduled_task`.\n\n## 5. Checkpointing\n\n- **Ref format** (`checkpointing/Utils.ts`): `refs/t3/checkpoints/${Base64Url(threadId)}/turn/${turnCount}`.\n- **Durable writes** (`vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts` L786-791): `-c core.fsync=objects,reference -c core.fsyncMethod=fsync`, because \"an unclean restart can leave 0-byte files under refs/t3/**\".\n- **Capture:** a temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` `t3-checkpoint-index-${uuid}` (L804), then `write-tree`, then `commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD -m \"t3 checkpoint ref=...\"` (L1025-1037), then `update-ref` (L1054).\n- **Restore:** `restore --source <oid> --worktree --staged -- .`, then `clean -fd -- .`, then `reset --quiet -- .`.\n- **Diff:** `diff --patch|--numstat -z --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv [--ignore-all-space]`.\n- **Callers:** `orchestration-v2/CheckpointService.ts` L287 and L398 (capture), L523 (restore), L551 (delete).\n\n## 6. Event logging and observability\n\n**Per-thread NDJSON provider log.** `provider/EventNdjsonLogger.ts`\n- Three streams: `native`, `canonical`, `orchestration`, labelled `NTIVE`/`CANON`/`ORCH` (around L179-181). Files are `${prefix}${threadSegment}.log`, and `_global` is used when there is no thread.\n- Limits (L29-39):\n  - Rotation and retention: `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 10 MiB`, `MAX_FILES = 10`, `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 MiB`, `MAX_AGE_MS = 14 days`.\n  - Buffering: batch window 1 s, buffer 1 MiB or 512 records.\n  - Per record: `MAX_RECORD_CHARACTERS = 64 KiB`, 1024 fields, depth 16.\n- Token-delta noise is dropped (L45-64): `content.delta`, `item/agentMessage/delta`, `agent_message_chunk` and similar. Raw frames are skipped when a decoded copy exists (\"Decoded frames carry the same information as raw frames\", around L205).\n- Oversized events become a summary (L339-370 `boundProviderEventForLogging`). The summary keeps whitelisted keys such as `session_id`, `api_error_status`, `terminal_reason`, `stop_reason` and `willRetry`, up to 8 KiB.\n\n**Paths** (`config.ts`):\n- L140: `server.trace.ndjson`, with trace limits of 10 MiB and 10 files (L199-200).\n- L142: `providerLogsDir/events.log`.\n- L58-63: OTLP URLs for traces, metrics and logs.\n\n**Metrics** (`observability/Metrics.ts` L30-38): `t3_provider_sessions_total`, `t3_provider_turns_total`, `t3_provider_turn_duration`, plus counters for git, webhooks and secrets.\n\n**Diagnostics:** `diagnostics/ProcessResourceMonitor.ts` reports `cpuPercent`, `rssBytes` and the top processes. The CLI command `t3 trace summary` (`cli/trace.ts` L150-200) prints \"counts, rates, and latency\".\n\n## 7. These controls cover fast-moving upstream features without forcing every native CLI option into agent-commander's typed API:\n\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.executable` / Rust `AgentOptions.executable` / CLI `--tool-executable`\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.extraEnv` / Rust `AgentOptions.extra_env` / CLI `--tool-env KEY=VALUE`\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.extraArgs` / Rust `AgentOptions.extra_args` / CLI `--tool-arg`\n- JavaScript `toolOptions.skipDefaultSafetyFlags` / Rust `AgentOptions.skip_default_safety_flags` / CLI `--skip-default-safety-flags`\n\nPassthrough environment variables are attached to the native tool side of prompt pipelines, so `cat prompt.txt | env KEY=value codex exec ...` applies `KEY` to `codex` without altering prompt-file reads. Raw arguments are appended after typed arguments, allowing callers to override or extend native CLI behavior such as MCP config, reasoning config, permission modes, sandbox modes, approval modes, and custom config paths.\n\nClaude and Codex builders also expose typed `permissionMode` / `permission_mode`, `sandboxMode` / `sandbox_mode`, and `approvalMode` / `approval_mode` fields for callers that build commands directly. The `agent` builder exposes typed `permissionMode` / `permission_mode` (`auto` | `plan` | `readonly` | `ask`) and an OpenCode-compatible `permission` / `permission` JSON policy. `--read-only` maps to `readonly` and `--plan-only` maps to `plan` for `agent`.\n\n## Claude Options\n\nBoth packages expose Claude-specific options for model fallback, session management, prompt appending, verbose mode, and replaying user messages:\nBundled aliases track a recorded Hive Mind catalogue (v2.39.5: `sonnet` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opus` is `claude-opus-5-5`); exact model IDs pass through for caller-managed live discovery. Omitting `model` leaves selection to the native CLI. Claude's `opus` execution alias stays rolling. Common `resume` works for all six tools; Agent adds `--no-fork`, and OpenCode uses `--session`.\n\nSee the [parity audit](../docs/case-studies/issue-50/README.md) and [dependency example](../examples/hive-mind-dependency.mjs), which can run against a credential-free fixture for any tool.\n\n### Launch options, live input and run telemetry\n\n```javascript\nimport { agent, getToolVersion } from 'agent-commander';\n\nconst { meetsMinimum } = await getToolVersion({\n  tool: 'claude',\n  minimumVersion: '2.0.0',\n});\n\nconst controller = agent({\n  tool: 'claude',\n  workingDirectory: '/tmp/project',\n  prompt: 'Refactor the parser',\n  reasoningEffort: 'high',\n  mcpConfig: {\n    mcpServers: { docs: { type: 'http', url: 'http://127.0.0.1:4100/mcp' } },\n  },\n  strictMcpConfig: true,\n  additionalDirectories: ['../shared'],\n  liveInput: true,\n});\nawait controller.start();\ncontroller.sendMessage('Keep the public API unchanged');\nconst result = await controller.stop();\nconsole.log(result.metadata.usageWindows, result.metadata.contextUsage);\n```\n\nA tool without a native flag for a launch option throws before it starts; `getLaunchCapabilities(tools.codex)` reports what a tool supports. `attachments` works for Codex (`--image`) and OpenCode (`--file`). `interrupt()` ends the running turn for Claude and Qwen; `endInput()` closes stdin. `metadata.usageWindows` comes from Claude `rate_limit_event` messages and Codex `rate_limits`; `metadata.contextUsage` reports the last and peak context fill against the model's window. [2026-10-22T14:10:58.977Z] [INFO]     "content": "//! Per-run tool overrides (issue #57).\n//!\n//! A caller replaces a failing or missing part of a tool for one run — the\n//! command builder, the output parser, the session ID or usage extractor, or\n//! the launch capabilities — without waiting for an agent-commander release.\n//! With a `build_command` an override also drives a tool that is not\n//! registered. Unset fields keep the built-in behavior.\n\nuse crate::command_builder::AgentCommandOptions;\nuse crate::tools::launch_options::LaunchCapabilities;\nuse serde_json::Value;\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Builds the native tool command (without the `cd` and isolation wrappers)\npub type BuildCommandFn = Arc<dyn Fn(&AgentCommandOptions) -> String + Send + Sync>;\n/// Parses the tool's stdout into messages\npub type ParseOutputFn = Arc<dyn Fn(&str) -> Vec<Value> + Send + Sync>;\n/// Reads the session ID from the tool's stdout\npub type ExtractSessionIdFn = Arc<dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String> + Send + Sync>;\n/// Reads the token usage from the tool's stdout\npub type ExtractUsageFn = Arc<dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Value> + Send + Sync>;\n\n/// Replacements for parts of a tool; `None` keeps the built-in part\n#[derive(Clone, Default)]\npub struct ToolOverrides {\n    /// Replaces the tool-specific command builder; it can call\n    /// [`crate::command_builder::build_base_command`] and extend the result\n    pub build_command: Option<BuildCommandFn>,\n    /// Replaces the output parser, including the streamed messages\n    pub parse_output: Option<ParseOutputFn>,\n    /// Replaces the session ID extractor\n    pub extract_session_id: Option<ExtractSessionIdFn>,\n    /// Replaces the usage extractor\n    pub extract_usage: Option<ExtractUsageFn>,\n    /// Replaces the launch capabilities checked before the run, so a builder\n    /// that adds a native flag can accept the matching launch option\n    pub launch_capabilities: Option<LaunchCapabilities>,\n}\n\nimpl ToolOverrides {\n    /// Whether no part is replaced\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.build_command.is_none()\n            && self.parse_output.is_none()\n            && self.extract_session_id.is_none()\n            && self.extract_usage.is_none()\n            && self.launch_capabilities.is_none()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Debug for ToolOverrides {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        formatter\n            .debug_struct(\"ToolOverrides\")\n            .field(\"build_command\", &self.build_command.is_some())\n            .field(\"parse_output\", &self.parse_output.is_some())\n            .field(\"extract_session_id\", &self.extract_session_id.is_some())\n            .field(\"extract_usage\", &self.extract_usage.is_some())\n            .field(\"launch_capabilities\", &self.launch_capabilities)\n            .finish()\n    }\n}\n",

The TUI tests check this argv.\n- **No live provider inference.** No live inference was run against provider CLIs, because that needs paid credentials. Native shapes come from Hive Mind's fixtures and the vendors' documentation. The e2e workflows stay credential-gated as before.\n- **Kilo gateway.** That the Kilo gateway still serves `nemotron-3-super-free` was checked only in the agent package source.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| Source                                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [Node.js `child_process`](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)                                                                         | \"On non-Windows platforms, if `options.detached` is set to true, the child process will be made the leader of a new process group and session.\" `unref()` lets the parent exit independently. This is the behavior the Rust `execute_detached` now matches.                                                                      |\n| [Bash manual, Exit Status](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Exit-Status.html)                                              | \"When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.\" The `bash -c` wrapper turns signals into exit codes, which is why X3 maps 128+N back to a signal.                                                                                                                 |\n| [Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)                                                                        | `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and the last line is a `result` message. SIGTERM gives exit 143. Background work is stopped after an idle wait that is configurable with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (C8–C10). `system/api_retry` carries `error: rate_limit` (C3). `parent_tool_use_id` marks subagent messages. |\n| [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (redirect from developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive) | \"Event types include `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.*`, and `error`.\" Progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout (X2, X4). `codex exec resume --last` / `<SESSION_ID>` resumes a run (X6).                                                                           |\n| npm registry, crates.io API, GitHub releases                                                                                                 | Every version in [dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md), and the command-stream release timeline in section 6 of the analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n| `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.12–0.26.15 package source (read only)                                                                           | `src/cli/output.ts` sends only fatal errors to stderr; `src/provider/kilo.ts` defines `nemotron-3-super-free` (A4).                                                                                                                                                                                                              |\n\n## Existing components and libraries\n\n- **command-stream** gives terminal capture, frame and recording modes, and quoting, all adopted. Its process runners were evaluated in full, and the blockers were filed (see above).\n- **Node `child_process` and Tokio `process`** stay the executor base. Process-group termination uses `process.kill(-pid)` in JS and a `kill -TERM -- -pid` shell-out in Rust, because the crate forbids `unsafe`, so `libc::kill` is not an option.\n- **Hive Mind's own libraries** (`claude.usage-limit-sources.lib.mjs`, `codex-rollout-usage-limit.lib.mjs`, `agent-error-events.lib.mjs` and the others) were ported for their general logic rather than imported. Importing them would make the dependency depend on its consumer.\n- **The `@link-assistant/agent` CLI** already defines the Kilo model, so no overlay was added.\n\n## Consumer migration\n\nEvery new field and option is additive. Hive Mind's existing `agent({...})`, `start({ attached, onOutput })` and `metadata.success` / `limitReached` / `limitResetTime` handling work unchanged. To benefit fully, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` should:\n\n1. copy the new metadata fields (`signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `limitSource`, `apiError*`, `observedModels` and the background-task fields) in `summarizeAgentCommanderResult`;\n2. pass `null` env values through instead of dropping them;\n3. replace its own `isRecoverableAgentToolError` fallback with the metadata verdict;\n4. call `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` with its own timeout values.\n\nhive-mind [#3690](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3690) tracks this. Future syncs should start from Hive Mind `5a7cb68b7` and repeat the same diff-and-classify method.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run check && npm test\ncd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\n```\n\nLocal results on 2026-10-21: `npm run check` clean and `npm test` 362 of 362 passing (Bun 362 of 362, and Deno 355 passing with 7 skipped); `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo doc` clean, and `cargo test` 358 of 358 passing. The release fragments make this a minor release.\n- **command-stream.** JS 2.4.0 and Rust 1.9.0, both released 2026-10-12, at upstream `main` `6ccdc2da`.\n\nThe issue has no comments, and PR #56 had no comments or reviews when work started.\n\nHive Mind, command-stream and the `@link-assistant/agent` package were treated as untrusted data. They were read with `git diff`, `git show` and file reads only, and never executed. Every gap was checked against both `js/src` and `rust/src`. The JavaScript gaps were reproduced by calling agent-commander's own metadata builder, and each fix landed with a regression test in both languages.\n\nThe issue asks for \"all the best practices\", so the work had to separate general behavior from Hive Mind policy, as in issue #50:\n\n- **General.** Anything that interprets a native CLI's output, exit or process lifetime belongs here. Every agent-commander consumer needs it.\n- **Policy.** Pricing tiers, retry caps, prompts, GitHub and Telegram stay in Hive Mind. They are passed in through the existing `extraArgs`, `extraEnv` and result-metadata hooks.\n\nThe full classification is in [hive-mind-delta-analysis.md](data/hive-mind-delta-analysis.md).\n\n## Every issue requirement and its execution plan\n\n| Requirement from the issue                                              | Solution and plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Delivered evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| R1. Where two commits are listed, the first is JavaScript and the second is Rust.\n\n| ID  | Gap                                                                                                                                               | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Commits              |\n| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |\n| C1  | Claude `rate_limit_event.rate_limit_info` was ignored                                                                                             | It counts as a limit when it is `rejected` with `resetsAt`, or exhausted with no overage. A rejection without a reset is a server throttle (`rate_limited`). `limitResetsAt` and `limitWindow` are reported. | `d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b` |\n| C2  | `api_error: \"usage_limit_reached\"` was not a limit                                                                                                | It is now a structured limit source.                                                                                                                                                                         | `d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b` |\n| C3  | A 429 \"(not your usage limit) · Rate limited\" was reported as a usage limit. Rust used looser patterns than JS.                                   | Throttle text is excluded and gives `errorType: 'rate_limited'`. Rust uses the JS pattern list.                                                                                                              | `d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b` |\n| C4  | A string `error` became the message, `errorType` was `assistant`, and the API details were dropped                                                | The string is the error type. `apiError`, `apiErrorStatus`, `terminalReason` and `requestId` are reported.                                                                                                   | `d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b` |\n| C5  | With `ANTHROPIC_LOG=debug`, a base64 dump became `errorMessage`, and the unified rate-limit headers were ignored                                  | `[log_…]` and base64 lines are skipped, and the `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` 429 headers are parsed.                                                                                                      | `d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b` |\n| C5b | Usage-limit errors that exist only in the Claude transcript were missed                                                                           | A best-effort read of the last transcript entry runs after a failed run that has no limit (`limitSource: 'claude-transcript'`), and the check is public.                                                     | `97be2dc`, `2c1e397` |\n| C6  | The reset time was taken from raw NDJSON (`11am (UTC)\",\"terminal_reason\"…`)                                                                       | Extracted texts are scanned first, and trailing JSON is stripped.                                                                                                                                            | `d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b` |\n| C7  | `terminate()` returned once the `bash -c` wrapper exited, so grandchildren holding the pipe could hang `stop()`. There was no SIGKILL escalation. | Termination is per process group, escalates to SIGKILL after a grace period, and waits for the group. Pipe draining is bounded after exit.                                                                   | `d83b799`, `b487dcc` |\n| C8  | Exit 143 after a completed result was a failure, with the raw JSON as `errorMessage`                                                              | A run the controller stopped after its result keeps `success` and sets `terminatedAfterResult`.                                                                                                              | `d83b799`, `b487dcc` |\n| C9  | No post-result close bound, and background tasks were not tracked (the Claude `-p` hang, hive-mind#1280)                                          | `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` / `AgentStopOptions { close_timeout, background_wait }` and `runningBackgroundTasks`. The timeout values stay with the caller.                                  | `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a` |\n| C10 | A success followed by `task_notification status: \"stopped\"` or \"Background tasks still running after Ns\" was reported as success                  | `background_tasks_stopped`, `stoppedBackgroundTasks`, `printWaitCeilingSeconds`.                                                                                                                             | `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a` |\n| C11 | The served model was not exposed, and `<synthetic>` was counted as a model                                                                        | `observedModels` / `observedModel`, and `<synthetic>` is excluded.                                                                                                                                           | `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a` |\n| C12 | An inherited environment variable could not be unset                                                                                              | JS `extraEnv: { K: null }` and Rust `unset_env` emit `env -u K`, with names validated. TUI launches go through `env -u`.                                                                                     | `36087a3`            |\n### Known limits\n\n- **TUI env removal.** command-stream's Rust terminal capture cannot remove an inherited variable, so TUI launches with `unset_env` run through `env -u` (#229). The TUI tests check this argv.\n- **No live provider inference.** No live inference was run against provider CLIs, because that needs paid credentials. Native shapes come from Hive Mind's fixtures and the vendors' documentation. The e2e workflows stay credential-gated as before.\n- **Kilo gateway.** That the Kilo gateway still serves `nemotron-3-super-free` was checked only in the agent package source.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| Source                                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [Node.js `child_process`](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)                                                                         | \"On non-Windows platforms, if `options.detached` is set to true, the child process will be made the leader of a new process group and session.\" `unref()` lets the parent exit independently. This is the behavior the Rust `execute_detached` now matches.                                                                      |\n| [Bash manual, Exit Status](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Exit-Status.html)                                              | \"When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.\" The `bash -c` wrapper turns signals into exit codes, which is why X3 maps 128+N back to a signal.                                                                                                                 |\n| [Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)                                                                        | `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and the last line is a `result` message. SIGTERM gives exit 143. Background work is stopped after an idle wait that is configurable with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (C8–C10). `system/api_retry` carries `error: rate_limit` (C3). `parent_tool_use_id` marks subagent messages. |\n| [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (redirect from developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive) | \"Event types include `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.*`, and `error`.\" Progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout (X2, X4). `codex exec resume --last` / `<SESSION_ID>` resumes a run (X6).                                                                           |\n| npm registry, crates.io API, GitHub releases                                                                                                 | Every version in [dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md), and the command-stream release timeline in section 6 of the analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n| `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.12–0.26.15 package source (read only)                                                                           | `src/cli/output.ts` sends only fatal errors to stderr; `src/provider/kilo.ts` defines `nemotron-3-super-free` (A4).                                                                                                                                                                                                              |\n\n## Existing components and libraries\n\n- **command-stream** gives terminal capture, frame and recording modes, and quoting, all adopted. Its process runners were evaluated in full, and the blockers were filed (see above).\n- **Node `child_process` and Tokio `process`** stay the executor base. Process-group termination uses `process.kill(-pid)` in JS and a `kill -TERM -- -pid` shell-out in Rust, because the crate forbids `unsafe`, so `libc::kill` is not an option.\n- **Hive Mind's own libraries** (`claude.usage-limit-sources.lib.mjs`, `codex-rollout-usage-limit.lib.mjs`, `agent-error-events.lib.mjs` and the others) were ported for their general logic rather than imported. Importing them would make the dependency depend on its consumer.\n- **The `@link-assistant/agent` CLI** already defines the Kilo model, so no overlay was added.\n\n## Consumer migration\n\nEvery new field and option is additive. Hive Mind's existing `agent({...})`, `start({ attached, onOutput })` and `metadata.success` / `limitReached` / `limitResetTime` handling work unchanged. To benefit fully, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` should:\n\n1. copy the new metadata fields (`signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `limitSource`, `apiError*`, `observedModels` and the background-task fields) in `summarizeAgentCommanderResult`;\n2. pass `null` env values through instead of dropping them;\n3. replace its own `isRecoverableAgentToolError` fallback with the metadata verdict;\n4. call `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` with its own timeout values.\n\nhive-mind [#3690](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3690) tracks this. Future syncs should start from Hive Mind `5a7cb68b7` and repeat the same diff-and-classify method.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run check && npm test\ncd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\n```\n\nLocal results on 2026-10-21: `npm run check` clean and `npm test` 362 of 362 passing (Bun 362 of 362, and Deno 355 passing with 7 skipped); `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo doc` clean, and `cargo test` 358 of 358 passing. The child runs in a detached process group with stdio `[\"pipe\",\"pipe\",\"ignore\"]` (242-256). `ClaudeHome.ts` sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. `ClaudeExecutable.ts` picks `claude.exe`/`cli.js` on Windows.\n- **L:**\n  - Query options (1058-1179) carry `resume`, `sessionId`, `resumeSessionAt`.\n  - Interrupt is `interrupt()` then close, with a 10s wait (8460-8544).\n  - Steer re-queues the message with priority `\"now\"` (8610-8656). Compact sends `\"/compact\"` (8814).\n  - Snapshot is unsupported (8961).\n  - Rollback uses a new UUID or `resumeSessionAt` (8969-9043). Fork uses `forkSession` (9044-9100).\n- **M:** `compileClaudeModelSelection` returns `apiModelId, effort, promptEffort, settings` (`apps/server/src/claudeModelOptions.ts:27-58`). Settings are `alwaysThinkingEnabled`, `fastMode`, `ultracode` (44-48). Live changes go through `setModel`/`applyFlagSettings` (856-955).\n- **P:**\n  - Runtime modes map to `plan/default/acceptEdits/auto/bypassPermissions/dontAsk` (1763-1810), with live `setPermissionMode`.\n  - `canUseTool` (7692-7911) turns `AskUserQuestion` into a user_input request. `ExitPlanMode` becomes a proposed plan, and the tool call is then denied.\n- **I:** System prompt is preset `claude_code` with `append`. Images go in as base64 blocks (1584-1678). MCP is injected through `setMcpServers`, not `--mcp-config` (729-787, 1181-1250).\n- **O:** `includePartialMessages: true`. Token usage is normalized in `ClaudeTurnTokenUsage.ts`.\n- **H:** `claude --version` (`ClaudeProvider.ts:508`). An SDK `initializationResult` probe runs at 346-426, with auth at 176-192. Manifest: supported `>=2.1.280`, graceful `2.1.111-2.1.280`.\n\n## 2. Codex (`apps/server/src/provider/CodexAdapterV2.ts`, `CodexProvider.ts`)\n- **T:** It runs `codex app-server` as JSON-RPC over stdio.\n  - Args: `[\"app-server\", ...launchArgs]` (`codexLaunchArgs.ts`), overridable with `T3CODE_CODEX_LAUNCH_ARGS`.\n  - Command is `binaryPath || \"codex\"`, wrapped by `AgentScope.wrap` and `resolveSpawnCommand` (1370-1397, 1527-1541).\n  - Env adds `CODEX_HOME` and `CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE` (`CodexProvider.ts:387-392`).\n  - `initialize` sends `experimentalApi: true` (394-405). For every other tool, `--approve-each` is rejected up front with a clear error — the same pattern `--read-only` uses for tools without an enforceable native restriction.\n\n## Launch options\n\nBoth packages map the same launch options onto each tool's native flag. A tool without a native flag rejects the option up front, naming the tools that support it, instead of dropping it silently. `getLaunchCapabilities(toolConfig)` / `launch_capabilities(tool)` report the matrix below.\n\n| Option (JS / Rust / CLI)                                                | `claude`               | `codex`                                 | `opencode`   | `qwen`                  | `gemini`                | `agent` |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ------- |\n| `reasoningEffort` / `launch.reasoning_effort` / `--reasoning-effort`    | `--effort`             | `-c model_reasoning_effort=`            | `--variant`  | ❌                      | ❌                      | ❌      |\n| `mcpConfig` / `launch.mcp_config` / `--mcp-config`                      | `--mcp-config`         | `-c mcp_servers={...}` (inline JSON)    | ❌           | `--mcp-config`          | ❌                      | ❌      |\n| `strictMcpConfig` / `launch.strict_mcp_config` / `--strict-mcp-config`  | `--strict-mcp-config`  | ❌ (overrides merge with `config.toml`) | ❌           | ❌                      | ❌                      | ❌      |\n| `additionalDirectories` / `launch.additional_directories` / `--add-dir` | `--add-dir`            | `exec --add-dir`                        | ❌           | `--include-directories` | `--include-directories` | ❌      |\n| `attachments` / `launch.attachments` / `--attach`                       | ❌ (live-input images) | `--image` (`exec` and `exec resume`)    | `run --file` | ❌ (live-input images)  | ❌                      | ❌      |\n\n`mcpConfig` takes a file path, inline JSON or (JavaScript) a `{mcpServers}` object. Codex receives the servers as one TOML `-c mcp_servers={...}` override: `headers` becomes `http_headers` and the transport `type` is implied by `command` or `url`. The TOML encoder in Rust writes keys in sorted order. Attachment paths that are relative resolve against the working directory; each path gets its own flag, because both native flags take several values.\n\n## Tool version probe\n\n`getToolVersion({ tool, executable, minimumVersion })` / `get_tool_version(tool, executable, minimum_version)` run `<tool> --version` (`buildVersionCommand` / `build_version_command`) and return `{ tool, installed, version, raw, meetsMinimum }`. `installed` is false when the shell cannot find or run the executable (exit 126 or 127). `version` is the first `x.y.z` in the output without a leading `v`. `meetsMinimum` is `null` / `None` when no minimum was asked for. `compareVersions` / `compare_versions` order versions, with a pre-release lower than its release.\n\n## Usage windows and context usage\n\nResult metadata carries two normalized views next to the token totals:\n\n- `usageWindows` / `usage_windows`: subscription windows as `{ id, kind, label, usedPercent, resetsAt, windowDurationMins }`, where `kind` is `session`, `weekly`, `monthly` or `other`, `usedPercent` is 0-100 and `resetsAt` is in epoch seconds. Claude streams them as `rate_limit_event` messages (`five_hour` is the session window, every `seven_day*` type is weekly). Codex writes `rate_limits.primary` / `secondary` to its rollout `token_count` events, which `stop()` reads after the run because `codex exec --json` does not print them. App-server `account/rateLimits/*` notifications are recognized too.\n- `contextUsage` / `context_usage`: how full the context window is, as `{ usedTokens, peakTokens, maxTokens, usedPercent, model, compactions }`. For Claude and Qwen a request fills input + cache writes + cache reads + output tokens. Sub-agent messages (`parent_tool_use_id`) are skipped, and `maxTokens` comes from the result's `modelUsage[model].contextWindow`. For Codex, `stop()` reads `last_token_usage.total_tokens` and `model_context_window` from the rollout. `compactions` counts `compact_boundary` messages. The value is `null` / `None` when the run reported no token usage.\n\nThe extractors are public for callers that read the streams themselves: `extractUsageWindows`, `usageWindowsFromMessage`, `mergeUsageWindows`, `extractContextUsage` and `contextReadingFromMessage` (snake_case in Rust).\n\n## Live input\n\n`liveInput: true` / `live_input: true` keeps the tool's stdin open as a stream-json channel for an attached run without isolation. The prompt becomes the first frame and JSON output is forced.\n\n| Tool     | `sendMessage` / `send_message`       | `interrupt`                   | Notes                                                                        |\n| -------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `claude` | text or content blocks (text, image) | `control_request` `interrupt` | Claude can read a queued message during the running turn.                    |\n| `qwen`   | text or content blocks               | `control_request` `interrupt` | Qwen turns non-text blocks into JSON text.                                   |\n| `agent`  | text                                 | ❌ (stop the agent instead)   | The message runs after the current turn.                                     |\n| others   | ❌                                   | ❌                            | `codex`, `opencode` and `gemini` read a plain prompt, so `liveInput` throws. |\n\n`endInput()` / `end_input()` closes stdin so the tool finishes the queued input and exits; `stop()` and `cancel()` also close it. In JavaScript, a run that also relays permission requests keeps stdin open until the last turn reports its result.\n\n- `success`, `exitCode`, `signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `errorDuringExecution`, `errorType`, and `errorMessage`. `errorType` includes `rate_limited` (a transient server throttle: retry it), `incomplete_stream` (the process exited before the native completion event) and `background_tasks_stopped`. A process that `stop()` ends after its completed result is not a failure.\n- `sessionId`\n- `limitReached`, `limitResetTime`, `limitTimezone`, `limitResetsAt` (epoch seconds, from structured sources) and `limitWindow` (`5-hour`, `weekly`, ...)\n- `limitSource`: set when the limit was found outside the output, as `codex-rollout` or `claude-transcript` (see below)\n- `apiError`, `apiErrorStatus`, `terminalReason`, and `requestId` (Claude API failure details)\n- `resultSummary`\n- `anthropicTotalCostUSD`, `publicPricingEstimate`, and `pricingInfo`\n- `resultModelUsage`, `streamTokenUsage`, `subAgentCalls`, `observedModels`, and `observedModel` (the models that actually answered)\n- `runningBackgroundTasks`, `backgroundTasksStopped`, `stoppedBackgroundTasks`, and `printWaitCeilingSeconds`\n- `usageWindows`: subscription windows (`{ id, kind, label, usedPercent, resetsAt, windowDurationMins }`) from Claude `rate_limit_event` messages and Codex `rate_limits`\n- `contextUsage`: context-window fill (`{ usedTokens, peakTokens, maxTokens, usedPercent, model, compactions }`)\n\nSee [usage windows and context usage](docs/common-concepts.md#usage-windows-and-context-usage) for the sources of each field.\n\n#### Usage limits that only the session files report\n\n`codex exec --json` and `claude -p` do not always print a usage limit when they fail on one. For a failed run that ended on its own, without a signal and without a limit in its output, `stop()` checks the session file the CLI wrote:\n\n- **Codex**: the last turn of `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*-<thread id>.jsonl`. It uses a `token_count` `rate_limits` window at 100% with a `resets_at`, or an `error` event with `usage_limit_exceeded`.\n- **Claude**: `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects/<working-directory slug>/<session id>.jsonl`, when its last conversation entry is an `isApiErrorMessage` usage-limit message.\n\nA `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` passed in `toolOptions.extraEnv` is honoured. Only the last turn or entry is read, so a limit the session recovered from is not reported. The same checks are exported for callers that run the CLIs themselves: `applyCodexRolloutUsageLimit`, `detectCodexRolloutUsageLimit`, `canResumeCodexSession` (a missing rollout means `codex exec resume` cannot work, so start a new session), `applyClaudeTranscriptUsageLimit` and `readClaudeTranscriptApiError`. Hive Mind's text classifiers are exported too: `detectUsageLimitSources`, `isUsageLimitText`, `extractResetTime` and `isRecoverableToolError`.\n\n### Launch Options\n\n```javascript\nconst controller = agent({\n  tool: \"codex\",\n  workingDirectory: \"/tmp/project\",\n  prompt: \"Compare the screenshot with the design\",\n  reasoningEffort: \"high\",\n  mcpConfig: {\n    mcpServers: { docs: { type: \"http\", url: \"http://127.0.0.1:4100/mcp\" } },\n  },\n  additionalDirectories: [\"../shared\"],\n  attachments: [\"screenshot.png\"],\n});\n```\n\nA tool without a native flag for an option throws before it starts. It hooks `pi.on(\"tool_call\")` and calls `ctx.ui.confirm(\\`Allow ${toolName}?\\`)`, returning `{ block: true, reason: … declined in Up.computer. }` on refusal (`mcpExtensionSource.ts:327-342`). Read-only tools pass; file edits pass in auto-accept-edits. The adapter maps `extension_ui_request` methods `select|confirm|input|editor` to approval or user_input and answers with `extension_ui_response` (`adapter.ts:1213-1285`).\n140\t- **I:** Images go in the `prompt` command. MCP and instructions come through env for the extension (T3 MCP URL/bearer, user-instructions path).\n141\t- **O:** Live usage `input/cacheRead/output/totalTokens`; \"Pi attaches the current message's cumulative usage to every streaming update (0.84.2+)\" (694-711).\n142\t- **H:** `--version` (`status.ts:201`). There is no real auth check: `authenticated: discoveredModels.length > 0` (167). Manifest: `>=0.80.5`.\n143\t\n144\t## 8. ACP registry / custom ACP agents (`packages/provider-acp-registry`, `packages/provider-acp`)\n145\t- **T:**\n146\t  - Registry: `\"https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json\"` (`AcpRegistrySupport.ts:49`).\n147\t  - Distributions: `binary` (with sha256), `npx`, `uvx`. Under `auto`, the order is `[\"binary\",\"npx\",\"uvx\"]` (422-450). npx/uvx specs \"must include an exact version\" (80-96).\n148\t  - Managed installs: `npm install --global <spec>` or `uv tool install --force <spec>` (1247-1253). Binaries are sha256-verified (1486-1488).\n149\t  - Local custom agents: `spawn: { command, args: settings.commandArgs, cwd, env, shell: false }` (1789-1808).\n150\t  - Everything goes through shared `AcpSessionRuntime` (`AcpSpawnInput {command,args,cwd,env,extendEnv}`, `AcpSessionRuntime.ts:85-92`), wrapped as AgentScope `\"acp\"`, optionally with a Linux cgroup wrapper (1440-1495).\n151\t- **L:**\n152\t  - Resume uses `session/load` if `loadSession`, else `session/resume`, else `session/new` (2179-2229).\n153\t  - Cancel is `session/cancel`; on timeout the runtime is retired (2355-2375).\n154\t  - Fork is `session/fork`, head only (`adapter.ts:7442-7470`). Rollback spawns a replacement runtime with a new sessionId (7352-7440).\n155\t  - Steer is unsupported (6952). Kill is SIGTERM then SIGKILL on the group (1617-1639), or `taskkill /T /F` on Windows (1050).\n156\t- **M:** `session/set_model`, `set_mode`, `set_config_option`, and `customModels` (`provider-acp-registry/.../adapter.ts:158-161`).\n157\t- **P:**\n158\t  - `session/request_permission` (5224). Elicitation in form and URL modes (5395-5425).\n159\t  - Approval is required if approval-required or `approvalPolicy !== \"never\"` (`clientPolicy.ts:84-86`).\n160\t  - Plan mode uses mode id `\"plan\"`/`\"architect\"` (5963-5986).\n161\t  - Client capabilities: fs read/write and terminal default false (1788-1801).\n162\t- **I:** Images `{type:\"image\", data, mimeType}`, with instructions appended as text (6355-6380). MCP uses `acpMcpServers` if the agent has `mcpCapabilities.acp`, else `mcpServers` (2108-2120).\n163\t- **O:** `agent_thought_chunk, tool_call(_update), plan, usage_update, available_commands_update, config_option_update, current_mode_update` (3761-3776). Vendor extras: Copilot `github.com/copilot/sessionEvent` (`copilotAcp.ts:16`), plus `devinAcp.ts`.\n164\t- **H:** `probe.ts` runs `initialize` and reads `authMethods`, `loadSession`, `sessionCapabilities.list/resume/delete`, `auth.logout` (251-258). Auth is lazy after an auth-required error, or eager (2125-2240).\n165\t\n166\t## 9. Muse (`packages/provider-muse/src/server`)\n167\t- **T:**\n168\t  - `@muse-code/sdk` `spawnMspConnection` (`sdk.ts:6-11`) runs `muse … serve`, wrapped as AgentScope `\"muse\"` (`adapter.ts:1614-1630`).\n169\t  - Args (`sdk.ts:139-150`):\n170\t    - Normal: `--trust-workspace`, plus `--disable-sandbox` for full-access.\n171\t    - Read-only probe: `--disable-shell --disable-write --no-session-log`.\n172\t  - Env drops `META_API_KEY` (53-61). Fork: \"does not support native forks\" (2256-2272).\n178\t- **M:** `model/list`, which must be `providerId \"meta\"` (`modelCatalog.ts:116-121`). `session/setModel` (1891).\n179\t- **P:**\n180\t  - `approvalMode`: `\"allowAll\"` for full-access, else `\"promptUnmatched\"`. `permissionProfile`: `\":unrestricted\"`, else `\":ask-me\"`. The code notes this avoids Muse's default `:auto-review` (`sdk.ts:126-137`).\n181\t  - Approvals are answered with `approval/decide {approvalId, requirementId, choiceId}` (1046-1050). Questions arrive as `request_user_input` (225, 1167-1172).\n182\t- **I:** Text with attachment paths, plus images as `{type:\"image\", base64Data, mediaType}` (1827-1846). Capabilities: `supportsActiveSteering: true`, `canRollbackThread: false` (100-124).\n184\t- **H:** `--version` (`status.ts:75`). Auth is always unknown: \"MSP has no auth signal, and model/list answers from Muse's cache even when logged out.\" (136-137). Manifest: `>=1.4.2`. The `-R<n>` suffix is stripped from versions.\n185\t\n186\t## Cross-provider abstractions\n187\t- **Adapter interface:** `packages/provider-core/src/server/ProviderAdapter.ts:633-649`:\n188\t  > `ProviderAdapterV2 extends Context.Service<…, { instanceId; driver; getCapabilities(); planSelectionTransition(input); openSession(input): Effect<SessionRuntime, Error, Scope> }>`\n189\t\n190\t  `SessionRuntime` (537-631):\n191\t  - Required: `ensureThread, resumeThread, startTurn, steerTurn, interruptTurn, respondToRuntimeRequest, readThreadSnapshot, rollbackThread, forkThread`.\n192\t  - Optional: `injectHistory, compactThread, stopTask, stopSubagent, unloadThread, mcpApps, getModelContextWindow, subscribeEvents, hasPendingBackgroundWork`.\n193\t- **Runtime policy:** `RuntimePolicy` (48-57) = `runtimeMode, interactionMode, cwd, additionalDirectories, approvalPolicy, sandboxPolicy, reasoningEffort`. Every driver maps it to its native knobs.\n194\t- **Adapter events:** The adapter-level union (81-170) is `provider_session.updated, provider_thread.updated, provider_turn.updated, node.updated, subagent.updated, message.updated, turn_item.updated, command_output.delta, runtime_request.updated, plan.updated, turn.terminal`, among others.\n195\t- **Canonical runtime events:** `packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts:152-200` includes:\n196\t  - `session.started/configured/state.changed/exited`\n197\t  - `thread.started`, `thread.token-usage.updated` (159)\n198\t  - `turn.started/completed/aborted/plan.updated/proposed.delta/diff.updated`\n199\t  - `item.started/updated/completed`, `content.delta`\n200\t  - `request.opened/resolved`, `user-input.requested/resolved`\n201\t  - `task.*`, `hook.*`, `tool.progress/summary/denied`\n202\t  - `auth.status`, `account.rate-limits.updated`, `mcp.status.updated`, `model.rerouted`, `runtime.warning/error`\n203\t  - Raw sources: `\"codex.eventmsg\"`, `\"claude.sdk.message\"`, `\"opencode.sdk.event\"`, `\"acp.jsonrpc\"` (26-31).\n204\t- **Shared plumbing:**\n205\t  - `AgentScope.wrap` and `resolveSpawnCommand` for launches.\n206\t  - Process-group SIGTERM then SIGKILL, or `taskkill /T /F` on Windows.\n207\t  - One authenticated \"t3-code\" HTTP MCP server, injected per provider: SDK `setMcpServers`, Codex config, Cursor `mcpServers`, OpenCode `mcp.add`, ACP `mcpServers`, Pi extension env, Muse session config.\n208\t  - Shared `AcpSessionRuntime` behind Grok, Antigravity and registry agents.\n209\t  - Image attachments plus `providerMessageTextWithAttachmentPaths`.\n210\t- **Version compatibility:** `apps/server/src/provider/providerCompatibility.ts:59-103` matches the probed version against `model-manifest.json` ranges and returns `broken | unsupported | graceful`.\n211\t- **Not found:** No provider is driven by a one-shot shell command parsing NDJSON from stdout, which is agent-commander's model. All are long-lived protocol sessions:\n212\t  - SDK in-process (Claude, Cursor)\n213\t  - JSON-RPC (Codex, Muse)\n214\t  - ACP (Grok, Antigravity, registry)\n215\t  - HTTP+SSE (OpenCode)\n216\t  - RPC (Pi)\n217\t\n218\t  Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` have no dedicated drivers. Claude Code (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAdapterV2.ts`, `ClaudeProvider.ts`)\n- **T:** It uses the Claude Agent SDK `query()` with a streaming prompt queue, not a hand-built shell command. The child runs in a detached process group with stdio `[\"pipe\",\"pipe\",\"ignore\"]` (242-256). `ClaudeHome.ts` sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. `ClaudeExecutable.ts` picks `claude.exe`/`cli.js` on Windows.\n- **L:**\n  - Query options (1058-1179) carry `resume`, `sessionId`, `resumeSessionAt`.\n  - Interrupt is `interrupt()` then close, with a 10s wait (8460-8544).\n  - Steer re-queues the message with priority `\"now\"` (8610-8656). Fork uses `forkSession` (9044-9100).\n- **M:** `compileClaudeModelSelection` returns `apiModelId, effort, promptEffort, settings` (`apps/server/src/claudeModelOptions.ts:27-58`). Settings are `alwaysThinkingEnabled`, `fastMode`, `ultracode` (44-48). Live changes go through `setModel`/`applyFlagSettings` (856-955).\n- **P:**\n  - Runtime modes map to `plan/default/acceptEdits/auto/bypassPermissions/dontAsk` (1763-1810), with live `setPermissionMode`.\n  - `canUseTool` (7692-7911) turns `AskUserQuestion` into a user_input request. `ExitPlanMode` becomes a proposed plan, and the tool call is then denied.\n- **I:** System prompt is preset `claude_code` with `append`. Images go in as base64 blocks (1584-1678). MCP is injected through `setMcpServers`, not `--mcp-config` (729-787, 1181-1250).\n- **O:** `includePartialMessages: true`. Token usage is normalized in `ClaudeTurnTokenUsage.ts`.\n- **H:** `claude --version` (`ClaudeProvider.ts:508`). An SDK `initializationResult` probe runs at 346-426, with auth at 176-192. Manifest: supported `>=2.1.280`, graceful `2.1.111-2.1.280`.\n\n## 2. Codex (`apps/server/src/provider/CodexAdapterV2.ts`, `CodexProvider.ts`)\n- **T:** It runs `codex app-server` as JSON-RPC over stdio.\n  - Args: `[\"app-server\", ...launchArgs]` (`codexLaunchArgs.ts`), overridable with `T3CODE_CODEX_LAUNCH_ARGS`.\n  - Command is `binaryPath || \"codex\"`, wrapped by `AgentScope.wrap` and `resolveSpawnCommand` (1370-1397, 1527-1541).\n  - Env adds `CODEX_HOME` and `CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE` (`CodexProvider.ts:387-392`).\n  - `initialize` sends `experimentalApi: true` (394-405). fixes:\n75\t\n76\t- **Model catalogue** synced to v2.39.5: Claude 5.5 family, Codex `sol`/`luna`/`astra`, the Kilo default for Agent, OpenCode `big-pickle`, the Qwen catalogue (`4367abf`, `0f729b9`). The withdrawn `openai/formal-ai` aliases were removed in Rust as well (`24e0014`).\n77\t- **JSON records.** Agent's default output is pretty-printed or concatenated JSON rather than NDJSON. Both parsers now read multi-line and back-to-back records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`). A shared JSON-lines parser and model mapper replaced the per-tool copies first (`872657e`).\n78\t- **Agent fatal errors on stderr.** The agent 0.26.15 source (`src/cli/output.ts`) prints only fatal errors, such as an unknown model, to stderr, so the metadata said only \"Process exited with code 1\". A failed exit with no error event on stdout now uses the last JSON error record of the output (`6ec13f1`, reproduced by [experiments/agent-stderr-error.mjs](../../../experiments/agent-stderr-error.mjs)).\n79\t- **Rust generic-tool quoting.** `build_tool_command` used a single-quote escape inside double quotes, so bash expanded `$`, backticks and `\"`. It now uses `escape_arg` like JS (`05d7264`).\n80\t- **Rust detached process group.** `execute_detached` left the child in the caller's process group, so Ctrl+C to the caller also stopped the agent. Node's `detached: true` makes the child \"the leader of a new process group and session\". The Rust helper now sets `process_group(0)`. `test_execute_detached_leads_its_own_process_group` failed before the fix (pgid 425119 ≠ pid 425409) and passes after it (`3851352`).\n81\t\n82\t### Hive Mind policy left to the caller\n83\t\n84\tThe following stay in Hive Mind, passed through `extraArgs` / `extraEnv` or derived from the metadata:\n85\t\n86\t- pricing tiers and context windows (`service_tier`, `model_context_window`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT`);\n87\t- Codex `features.goals` and memory overrides;\n88\t- Formal AI pricing and attribution;\n89\t- OOM, disk and container recovery, and the Codex trace-file routing;\n90\t- retry and auto-resume decisions, and close-timeout values;\n91\t- loop reports and version probes;\n92\t- prompts, GitHub, Telegram and queues.\n93\t\n94\tCopying any of these into agent-commander would duplicate Hive Mind's policy state (see section (c) of the delta analysis).\n95\t\n96\t## Dependency updates\n97\t\n98\tAll packages were checked on 2026-10-21 against npm, crates.io, GitHub releases and the pre-commit hook repositories ([dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md)).\n99\t\n100\t- **npm** (`62a4a1a`): @changesets/cli 3, ESLint and @eslint/js 10, jscpd 5, lint-staged 17, prettier 3.9.10 and eslint-plugin-prettier 5.5.7.
