The Rust command-stream upgrade broke three struct literals in `tui.rs`, which were fixed in the same commit. jscpd 5's validation exposed that duplicate detection had never run.\n138\t2. **Shared parsing, then the catalogue** (`872657e`, `4367abf`). Without parsing the agent's pretty-printed records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`), the agent default output ended as `incomplete_stream`.\n139\t3. **Classification port** (`d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b`). Each of C1–C6, X1, X2, X4 and A1–A3 started as a probe against `buildNormalizedResultMetadata`, then became a shared fixture. One example: a Codex failure whose tool output quoted a limit reported `limitReached: true` with a reset time full of JSON.\n140\t4. **Process lifetime** (`d83b799`, `b487dcc`, `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a`). A finite fixture forks a grandchild that holds stdout, then exits the wrapper. Before the fix `stop()` waited for the grandchild, and after it the group is terminated and draining is bounded.\n141\t5. **Sandbox finding.** In the test sandbox, PID 1 never reaps zombies, so a killed process group stays visible to `kill -0`. [experiments/process-group-reap.mjs](../../../experiments/process-group-reap.mjs) shows this. The group tests therefore check for live, non-zombie members with `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` instead of `kill -0`.\n142\t6. **Session files, env, aliases** (`c41770c`, `0219c31`, `97be2dc`, `2c1e397`, `36087a3`, `c7066de`). These use synthetic `CODEX_HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trees in temporary directories, so no credentials are read.\n143\t7. **command-stream features and quoting** (`decbeba`, `5e479d0`, `05d7264`), the **agent stderr error** (`6ec13f1`), and the **Rust detached process group** (`3851352`). The last one was found while writing #232.\n144\t8. **CI-only failures** (`d6b4591`, `55d2c74`). Two failures appeared only in the CI matrix:\n145\t   - Deno on all three OSes: `NotCapable: Requires sys access to \"homedir\"`. The session-file helpers called `os.homedir()` as a default parameter even when `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` was set. This also affected Deno consumers. The home directory is now read lazily, with a `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` fallback. The failure was reproduced locally with the CI's `deno test` flags (7 failed), and passes after the fix.\n146\t   - Rust on macOS: `File exists (os error 17)` in `gemini_controller_collects_formatted_json`. Prompt temp directories were named `agent-commander-{pid}-{nanos}`, and parallel tests on macOS's coarse clock got the same name. Names now carry a per-process sequence, and existing names are skipped. `prompt_dirs_are_unique_within_one_clock_tick` creates two directories with the same clock value, which failed under the old naming.\n147\t\n148\t### Known limits\n149\t\n150\t- **TUI env removal.** command-stream's Rust terminal capture cannot remove an inherited variable, so TUI launches with `unset_env` run through `env -u` (#229). The TUI tests check this argv.\n151\t- **No live provider inference.** No live inference was run against provider CLIs, because that needs paid credentials. Native shapes come from Hive Mind's fixtures and the vendors' documentation. The e2e workflows stay credential-gated as before.\n152\t- **Kilo gateway.** That the Kilo gateway still serves `nemotron-3-super-free` was checked only in the agent package source.\n153\t\n154\t## Primary-source research\n155\t\n156\t| Source                                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\n157\t| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n158\t| [Node.js `child_process`](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)                                                                         | \"On non-Windows platforms, if `options.detached` is set to true, the child process will be made the leader of a new process group and session.\" `unref()` lets the parent exit independently. This is the behavior the Rust `execute_detached` now matches.                                                                      |\n159\t| [Bash manual, Exit Status](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Exit-Status.html)                                              | \"When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.\" The `bash -c` wrapper turns signals into exit codes, which is why X3 maps 128+N back to a signal.                                                                                                                 |\n160\t| [Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)                                                                        | `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and the last line is a `result` message. SIGTERM gives exit 143. Background work is stopped after an idle wait that is configurable with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (C8–C10). `system/api_retry` carries `error: rate_limit` (C3). `parent_tool_use_id` marks subagent messages. |\n161\t| [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (redirect from developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive) | \"Event types include `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.*`, and `error`.\" Progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout (X2, X4). `codex exec resume --last` / `<SESSION_ID>` resumes a run (X6).                                                                           |\n162\t| npm registry, crates.io API, GitHub releases                                                                                                 | Every version in [dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md), and the command-stream release timeline in section 6 of the analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n163\t| `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.12–0.26.15 package source (read only)                                                                           | `src/cli/output.ts` sends only fatal errors to stderr; `src/provider/kilo.ts` defines `nemotron-3-super-free` (A4).                                                                                                                                                                                                              |\n164\t\n165\t## Existing components and libraries\n166\t\n167\t- **command-stream** gives terminal capture, frame and recording modes, and quoting, all adopted. Its process runners were evaluated in full, and the blockers were filed (see above).\n168\t- **Node `child_process` and Tokio `process`** stay the executor base. Process-group termination uses `process.kill(-pid)` in JS and a `kill -TERM -- -pid` shell-out in Rust, because the crate forbids `unsafe`, so `libc::kill` is not an option.\n169\t- **Hive Mind's own libraries** (`claude.usage-limit-sources.lib.mjs`, `codex-rollout-usage-limit.lib.mjs`, `agent-error-events.lib.mjs` and the others) were ported for their general logic rather than imported. Importing them would make the dependency depend on its consumer.\n170\t- **The `@link-assistant/agent` CLI** already defines the Kilo model, so no overlay was added.\n171\t\n172\t## Consumer migration\n173\t\n174\tEvery new field and option is additive. Hive Mind's existing `agent({...})`, `start({ attached, onOutput })` and `metadata.success` / `limitReached` / `limitResetTime` handling work unchanged. To benefit fully, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` should:\n175\t\n176\t1. copy the new metadata fields (`signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `limitSource`, `apiError*`, `observedModels` and the background-task fields) in `summarizeAgentCommanderResult`;\n177\t2. pass `null` env values through instead of dropping them;\n178\t3. replace its own `isRecoverableAgentToolError` fallback with the metadata verdict;\n179\t4. call `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` with its own timeout values.\n180\t\n181\thive-mind [#3690](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3690) tracks this. Future syncs should start from Hive Mind `5a7cb68b7` and repeat the same diff-and-classify method.\n182\t\n183\t## Validation\n184\t\n185\t```bash\n186\tcd js && npm run check && npm test\n187\tcd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\n188\t```\n189\t\n190\tLocal results on 2026-10-21: `npm run check` clean and `npm test` 362 of 362 passing (Bun 362 of 362, and Deno 355 passing with 7 skipped); `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo doc` clean, and `cargo test` 358 of 358 passing. Every agent-commander consumer needs it.\n- **Policy.** Pricing tiers, retry caps, prompts, GitHub and Telegram stay in Hive Mind. synced to v2.39.5: Claude 5.5 family, Codex `sol`/`luna`/`astra`, the Kilo default for Agent, OpenCode `big-pickle`, the Qwen catalogue (`4367abf`, `0f729b9`). It now uses `escape_arg` like JS (`05d7264`).\n- **Rust detached process group.** `execute_detached` left the child in the caller's process group, so Ctrl+C to the caller also stopped the agent. Node's `detached: true` makes the child \"the leader of a new process group and session\". The Rust helper now sets `process_group(0)`. `test_execute_detached_leads_its_own_process_group` failed before the fix (pgid 425119 ≠ pid 425409) and passes after it (`3851352`).\n\n### Hive Mind policy left to the caller\n\nThe following stay in Hive Mind, passed through `extraArgs` / `extraEnv` or derived from the metadata:\n\n- pricing tiers and context windows (`service_tier`, `model_context_window`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT`);\n- Codex `features.goals` and memory overrides;\n- Formal AI pricing and attribution;\n- OOM, disk and container recovery, and the Codex trace-file routing;\n- retry and auto-resume decisions, and close-timeout values;\n- loop reports and version probes;\n- prompts, GitHub, Telegram and queues.\n\nCopying any of these into agent-commander would duplicate Hive Mind's policy state (see section (c) of the delta analysis).\n\n## Dependency updates\n\nAll packages were checked on 2026-10-21 against npm, crates.io, GitHub releases and the pre-commit hook repositories ([dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md)).\n\n- **npm** (`62a4a1a`): @changesets/cli 3, ESLint and @eslint/js 10, jscpd 5, lint-staged 17, prettier 3.9.10 and eslint-plugin-prettier 5.5.7. The Rust command-stream upgrade broke three struct literals in `tui.rs`, which were fixed in the same commit. jscpd 5's validation exposed that duplicate detection had never run.\n2. **Shared parsing, then the catalogue** (`872657e`, `4367abf`). Without parsing the agent's pretty-printed records (`99ca23b`, `c7b0176`), the agent default output ended as `incomplete_stream`.\n3. **Classification port** (`d0c0e96`, `cd68c2b`). Each of C1–C6, X1, X2, X4 and A1–A3 started as a probe against `buildNormalizedResultMetadata`, then became a shared fixture. One example: a Codex failure whose tool output quoted a limit reported `limitReached: true` with a reset time full of JSON.\n4. **Process lifetime** (`d83b799`, `b487dcc`, `95acdbe`, `3b4e97a`). A finite fixture forks a grandchild that holds stdout, then exits the wrapper. Before the fix `stop()` waited for the grandchild, and after it the group is terminated and draining is bounded.\n5. **Sandbox finding.** In the test sandbox, PID 1 never reaps zombies, so a killed process group stays visible to `kill -0`. [experiments/process-group-reap.mjs](../../../experiments/process-group-reap.mjs) shows this. The group tests therefore check for live, non-zombie members with `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` instead of `kill -0`.\n6. **Session files, env, aliases** (`c41770c`, `0219c31`, `97be2dc`, `2c1e397`, `36087a3`, `c7066de`). These use synthetic `CODEX_HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trees in temporary directories, so no credentials are read.\n7. **command-stream features and quoting** (`decbeba`, `5e479d0`, `05d7264`), the **agent stderr error** (`6ec13f1`), and the **Rust detached process group** (`3851352`). The last one was found while writing #232.\n8. **CI-only failures** (`d6b4591`, `55d2c74`). Two failures appeared only in the CI matrix:\n   - Deno on all three OSes: `NotCapable: Requires sys access to \"homedir\"`. The session-file helpers called `os.homedir()` as a default parameter even when `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` was set. This also affected Deno consumers. The home directory is now read lazily, with a `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` fallback. The failure was reproduced locally with the CI's `deno test` flags (7 failed), and passes after the fix.\n   - Rust on macOS: `File exists (os error 17)` in `gemini_controller_collects_formatted_json`. Prompt temp directories were named `agent-commander-{pid}-{nanos}`, and parallel tests on macOS's coarse clock got the same name. Names now carry a per-process sequence, and existing names are skipped. `prompt_dirs_are_unique_within_one_clock_tick` creates two directories with the same clock value, which failed under the old naming.\n\n### Known limits\n\n- **TUI env removal.** command-stream's Rust terminal capture cannot remove an inherited variable, so TUI launches with `unset_env` run through `env -u` (#229). The TUI tests check this argv.\n- **No live provider inference.** No live inference was run against provider CLIs, because that needs paid credentials. Native shapes come from Hive Mind's fixtures and the vendors' documentation. The e2e workflows stay credential-gated as before.\n- **Kilo gateway.** That the Kilo gateway still serves `nemotron-3-super-free` was checked only in the agent package source.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| Source                                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| [Node.js `child_process`](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)                                                                         | \"On non-Windows platforms, if `options.detached` is set to true, the child process will be made the leader of a new process group and session.\" `unref()` lets the parent exit independently. This is the behavior the Rust `execute_detached` now matches.                                                                      |\n| [Bash manual, Exit Status](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Exit-Status.html)                                              | \"When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.\" The `bash -c` wrapper turns signals into exit codes, which is why X3 maps 128+N back to a signal.                                                                                                                 |\n| [Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)                                                                        | `stream-json` requires `--verbose`, and the last line is a `result` message. SIGTERM gives exit 143. Background work is stopped after an idle wait that is configurable with `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (C8–C10). `system/api_retry` carries `error: rate_limit` (C3). `parent_tool_use_id` marks subagent messages. |\n| [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) (redirect from developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive) | \"Event types include `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `item.*`, and `error`.\" Progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout (X2, X4). `codex exec resume --last` / `<SESSION_ID>` resumes a run (X6).                                                                           |\n| npm registry, crates.io API, GitHub releases                                                                                                 | Every version in [dependency-versions.md](data/dependency-versions.md), and the command-stream release timeline in section 6 of the analysis.                                                                                                                                                                                    |\n| `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.12–0.26.15 package source (read only)                                                                           | `src/cli/output.ts` sends only fatal errors to stderr; `src/provider/kilo.ts` defines `nemotron-3-super-free` (A4).                                                                                                                                                                                                              |\n\n## Existing components and libraries\n\n- **command-stream** gives terminal capture, frame and recording modes, and quoting, all adopted. Its process runners were evaluated in full, and the blockers were filed (see above).\n- **Node `child_process` and Tokio `process`** stay the executor base. Process-group termination uses `process.kill(-pid)` in JS and a `kill -TERM -- -pid` shell-out in Rust, because the crate forbids `unsafe`, so `libc::kill` is not an option.\n- **Hive Mind's own libraries** (`claude.usage-limit-sources.lib.mjs`, `codex-rollout-usage-limit.lib.mjs`, `agent-error-events.lib.mjs` and the others) were ported for their general logic rather than imported. Importing them would make the dependency depend on its consumer.\n- **The `@link-assistant/agent` CLI** already defines the Kilo model, so no overlay was added.\n\n## Consumer migration\n\nEvery new field and option is additive. Hive Mind's existing `agent({...})`, `start({ attached, onOutput })` and `metadata.success` / `limitReached` / `limitResetTime` handling work unchanged. To benefit fully, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` should:\n\n1. copy the new metadata fields (`signal`, `terminatedAfterResult`, `limitResetsAt`, `limitWindow`, `limitSource`, `apiError*`, `observedModels` and the background-task fields) in `summarizeAgentCommanderResult`;\n2. pass `null` env values through instead of dropping them;\n3. replace its own `isRecoverableAgentToolError` fallback with the metadata verdict;\n4. call `stop({ closeTimeoutMs, backgroundWaitMs })` with its own timeout values.\n\nhive-mind [#3690](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3690) tracks this. Future syncs should start from Hive Mind `5a7cb68b7` and repeat the same diff-and-classify method.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run check && npm test\ncd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\n```\n\nLocal results on 2026-10-21: `npm run check` clean and `npm test` 362 of 362 passing (Bun 362 of 362, and Deno 355 passing with 7 skipped); `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo doc` clean, and `cargo test` 358 of 358 passing. Requires `--config` pointing at a [`gateway.yaml`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config). | `claude gateway --config gateway.yaml` |\n| `claude install [version]` | Install or reinstall the native binary. Accepts a version like `2.1.118`, or `stable` or `latest`. See [Install a specific version](/docs/en/setup#install-a-specific-version) | `claude install stable` |\n| `claude auth login` | Sign in to your Anthropic account. Use `--email` to pre-fill your email address, `--sso` to force SSO authentication, and `--console` to sign in with Anthropic Console for API usage billing instead of a Claude subscription | `claude auth login --console` |\n| `claude auth logout` | Log out from your Anthropic account | `claude auth logout` |\n| `claude auth status` | Show authentication status as JSON. Use `--text` for human-readable output. Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not. The JSON includes a `configDirectory` field naming the [configuration directory](/docs/en/claude-directory) the CLI uses. The field requires Claude Code v2.1.268 or later. The JSON's `authMethod` field is one of `none`, `claude.ai`, `oauth_token`, `api_key`, `api_key_helper`, or `third_party` | `claude auth status` |\n| `claude agents` | Open [agent view](/docs/en/agent-view) to monitor and dispatch parallel background sessions. Use `--cwd <path>` to show only sessions started under that directory, or `--json` to print active sessions as a JSON array for scripting (`--json --all` also includes completed background sessions). Pass `--permission-mode`, `--model`, `--effort`, or `--agent` to set [defaults for dispatched sessions](/docs/en/agent-view#permission-mode-model-and-effort). Accepts `--settings`, `--add-dir`, `--plugin-dir`, and `--mcp-config` like the top-level `claude` command. Opening agent view requires an interactive terminal | `claude agents --json` |\n| `claude attach <id\\|name>` | Attach to a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell) in this terminal. Passing part of a running session's name in place of the ID requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later | `claude attach 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude auto-mode defaults` | Print the built-in [auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) classifier rules as JSON. Use `claude auto-mode config` to see your effective config with settings applied. `--label <prefix>` prints only the rules whose label starts with that prefix, matched case-insensitively. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later | `claude auto-mode defaults --label 'Git Destructive'` |\n| `claude auto-mode reset` | Restore the default [auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) configuration by removing the `autoMode` section from your user settings file. Prompts for confirmation before writing; pass `-y`/`--yes` to skip the prompt. Rules from [managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings) or the `--settings` flag still apply. Requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later. See [Inspect the defaults and your effective config](/docs/en/auto-mode-config#inspect-the-defaults-and-your-effective-config) | `claude auto-mode reset --yes` |\n| `claude daemon logs` | Follow the background-session [supervisor's](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) log file, `~/.claude/daemon.log`, printing new lines as they arrive until you press `Ctrl+C` | `claude daemon logs` |\n| `claude daemon run` | Run the background-session [supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) in the foreground of this terminal, printing its log | `claude daemon run` |\n| `claude daemon status` | Print the background-session [supervisor's](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) state, version, socket directory, and worker count for diagnostics. Exits 1 if the supervisor isn't running | `claude daemon status` |\n| `claude daemon stop --any` | Stop the background-session [supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) and the sessions it hosts. Pass `--keep-workers` to leave background sessions running for the next supervisor to reconnect to. `--any` confirms stopping an on-demand supervisor, which is the default. Use this to recover from an [unresponsive supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#agent-view-says-the-background-service-did-not-respond) | `claude daemon stop --any --keep-workers` |\n| `claude doctor` | Print read-only installation and settings diagnostics from the terminal without starting a session, including install health, settings-file validation errors, and Remote Control eligibility. For the in-session setup checkup that can also apply fixes, run [`/doctor`](/docs/en/commands#all-commands) | `claude doctor` |\n| `claude import [source]` | Start an interactive session that runs [`/import`](/docs/en/commands#all-commands) to bring configuration from other coding agents into Claude Code. Accepts the same `--dry-run` and `--yes` options as the command. Not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or Claude Platform on AWS. Also unavailable when you turn off [feature-flag fetching](/docs/en/env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching). Requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later | `claude import codex --dry-run` |\n| `claude logs <id\\|name>` | Print recent output from a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell). Passing part of a session's name in place of the ID requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later | `claude logs 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude mcp` | Configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers | See the [Claude Code MCP documentation](/docs/en/mcp). |\n| `claude mcp login <name>` | Run a configured MCP server's OAuth flow without opening the interactive `/mcp` panel. Works for HTTP, SSE, and claude.ai connector servers. Add `--no-browser` over SSH to print the authorization URL instead of opening a browser. For an HTTP or SSE server, paste the redirect URL back at the prompt. For a claude.ai connector, see [Authorize a connector again from your shell](/docs/en/remote-control#authorize-a-connector-again-from-your-shell). See [Authenticate from the command line](/docs/en/mcp#authenticate-from-the-command-line) | `claude mcp login sentry` |\n| `claude mcp logout <name>` | Clear stored OAuth credentials for an MCP server | `claude mcp logout sentry` |\n| `claude plugin` | Manage Claude Code [plugins](/docs/en/plugins/overview). Alias: `claude plugins`. See [plugin reference](/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#claude-plugin-commands) for subcommands | `claude plugin install code-review@claude-plugins-official` |\n| `claude purge [path]` | Delete all local Claude Code state for a project: transcripts, task lists, debug logs, file-edit history, prompt history lines, and the project's entry in `~/.claude.json`. Omit `[path]` to pick from an interactive list. Flags: `--dry-run` to preview, `-y`/`--yes` to skip confirmation, `-i`/`--interactive` to confirm each item, `--all` for every project. See [Clear local data](/docs/en/claude-directory#clear-local-data) | `claude purge ~/work/repo --dry-run` |\n| `claude remote-control` | Start a [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) server to control Claude Code from Claude.ai or the Claude app. Runs in server mode (no local interactive session). See [Server mode flags](/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session). After you stop the server, you can bring back the sessions it was serving. See [Resume sessions after stopping the server](/docs/en/remote-control#resume-sessions-after-stopping-the-server) | `claude remote-control --name \"My Project\"` |\n| `claude respawn <id>` | Restart a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell), running or stopped, with its conversation intact. Use `--all` to restart every running session, e.g. to pick up an updated Claude Code binary | `claude respawn 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude rm <id>` | Remove a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell) from the list. When the removal is [refused over the session's worktree](/docs/en/agent-view#what-deleting-a-session-removes) and a second `claude rm` can resolve it, the refusal prints the exact flag and value to pass: `--discard-unpushed <commit>@<worktree-id>` discards a worktree that has unpushed commits along with those commits, and `--force-remove-worktree <worktree-id>` deletes a worktree directory that git or the `WorktreeRemove` hook couldn't remove. `--discard-unpushed` requires Claude Code v2.1.260 or later, and `--force-remove-worktree` requires v2.1.268 or later. The conversation transcript stays on your local machine, available through `claude --resume` | `claude rm 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude self-hosted-runner` | Start a runner process that registers this machine or container with a [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments) and hosts Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure. Run `claude self-hosted-runner setup` for a guided operator walkthrough, `claude self-hosted-runner doctor` to [diagnose a deployed runner](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-deploy#troubleshooting), and `claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator` to spawn [on-demand runners](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-configuration#on-demand-runners). Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later | `claude self-hosted-runner setup` |\n| `claude setup-token` | Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription. See [Generate a long-lived token](/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token) | `claude setup-token` |\n| `claude stop <id>` | Stop a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell). Also accepts `claude kill` | `claude stop 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude ultrareview [target]` | Run [ultrareview](/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively) non-interactively. Prints findings to stdout and exits 0 on success or 1 on failure. Use `--json` for the raw payload and `--timeout <minutes>` to override the 45-minute default. Use `--post` on a `github.com` pull request target to post the finished findings to the PR as one plain comment from your GitHub account. `--no-post` is the default. `--post` and `--no-post` require Claude Code v2.1.227 or later. See [Post findings to the pull request](/docs/en/ultrareview#post-findings-to-the-pull-request) | `claude ultrareview 1234 --json` |\n\nIf you mistype a subcommand, Claude Code suggests the closest match and exits without starting a session. For example, `claude udpate` prints `Did you mean claude update?`.\n\n`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions daemon <subcommand>` runs the `daemon` subcommand, so the subcommand works when `claude` is aliased to include the flag. Only a leading `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` routes to `daemon` this way; with any other flag ahead of `daemon`, the subcommand doesn't run.\n\n## CLI flags\n\nCustomize Claude Code's behavior with these command-line flags. `claude --help` does not list every flag, so a flag's absence from `--help` does not mean it is unavailable.\n\n| Flag | Description | Example |\n| :- | :- | :- |\n| `--add-dir` | Add additional working directories for Claude to read and edit files. Grants file access; Claude Code [doesn't discover](/docs/en/permissions#additional-directories-grant-file-access-not-configuration) most `.claude/` configuration from these directories. Validates that each path exists as a directory. You can't add most [network paths](/docs/en/errors#working-directory-is-a-network-path), such as `\\\\server\\share`. To persist these directories across sessions, set [`permissions.additionalDirectories`](/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions-additionaldirectories) in settings | `claude --add-dir ../apps ../lib` |\n| `--advisor <model>` | Enable the server-side [advisor tool](/docs/en/advisor) for this session with a model alias, `fable`, `opus`, or `sonnet`, or a full model ID. Takes precedence over the `advisorModel` setting for the session. `fable` requires [Fable access](/docs/en/advisor#choose-an-advisor-model) | `claude --advisor opus` |\n| `--agent` | Specify an agent for the current session (overrides the `agent` setting) | `claude --agent my-custom-agent` |\n| `--agents` | Define custom subagents dynamically via JSON. Accepts the [fields listed for CLI-defined subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents#choose-the-subagent-scope). With `--print`, the value can instead be the path to a JSON file holding the object; the file form requires Claude Code v2.1.281 or later. Claude Code validates the value at startup and exits on an invalid one; see [`Invalid --agents configuration`](/docs/en/errors#invalid-agents-configuration) for the message and for the flags and environment variable that skip the validation. Validation requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later | `claude --agents '{\"reviewer\":{\"description\":\"Reviews code\",\"prompt\":\"You are a code reviewer\"}}'` |\n| `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` | Add `bypassPermissions` to the `Shift+Tab` mode cycle without starting in it. Lets you begin in a different mode like `plan` and switch to `bypassPermissions` later. See [permission modes](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) | `claude --permission-mode plan --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` |\n| `--allowedTools`, `--allowed-tools` | Tools that execute without prompting for permission, apart from reads from [network paths](/docs/en/permissions#network-paths). See [permission rule syntax](/docs/en/settings-reference#permission-rule-syntax) for pattern matching. To restrict which tools are available, use `--tools` instead. If you name one of the [task-tracking tools](/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability) here, Claude Code also opts the session in | `\"Bash(git log *)\" \"Bash(git diff *)\" \"Read\"` |\n| `--append-subagent-system-prompt` | Append custom text to the end of every [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents)'s system prompt, nested subagents included, apart from a [forked subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents#fork-the-current-conversation), which reuses the conversation's own prompt. Only applies in non-interactive mode with `-p`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.205 or later | `claude -p --append-subagent-system-prompt \"Cite file paths in every answer\" \"query\"` |\n| `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file` | Load text from a file and append it to [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) system prompts. An alternative to `--append-subagent-system-prompt` for text too long to pass on the command line. The two flags can't be combined. Only applies in non-interactive mode with `-p`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.261 or later | `claude -p --append-subagent-system-prompt-file ./subagent-rules.txt \"query\"` |\n| `--append-system-prompt` | Append custom text to the end of the default system prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt \"Always use TypeScript\"` |\n| `--append-system-prompt-file` | Load additional system prompt text from a file and append to the default prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt-file ./extra-rules.txt` |\n| `--autocompact <auto\\|tokens>` | Set the [auto-compact window](/docs/en/model-config#set-the-auto-compact-window) for this session without changing your saved settings. Accepts the same values as `/autocompact`; that section covers the value forms and what overrides the flag. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later | `claude --autocompact 500k` |\n| `--ax-screen-reader` | Render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Forces the classic renderer, so the [`tui`](/docs/en/settings-reference#tui) setting has no effect; attached [background sessions](/docs/en/agent-view) still render fullscreen. Takes precedence over [`CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER`](/docs/en/env-vars) and the [`axScreenReader`](/docs/en/settings-reference#axscreenreader) setting. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later | `claude --ax-screen-reader` |\n| `--bare` | Minimal mode: skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster. Skills in a directory you pass with `--add-dir` still load. Claude has access to Bash, file read, and file edit tools. Sets [`CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`](/docs/en/env-vars). See [bare mode](/docs/en/headless#start-faster-with-bare-mode) | `claude --bare -p \"query\"` |\n| `--betas` | Beta headers to include in API requests (API key users only) | `claude --betas interleaved-thinking` |\n| `--bg`, `--background` | Start the session as a [background agent](/docs/en/agent-view) and return immediately. Prints the session ID and management commands. Combine with `--exec` to run a shell command as a background job instead of a Claude session, or with `--agent` to run a specific subagent. Checks [workspace trust](/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust) for the directory before it starts. Can't be combined with `-p`/`--print`; see the [error reference](/docs/en/errors#command-line-errors) | `claude --bg \"investigate the flaky test\"` |\n| `--channels` | (Research preview) MCP servers whose [channel](/docs/en/channels) notifications Claude should listen for in this session. Space-separated list of `plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` entries. Requires Anthropic authentication through claude.ai or a Console API key | `claude --channels plugin:my-notifier@my-marketplace` |\n| `--chrome` | Enable [Chrome browser integration](/docs/en/chrome) for web automation and testing | `claude --chrome` |\n| `--cloud` | With a task description, create a new [cloud session](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). With a session ID (`session_...` or `cse_...`) or a claude.ai/code URL, queue a message into that existing session instead, with `-p`. See [send a follow-up message](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#send-follow-ups-from-the-cli). | `claude --cloud \"Fix the login bug\"` |\n| `--continue`, `-c` | Load the most recent conversation in the current directory, including a [background session that has finished](/docs/en/sessions#where-the-session-picker-looks); opening finished background sessions requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later. Skips sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK, and sessions whose first prompt was `/loop`. `claude -p --continue` includes `-p`, SDK, and `/loop` sessions. Includes sessions that added this directory with `/add-dir` | `claude --continue` |\n| `--dangerously-load-development-channels` | Enable [channels](/docs/en/channels-reference#test-during-the-research-preview) that are not on the approved allowlist, for local development. Accepts `plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` and `server:<name>` entries. Prompts for confirmation, so it takes effect in interactive sessions. With `-p`, Claude Code ignores the flag | `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:webhook` |\n| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Skip permission prompts. Four set its text, and with `--system-prompt-snapshot` you control whether a conversation keeps the text it started with. All five work in both interactive and non-interactive modes.\n\n| Flag | Behavior | Example |\n| :- | :- | :- |\n| `--system-prompt` | Replaces the entire default prompt | `claude --system-prompt \"You are a Python expert\"` |\n| `--system-prompt-file` | Replaces with file contents | `claude --system-prompt-file ./prompts/review.txt` |\n| `--append-system-prompt` | Appends to the default prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt \"Always use TypeScript\"` |\n| `--append-system-prompt-file` | Appends file contents to the default prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt-file ./style-rules.txt` |\n| `--system-prompt-snapshot` | With `off`, rebuilds the prompt on every request. With `on`, the default, reuses a recorded prompt where [recording applies](#system-prompt-flags-in-resumed-conversations) | `claude --append-system-prompt \"Draft rules\" --system-prompt-snapshot off` |\n\nYou can combine these flags. To replace the default prompt and still append your own text, pass `--append-system-prompt` or `--append-system-prompt-file` together with `--system-prompt` or `--system-prompt-file`. With Claude Code v2.1.283 or later, you can also pass a flag together with its own file form, such as `--append-system-prompt` with `--append-system-prompt-file`, and Claude Code uses both.\n\nFor example, run the following in your shell to append both a style guide from a file and one extra instruction:\n\n```bash theme={null}\nclaude -p --append-system-prompt-file ./style.md --append-system-prompt \"Always reply in French\" \"Summarize README.md\"\n```\n\nClaude receives the default system prompt followed by the contents of `style.md`, a blank line, and then `Always reply in French`. The file's contents come first even if you pass `--append-system-prompt` before `--append-system-prompt-file`.\n\nWhen the replacement text combines instructions that are the same on every run with context that changes per run, add a line containing only `__SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__` between the instructions and the context. Claude Code splits the prompt at the first such line and removes that line, so the part above it stays cached while the part below changes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.275 or later. [Cache the static part of a custom prompt](/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#cache-the-static-part-of-a-custom-prompt) lists the configurations where the split applies.\n\nChoose based on whether Claude Code's default identity still fits your task. Use an append flag when Claude should remain a coding assistant that also follows your extra rules: per-invocation instructions, output formatting, or domain context for a `-p` script. Appending preserves the default tool guidance, safety instructions, and coding conventions, so you only supply what differs. Use a replacement flag when the surface, identity, or permission model differs from Claude Code's, like a non-coding agent in a pipeline that no human watches. Replacing drops all of the default prompt, including tool guidance and safety instructions, so you take responsibility for whatever your task still needs.\n\nFor persistent personas you can switch between and share across a project, use [output styles](/docs/en/output-styles). For project conventions Claude should always follow, use [CLAUDE.md](/docs/en/memory). The [Agent SDK guide on system prompts](/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#decide-on-a-starting-point) covers the same decision in more depth.\n\n#### System prompt flags in resumed conversations\n\nBy default, Claude Code builds the system prompt once, on a conversation's first request, with the text from any system prompt flags applied, and records it in the session. Until the conversation is compacted, every later request uses that recorded prompt, including after you return to the conversation with `--resume` or `--continue`. If you pass different system prompt flag text, or none, on that later launch, it takes effect once the conversation is compacted or when you start a new conversation.\n\nOutside of [cloud sessions](/docs/en/cloud-environments), if you start Claude Code in [bare mode](/docs/en/headless#start-faster-with-bare-mode) by passing `--bare` or setting `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`, recording stays off unless you pass `--system-prompt-snapshot on`. Before v2.1.268, sessions that don't [fetch feature flags](/docs/en/env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching), including sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry, rebuilt the prompt on every request and `--system-prompt-snapshot` had no effect.\n\nTo rebuild the prompt on every request instead, for example while you iterate on its wording across `--continue` runs, pass `--system-prompt-snapshot off`. Before v2.1.265, passing any of the system prompt flags also turned recording off unless you passed `--system-prompt-snapshot on`.\n\n## See also\n\n* [Chrome extension](/docs/en/chrome) - Browser automation and web testing\n* [Interactive mode](/docs/en/interactive-mode) - Shortcuts, input modes, and interactive features\n* [Quickstart guide](/docs/en/quickstart) - Getting started with Claude Code\n* [Common workflows](/docs/en/common-workflows) - Advanced workflows and patterns\n* [Settings](/docs/en/settings) - Configuration options\n* [Agent SDK documentation](/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) - Programmatic usage and integrations\n"

Requires `--config` pointing at a [`gateway.yaml`](/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config). | `claude gateway --config gateway.yaml` |\n| `claude install [version]` | Install or reinstall the native binary. Accepts a version like `2.1.118`, or `stable` or `latest`. See [Install a specific version](/docs/en/setup#install-a-specific-version) | `claude install stable` |\n| `claude auth login` | Sign in to your Anthropic account. Use `--email` to pre-fill your email address, `--sso` to force SSO authentication, and `--console` to sign in with Anthropic Console for API usage billing instead of a Claude subscription | `claude auth login --console` |\n| `claude auth logout` | Log out from your Anthropic account | `claude auth logout` |\n| `claude auth status` | Show authentication status as JSON. Use `--text` for human-readable output. Exits with code 0 if logged in, 1 if not. The JSON includes a `configDirectory` field naming the [configuration directory](/docs/en/claude-directory) the CLI uses. The field requires Claude Code v2.1.268 or later. The JSON's `authMethod` field is one of `none`, `claude.ai`, `oauth_token`, `api_key`, `api_key_helper`, or `third_party` | `claude auth status` |\n| `claude agents` | Open [agent view](/docs/en/agent-view) to monitor and dispatch parallel background sessions. Use `--cwd <path>` to show only sessions started under that directory, or `--json` to print active sessions as a JSON array for scripting (`--json --all` also includes completed background sessions). Pass `--permission-mode`, `--model`, `--effort`, or `--agent` to set [defaults for dispatched sessions](/docs/en/agent-view#permission-mode-model-and-effort). Accepts `--settings`, `--add-dir`, `--plugin-dir`, and `--mcp-config` like the top-level `claude` command. Opening agent view requires an interactive terminal | `claude agents --json` |\n| `claude attach <id\\|name>` | Attach to a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell) in this terminal. Passing part of a running session's name in place of the ID requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later | `claude attach 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude auto-mode defaults` | Print the built-in [auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) classifier rules as JSON. Use `claude auto-mode config` to see your effective config with settings applied. `--label <prefix>` prints only the rules whose label starts with that prefix, matched case-insensitively. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later | `claude auto-mode defaults --label 'Git Destructive'` |\n| `claude auto-mode reset` | Restore the default [auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode) configuration by removing the `autoMode` section from your user settings file. Prompts for confirmation before writing; pass `-y`/`--yes` to skip the prompt. Rules from [managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings) or the `--settings` flag still apply. Requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later. See [Inspect the defaults and your effective config](/docs/en/auto-mode-config#inspect-the-defaults-and-your-effective-config) | `claude auto-mode reset --yes` |\n| `claude daemon logs` | Follow the background-session [supervisor's](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) log file, `~/.claude/daemon.log`, printing new lines as they arrive until you press `Ctrl+C` | `claude daemon logs` |\n| `claude daemon run` | Run the background-session [supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) in the foreground of this terminal, printing its log | `claude daemon run` |\n| `claude daemon status` | Print the background-session [supervisor's](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) state, version, socket directory, and worker count for diagnostics. Exits 1 if the supervisor isn't running | `claude daemon status` |\n| `claude daemon stop --any` | Stop the background-session [supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#the-supervisor-process) and the sessions it hosts. Pass `--keep-workers` to leave background sessions running for the next supervisor to reconnect to. `--any` confirms stopping an on-demand supervisor, which is the default. Use this to recover from an [unresponsive supervisor](/docs/en/agent-view#agent-view-says-the-background-service-did-not-respond) | `claude daemon stop --any --keep-workers` |\n| `claude doctor` | Print read-only installation and settings diagnostics from the terminal without starting a session, including install health, settings-file validation errors, and Remote Control eligibility. For the in-session setup checkup that can also apply fixes, run [`/doctor`](/docs/en/commands#all-commands) | `claude doctor` |\n| `claude import [source]` | Start an interactive session that runs [`/import`](/docs/en/commands#all-commands) to bring configuration from other coding agents into Claude Code. Accepts the same `--dry-run` and `--yes` options as the command. Not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or Claude Platform on AWS. Also unavailable when you turn off [feature-flag fetching](/docs/en/env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching). Requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later | `claude import codex --dry-run` |\n| `claude logs <id\\|name>` | Print recent output from a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell). Passing part of a session's name in place of the ID requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later | `claude logs 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude mcp` | Configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers | See the [Claude Code MCP documentation](/docs/en/mcp). |\n| `claude mcp login <name>` | Run a configured MCP server's OAuth flow without opening the interactive `/mcp` panel. Works for HTTP, SSE, and claude.ai connector servers. Add `--no-browser` over SSH to print the authorization URL instead of opening a browser. For an HTTP or SSE server, paste the redirect URL back at the prompt. For a claude.ai connector, see [Authorize a connector again from your shell](/docs/en/remote-control#authorize-a-connector-again-from-your-shell). See [Authenticate from the command line](/docs/en/mcp#authenticate-from-the-command-line) | `claude mcp login sentry` |\n| `claude mcp logout <name>` | Clear stored OAuth credentials for an MCP server | `claude mcp logout sentry` |\n| `claude plugin` | Manage Claude Code [plugins](/docs/en/plugins/overview). Alias: `claude plugins`. See [plugin reference](/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#claude-plugin-commands) for subcommands | `claude plugin install code-review@claude-plugins-official` |\n| `claude purge [path]` | Delete all local Claude Code state for a project: transcripts, task lists, debug logs, file-edit history, prompt history lines, and the project's entry in `~/.claude.json`. Omit `[path]` to pick from an interactive list. Flags: `--dry-run` to preview, `-y`/`--yes` to skip confirmation, `-i`/`--interactive` to confirm each item, `--all` for every project. See [Clear local data](/docs/en/claude-directory#clear-local-data) | `claude purge ~/work/repo --dry-run` |\n| `claude remote-control` | Start a [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) server to control Claude Code from Claude.ai or the Claude app. Runs in server mode (no local interactive session). See [Server mode flags](/docs/en/remote-control#start-a-remote-control-session). After you stop the server, you can bring back the sessions it was serving. See [Resume sessions after stopping the server](/docs/en/remote-control#resume-sessions-after-stopping-the-server) | `claude remote-control --name \"My Project\"` |\n| `claude respawn <id>` | Restart a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell), running or stopped, with its conversation intact. Use `--all` to restart every running session, e.g. to pick up an updated Claude Code binary | `claude respawn 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude rm <id>` | Remove a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell) from the list. When the removal is [refused over the session's worktree](/docs/en/agent-view#what-deleting-a-session-removes) and a second `claude rm` can resolve it, the refusal prints the exact flag and value to pass: `--discard-unpushed <commit>@<worktree-id>` discards a worktree that has unpushed commits along with those commits, and `--force-remove-worktree <worktree-id>` deletes a worktree directory that git or the `WorktreeRemove` hook couldn't remove. `--discard-unpushed` requires Claude Code v2.1.260 or later, and `--force-remove-worktree` requires v2.1.268 or later. The conversation transcript stays on your local machine, available through `claude --resume` | `claude rm 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude self-hosted-runner` | Start a runner process that registers this machine or container with a [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments) and hosts Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure. Run `claude self-hosted-runner setup` for a guided operator walkthrough, `claude self-hosted-runner doctor` to [diagnose a deployed runner](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-deploy#troubleshooting), and `claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator` to spawn [on-demand runners](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-configuration#on-demand-runners). Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later | `claude self-hosted-runner setup` |\n| `claude setup-token` | Generate a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts. Prints the token to the terminal without saving it. Requires a Claude subscription. See [Generate a long-lived token](/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token) | `claude setup-token` |\n| `claude stop <id>` | Stop a [background session](/docs/en/agent-view#manage-sessions-from-the-shell). Also accepts `claude kill` | `claude stop 7c5dcf5d` |\n| `claude ultrareview [target]` | Run [ultrareview](/docs/en/ultrareview#run-ultrareview-non-interactively) non-interactively. Prints findings to stdout and exits 0 on success or 1 on failure. Use `--json` for the raw payload and `--timeout <minutes>` to override the 45-minute default. Use `--post` on a `github.com` pull request target to post the finished findings to the PR as one plain comment from your GitHub account. `--no-post` is the default. `--post` and `--no-post` require Claude Code v2.1.227 or later. See [Post findings to the pull request](/docs/en/ultrareview#post-findings-to-the-pull-request) | `claude ultrareview 1234 --json` |\n\nIf you mistype a subcommand, Claude Code suggests the closest match and exits without starting a session. For example, `claude udpate` prints `Did you mean claude update?`.\n\n`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions daemon <subcommand>` runs the `daemon` subcommand, so the subcommand works when `claude` is aliased to include the flag. Only a leading `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` routes to `daemon` this way; with any other flag ahead of `daemon`, the subcommand doesn't run.\n\n## CLI flags\n\nCustomize Claude Code's behavior with these command-line flags. `claude --help` does not list every flag, so a flag's absence from `--help` does not mean it is unavailable.\n\n| Flag | Description | Example |\n| :- | :- | :- |\n| `--add-dir` | Add additional working directories for Claude to read and edit files. Grants file access; Claude Code [doesn't discover](/docs/en/permissions#additional-directories-grant-file-access-not-configuration) most `.claude/` configuration from these directories. Validates that each path exists as a directory. You can't add most [network paths](/docs/en/errors#working-directory-is-a-network-path), such as `\\\\server\\share`. To persist these directories across sessions, set [`permissions.additionalDirectories`](/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions-additionaldirectories) in settings | `claude --add-dir ../apps ../lib` |\n| `--advisor <model>` | Enable the server-side [advisor tool](/docs/en/advisor) for this session with a model alias, `fable`, `opus`, or `sonnet`, or a full model ID. Takes precedence over the `advisorModel` setting for the session. `fable` requires [Fable access](/docs/en/advisor#choose-an-advisor-model) | `claude --advisor opus` |\n| `--agent` | Specify an agent for the current session (overrides the `agent` setting) | `claude --agent my-custom-agent` |\n| `--agents` | Define custom subagents dynamically via JSON. Accepts the [fields listed for CLI-defined subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents#choose-the-subagent-scope). With `--print`, the value can instead be the path to a JSON file holding the object; the file form requires Claude Code v2.1.281 or later. Claude Code validates the value at startup and exits on an invalid one; see [`Invalid --agents configuration`](/docs/en/errors#invalid-agents-configuration) for the message and for the flags and environment variable that skip the validation. Validation requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later | `claude --agents '{\"reviewer\":{\"description\":\"Reviews code\",\"prompt\":\"You are a code reviewer\"}}'` |\n| `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` | Add `bypassPermissions` to the `Shift+Tab` mode cycle without starting in it. Lets you begin in a different mode like `plan` and switch to `bypassPermissions` later. See [permission modes](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) | `claude --permission-mode plan --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` |\n| `--allowedTools`, `--allowed-tools` | Tools that execute without prompting for permission, apart from reads from [network paths](/docs/en/permissions#network-paths). See [permission rule syntax](/docs/en/settings-reference#permission-rule-syntax) for pattern matching. To restrict which tools are available, use `--tools` instead. If you name one of the [task-tracking tools](/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability) here, Claude Code also opts the session in | `\"Bash(git log *)\" \"Bash(git diff *)\" \"Read\"` |\n| `--append-subagent-system-prompt` | Append custom text to the end of every [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents)'s system prompt, nested subagents included, apart from a [forked subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents#fork-the-current-conversation), which reuses the conversation's own prompt. Only applies in non-interactive mode with `-p`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.205 or later | `claude -p --append-subagent-system-prompt \"Cite file paths in every answer\" \"query\"` |\n| `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file` | Load text from a file and append it to [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) system prompts. An alternative to `--append-subagent-system-prompt` for text too long to pass on the command line. The two flags can't be combined. Only applies in non-interactive mode with `-p`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.261 or later | `claude -p --append-subagent-system-prompt-file ./subagent-rules.txt \"query\"` |\n| `--append-system-prompt` | Append custom text to the end of the default system prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt \"Always use TypeScript\"` |\n| `--append-system-prompt-file` | Load additional system prompt text from a file and append to the default prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt-file ./extra-rules.txt` |\n| `--autocompact <auto\\|tokens>` | Set the [auto-compact window](/docs/en/model-config#set-the-auto-compact-window) for this session without changing your saved settings. Accepts the same values as `/autocompact`; that section covers the value forms and what overrides the flag. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later | `claude --autocompact 500k` |\n| `--ax-screen-reader` | Render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Forces the classic renderer, so the [`tui`](/docs/en/settings-reference#tui) setting has no effect; attached [background sessions](/docs/en/agent-view) still render fullscreen. Takes precedence over [`CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER`](/docs/en/env-vars) and the [`axScreenReader`](/docs/en/settings-reference#axscreenreader) setting. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later | `claude --ax-screen-reader` |\n| `--bare` | Minimal mode: skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster. Skills in a directory you pass with `--add-dir` still load. Claude has access to Bash, file read, and file edit tools. Sets [`CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`](/docs/en/env-vars). See [bare mode](/docs/en/headless#start-faster-with-bare-mode) | `claude --bare -p \"query\"` |\n| `--betas` | Beta headers to include in API requests (API key users only) | `claude --betas interleaved-thinking` |\n| `--bg`, `--background` | Start the session as a [background agent](/docs/en/agent-view) and return immediately. Prints the session ID and management commands. Combine with `--exec` to run a shell command as a background job instead of a Claude session, or with `--agent` to run a specific subagent. Checks [workspace trust](/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust) for the directory before it starts. Can't be combined with `-p`/`--print`; see the [error reference](/docs/en/errors#command-line-errors) | `claude --bg \"investigate the flaky test\"` |\n| `--channels` | (Research preview) MCP servers whose [channel](/docs/en/channels) notifications Claude should listen for in this session. Space-separated list of `plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` entries. Requires Anthropic authentication through claude.ai or a Console API key | `claude --channels plugin:my-notifier@my-marketplace` |\n| `--chrome` | Enable [Chrome browser integration](/docs/en/chrome) for web automation and testing | `claude --chrome` |\n| `--cloud` | With a task description, create a new [cloud session](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). With a session ID (`session_...` or `cse_...`) or a claude.ai/code URL, queue a message into that existing session instead, with `-p`. See [send a follow-up message](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#send-follow-ups-from-the-cli). | `claude --cloud \"Fix the login bug\"` |\n| `--continue`, `-c` | Load the most recent conversation in the current directory, including a [background session that has finished](/docs/en/sessions#where-the-session-picker-looks); opening finished background sessions requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later. Skips sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK, and sessions whose first prompt was `/loop`. `claude -p --continue` includes `-p`, SDK, and `/loop` sessions. Includes sessions that added this directory with `/add-dir` | `claude --continue` |\n| `--dangerously-load-development-channels` | Enable [channels](/docs/en/channels-reference#test-during-the-research-preview) that are not on the approved allowlist, for local development. Accepts `plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` and `server:<name>` entries. Prompts for confirmation, so it takes effect in interactive sessions. With `-p`, Claude Code ignores the flag | `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:webhook` |\n| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Skip permission prompts. Equivalent to `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. See [permission modes](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) for what this does and does not skip. For sessions started with `--bg`, the mode [persists when the supervisor restarts the session](/docs/en/agent-view#permission-mode-model-and-effort) | `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` |\n| `--debug` | Enable debug mode with optional category filtering, such as `--debug='mcp,startup'` or `--debug='!mcp'`. The filter binds only in the `=` form; a space-separated filter enables debug mode without filtering | `claude --debug='mcp,startup'` |\n| `--debug-file <path>` | Write debug logs to a specific file path. Implicitly enables debug mode. Takes precedence over `CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOGS_DIR` | `claude --debug-file /tmp/claude-debug.log` |\n| `--desktop` | Open the [Claude Desktop app](/docs/en/desktop) on the current directory and exit without starting a session in the terminal. Add `--continue`, or `--resume` with a session ID, to [open that session in Desktop](/docs/en/desktop#coming-from-the-cli) instead. `--resume` here takes only a session ID, not a name or transcript path. Takes no prompt and no other flags except `--verbose` and the `--debug` flags, since the app starts the session itself. Available on macOS and x64 Windows when you're signed in with a Claude subscription. Requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later | `claude --desktop` |\n| `--disable-slash-commands` | Disable all skills and commands for this session | `claude --disable-slash-commands` |\n| `--disallowedTools`, `--disallowed-tools` | Deny rules. A bare tool name removes the matching tools from Claude's context: `\"Edit\"` removes Edit, `\"*\"` removes every tool, and `\"mcp__*\"` removes every MCP tool. A scoped rule such as `Bash(rm *)` leaves the tool available and denies only calls that match [as written](/docs/en/permissions#bash-rule-limits). A rule naming [`EndConversation`](/docs/en/tools-reference#endconversation-tool-behavior) can't remove it while any other tool remains | `\"Bash(git log *)\" \"Bash(git diff *)\" \"Edit\"` |\n| `--effort` | Set the [effort level](/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level) for the current session. Options: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or `ultracode`. Available levels depend on the model. `ultracode` requests `xhigh` effort with [ultracode](/docs/en/workflows#let-claude-decide-with-ultracode) turned on, and requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. Overrides the [`modelSettings`](/docs/en/settings-reference#modelsettings) and [`effortLevel`](/docs/en/settings-reference#effortlevel) settings for this session and does not persist | `claude --effort high` |\n| `--enable-auto-mode` | Removed in v2.1.111. Auto mode is now in the `Shift+Tab` cycle by default; use `--permission-mode auto` to start in it | `claude --permission-mode auto` |\n| `--environment <environment-id>` | Create a new cloud session that runs on the [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments) with the given ID. Environment IDs start with `ccpool_`. See [`--environment` dispatch behavior](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-testing#environment-dispatch-behavior) for dispatch behavior and the flag combinations it rejects. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later | `claude -p \"Fix the login bug\" --environment ccpool_abc123` |\n| `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` | Move per-user context, such as the auto memory location, out of the system prompt and into the first user message. Improves prompt-cache reuse across different users and machines running the same task. Only applies with the default system prompt; ignored when `--system-prompt` or `--system-prompt-file` is set. Use with `-p` for scripted, multi-user workloads | `claude -p --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections \"query\"` |\n| `--exec` | Run a shell command as a PTY-backed background job instead of starting a Claude session. Use with `--bg` to launch from the shell | `claude --bg --exec 'pytest -x'` |\n| `--fallback-model` | Enable automatic fallback to the specified model(s) when the primary model is overloaded or not available, for example a retired model. Accepts a comma-separated list tried in order. See [Fallback model chains](/docs/en/model-config#fallback-model-chains). To persist a chain across sessions, use the [`fallbackModel` setting](/docs/en/settings-reference#fallbackmodel), which this flag overrides | `claude --fallback-model sonnet,haiku` |\n| `--fork-session` | When resuming, create a new session ID instead of reusing the original (use with `--resume` or `--continue`) | `claude --resume abc123 --fork-session` |\n| `--forward-subagent-text` | Emit [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) text and thinking blocks in the output stream as `assistant` and `user` messages with `parent_tool_use_id` set, so you can reconstruct each subagent's transcript. Without this flag, Claude Code omits the text and thinking blocks of a subagent that runs in the [foreground](/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background). Requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`. For nested subagents, forked skills, and the version each needs, see [Follow subagent messages](/docs/en/headless#follow-subagent-messages). The [`CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT`](/docs/en/env-vars) environment variable enables the same behavior. Branching from a GitLab merge request requires Claude Code v2.1.233 or later | `claude -w feature-auth` |\n\n### System prompt flags\n\nClaude Code provides five flags for customizing the system prompt. Four set its text, and with `--system-prompt-snapshot` you control whether a conversation keeps the text it started with. All five work in both interactive and non-interactive modes.\n\n| Flag | Behavior | Example |\n| :- | :- | :- |\n| `--system-prompt` | Replaces the entire default prompt | `claude --system-prompt \"You are a Python expert\"` |\n| `--system-prompt-file` | Replaces with file contents | `claude --system-prompt-file ./prompts/review.txt` |\n| `--append-system-prompt` | Appends to the default prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt \"Always use TypeScript\"` |\n| `--append-system-prompt-file` | Appends file contents to the default prompt | `claude --append-system-prompt-file ./style-rules.txt` |\n| `--system-prompt-snapshot` | With `off`, rebuilds the prompt on every request. With `on`, the default, reuses a recorded prompt where [recording applies](#system-prompt-flags-in-resumed-conversations) | `claude --append-system-prompt \"Draft rules\" --system-prompt-snapshot off` |\n\nYou can combine these flags. To replace the default prompt and still append your own text, pass `--append-system-prompt` or `--append-system-prompt-file` together with `--system-prompt` or `--system-prompt-file`. With Claude Code v2.1.283 or later, you can also pass a flag together with its own file form, such as `--append-system-prompt` with `--append-system-prompt-file`, and Claude Code uses both.\n\nFor example, run the following in your shell to append both a style guide from a file and one extra instruction:\n\n```bash theme={null}\nclaude -p --append-system-prompt-file ./style.md --append-system-prompt \"Always reply in French\" \"Summarize README.md\"\n```\n\nClaude receives the default system prompt followed by the contents of `style.md`, a blank line, and then `Always reply in French`. The file's contents come first even if you pass `--append-system-prompt` before `--append-system-prompt-file`.\n\nWhen the replacement text combines instructions that are the same on every run with context that changes per run, add a line containing only `__SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__` between the instructions and the context. Claude Code splits the prompt at the first such line and removes that line, so the part above it stays cached while the part below changes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.275 or later. [Cache the static part of a custom prompt](/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#cache-the-static-part-of-a-custom-prompt) lists the configurations where the split applies.\n\nChoose based on whether Claude Code's default identity still fits your task. Use an append flag when Claude should remain a coding assistant that also follows your extra rules: per-invocation instructions, output formatting, or domain context for a `-p` script. Appending preserves the default tool guidance, safety instructions, and coding conventions, so you only supply what differs. Use a replacement flag when the surface, identity, or permission model differs from Claude Code's, like a non-coding agent in a pipeline that no human watches. Replacing drops all of the default prompt, including tool guidance and safety instructions, so you take responsibility for whatever your task still needs.\n\nFor persistent personas you can switch between and share across a project, use [output styles](/docs/en/output-styles). For project conventions Claude should always follow, use [CLAUDE.md](/docs/en/memory). The [Agent SDK guide on system prompts](/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts#decide-on-a-starting-point) covers the same decision in more depth.\n\n#### System prompt flags in resumed conversations\n\nBy default, Claude Code builds the system prompt once, on a conversation's first request, with the text from any system prompt flags applied, and records it in the session. Until the conversation is compacted, every later request uses that recorded prompt, including after you return to the conversation with `--resume` or `--continue`. If you pass different system prompt flag text, or none, on that later launch, it takes effect once the conversation is compacted or when you start a new conversation.\n\nOutside of [cloud sessions](/docs/en/cloud-environments), if you start Claude Code in [bare mode](/docs/en/headless#start-faster-with-bare-mode) by passing `--bare` or setting `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1`, recording stays off unless you pass `--system-prompt-snapshot on`. Before v2.1.268, sessions that don't [fetch feature flags](/docs/en/env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching), including sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry, rebuilt the prompt on every request and `--system-prompt-snapshot` had no effect.\n\nTo rebuild the prompt on every request instead, for example while you iterate on its wording across `--continue` runs, pass `--system-prompt-snapshot off`. Before v2.1.265, passing any of the system prompt flags also turned recording off unless you passed `--system-prompt-snapshot on`.\n\n## See also\n\n* [Chrome extension](/docs/en/chrome) - Browser automation and web testing\n* [Interactive mode](/docs/en/interactive-mode) - Shortcuts, input modes, and interactive features\n* [Quickstart guide](/docs/en/quickstart) - Getting started with Claude Code\n* [Common workflows](/docs/en/common-workflows) - Advanced workflows and patterns\n* [Settings](/docs/en/settings) - Configuration options\n* [Agent SDK documentation](/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) - Programmatic usage and integrations\n",

[2026-10-22T14:36:20.443Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Issue #57: Can upcomputer benefit from agent-commander?\n\nThis case study compares [krl-gr/upcomputer](https://github.com/krl-gr/upcomputer) (\"The self-orchestrating control plane for coding agents\", TypeScript, MIT) and [link-assistant/hive-mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind) with agent-commander. It adds every general agent-control feature that either project needs and agent-commander lacked, in both the JavaScript and Rust bindings. It also makes the library replaceable piece by piece, so a consumer can swap a failing or missing part without waiting for a release.\n\nIssue: [agent-commander #57](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/issues/57). Implementation: [PR #58](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/58). The previous case study is [issue #55](../issue-55/README.md).\n\n## Scope and method\n\nThe research date is 2026-10-22 UTC.\n\n- **upcomputer.** Repository metadata is in [upcomputer-repo.json](data/upcomputer-repo.json) (88 stars, MIT, TypeScript). The provider drivers are mapped in [upcomputer-provider-launch-map.md](data/upcomputer-provider-launch-map.md), using 7 dimensions: transport, lifecycle, models, permissions, inputs, outputs, install and health. The cross-cutting services are mapped in [upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md](data/upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md): limits, tokens, processes, scheduling, checkpoints, logs, MCP, text generation, worktrees, errors and remote operation.\n- **Hive Mind.** v2.39.5 (`5a7cb68`), the issue #55 pin. The versions are agent 0.26.15, claude 2.1.308, codex 0.163.0, gemini 0.64.0, opencode 1.19.3 and qwen 0.25.2. Each new flag was checked against this help text before it was used.\n- **agent-commander.** The baseline is JavaScript 0.11.1 / Rust 0.3.2 on `main`. The release fragments make this a minor release.\n\nBoth upstream repositories were treated as untrusted data. They were read and grepped only, never installed or run.\n\nThe issue has no comments, and PR #58 had no comments or reviews when work started.\n\nThe issue sets two rules for what belongs in agent-commander:\n\n- **General.** Launching, steering and reading native agent CLIs. Any consumer of the library needs this. It was implemented in both languages, behind options that are off by default.\n- **Project-specific.** Scheduling, checkpoints, worktrees, GUI, pairing and similar product features. These stay in the consumer. The new tool overrides make sure a consumer can still rebuild any general part that is missing or broken.\n\n## Every issue requirement and its execution plan\n\n| Requirement from the issue                                                         | Solution and plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Delivered evidence                                                                                                                                       |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| R1.
