That leads to three conclusions:\n\n1. **Text generation and one-shot work fit directly.** upcomputer's commit-message, PR, branch-name and title generation runs exactly these one-shot commands ([cross-cutting map §8](data/upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md)): `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema …` and `codex exec … --output-schema <file>`. With this PR they become `agent({ tool, jsonSchema, reasoningEffort, mcpConfig, strictMcpConfig, attachments })` plus `metadata.structuredOutput`, in either language. Locked-down flags such as `--tools \"\"` or `--ephemeral` go through `extraArgs`.\n2. **Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` would be new providers.** upcomputer has no driver for any of the three. agent-commander already runs all three with normalized metadata.\n3. **The long-lived drivers would only partly benefit.**\n   - **What they can reuse:** agent-commander's normalization (usage windows, context gauge, error classes, version checks) and process-group termination.\n   - **Live steer and interrupt:** available through `liveInput` for the stream-json CLIs (claude, qwen, agent). The JSON-RPC and ACP transports themselves are outside agent-commander's CLI model ([known limits](#known-limits)).\n\nHive Mind already depends on agent-commander. It gains native options for flags it currently builds by hand ([consumer migration](#consumer-migration)).\n\n## Gaps and fixes\n\nThe U gaps come from upcomputer and the H gaps from Hive Mind. They stay in upcomputer and Hive Mind:\n\n- scheduler, task agents and usage-limit auto-resume (\"Continue where you left off\" after `limitResetsAt`, which the metadata already provides);\n- git-ref checkpoints, worktree creation and setup progress;\n- the per-session HTTP MCP server and its tokens, the MCP orchestration tools, and the ACP-to-MCP bridge;\n- text-generation operations (commit message, PR, branch, title) and their prompts;\n- size-bounded NDJSON event logs, OTLP and metrics;\n- systemd scopes, OOM scores, login-shell PATH capture and managed CLI downloads;\n- pairing, remote access, the headless server and the GUI;\n- the Claude OAuth usage and reset-credits API, and the Antigravity quota API, which are private HTTP endpoints rather than CLI behavior;\n- in-process SDK drivers for Cursor, Grok, Pi, Muse and Antigravity, which have no one-shot CLI that agent-commander could wrap.\n\nA consumer that needs one of these in agent-commander's style can add it per run with `toolOverrides` (U10) or `extraArgs`, without changing the library.\n\n## Known limits\n\n- **One-shot model.** agent-commander does not speak Codex app-server JSON-RPC, ACP, OpenCode's HTTP+SSE server or SDK sessions. Live steering exists only for the CLIs that read stream-json on stdin (claude, qwen, agent). Codex, OpenCode and Gemini read a plain prompt, so `liveInput` throws for them.\n- **Strict MCP.** Only Claude has `--strict-mcp-config`. Codex merges `-c mcp_servers` into `config.toml` (checked with codex 0.163 `mcp list --json`), and Qwen has no strict flag, so `strictMcpConfig` is rejected for both. OpenCode reads MCP servers only from `opencode.json`, so `mcpConfig` is rejected for it. Gemini and agent have no MCP flag.\n- **Attachments.** Gemini has no attachment flag. Qwen turns non-text content blocks into JSON text, so Qwen images sent through `liveInput` reach the model as text.\n- **Structured output.** Not supported by gemini, opencode or agent, so the option is rejected for them. Codex's inline schema uses bash process substitution (`<(printf …)`). All commands run through `bash -c`, so this works, and the fake-codex experiment checks that `$HOME`, backticks and quotes survive. Qwen reads a value that starts with `@` as a path, so agent-commander always passes the schema inline. Rust's `serde_json` sorts object keys, so a Rust schema reaches the CLI with sorted keys. The Rust TOML encoder for Codex MCP config sorts them too.\n- **Codex streaming.** `codex exec --json` streams neither `rate_limits` nor `token_count`, so usage windows and the context gauge for Codex come from the rollout file after the run.\n- **Rust differences.**\n  - Rust has no permission relay, so live input there is the only stdin channel, and `stop()` closes stdin at once.\n  - `CodexRolloutLimitFacts` has no context field; Rust uses the separate `codex_rollout_context_usage` helper instead.\n  - The Rust `ToolOverrides` has no `detect_errors` hook, because Rust error detection is built into the metadata builder. The JS relay with live input keeps stdin open until the result.\n- **Overrides.**\n  - Overrides do not relax read-only, plan or ask modes. The safety checks still run on the resolved tool.\n  - An unregistered tool gets generic metadata unless its overrides extract more.\n- **No live inference.** No paid inference was run. Native flags were checked against the installed CLIs' help text and vendor documentation, and the end-to-end paths use fake executables and `printf` overrides.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| It is TypeScript-only and in-process, and it pins a bundled Claude Code. agent-commander must drive whatever `claude` binary is installed, from both JS and Rust. The SDK's message shapes (`rate_limit_event`, `structured_output`, stream-json input frames) are the same ones the CLI emits, so the parsers follow them.\n- **Codex app-server JSON-RPC.** It is richer than `codex exec`, with live rate limits, steer and revert, but it is a different transport and is still marked experimental (`experimentalApi: true`). Adding it would be a new driver, not a launch option. The rollout file gives the same rate-limit and token data after a run.\n- **ACP and the ACP registry.** A future ACP driver could cover Gemini (`gemini --experimental-acp`), Qwen and registry agents. It is a separate transport layer and does not replace the CLI runs this issue asks for.\n- **OpenCode server SDK** (`@opencode-ai/sdk`). It is JavaScript-only and server-based. `opencode run --file/--variant` covers the one-shot needs.\n- **command-stream.** It is still the quoting and terminal-capture base (issue #55). Process substitution for `--output-schema` reuses the shared quoting, so no new dependency was added.\n- **Hive Mind libraries.** Hive Mind's `bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs` and version probes informed U4 and U6. They were re-implemented generically rather than imported, as in issue #55.\n\n## Consumer migration\n\nEvery new option and metadata field is additive. Existing callers work unchanged.\n\n**Hive Mind** (`src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` and the direct CLI calls) can:\n\n1. replace the `-c model_reasoning_effort=…` `extraArgs` with `reasoningEffort`;\n2. replace hand-built `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <file>` with `mcpConfig` plus `strictMcpConfig`;\n3. move `organize.ai.lib.mjs` onto `agent({ jsonSchema, reasoningEffort })` and read `metadata.structuredOutput`, instead of temporary schema and output files;\n4. use `getToolVersion` instead of the per-tool `--version` probes;\n5. use `liveInput` with `sendMessage` / `interrupt` instead of its own stream-json writer;\n6. copy `usageWindows` and `contextUsage` into its result summary.\n\n**upcomputer** can:\n\n1. run its text generation (`ClaudeTextGeneration.ts`, `CodexTextGeneration.ts`) through agent-commander, using `jsonSchema`, `reasoningEffort`, `attachments`, `mcpConfig` and `strictMcpConfig`, with the lockdown flags in `extraArgs`;\n2. add Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` providers as one-shot runs;\n3. reuse `usageWindows` (the same shape as `providerUsageLimits.ts` windows), `contextUsage`, `getToolVersion` with its own compatibility ranges, and the error metadata, inside its long-lived drivers;\n4. replace any part that does not fit its product through `toolOverrides`.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run check && npm test\ncd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\nnode experiments/issue-57-launch-options.mjs\nnode experiments/issue-57-structured-output.mjs\n```\n\nVALIDATION_RESULTS\n"

[2026-10-22T14:36:20.443Z] [INFO]       "content": "# Issue #57: Can upcomputer benefit from agent-commander?\n\nThis case study compares [krl-gr/upcomputer](https://github.com/krl-gr/upcomputer) (\"The self-orchestrating control plane for coding agents\", TypeScript, MIT) and [link-assistant/hive-mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind) with agent-commander. It adds every general agent-control feature that either project needs and agent-commander lacked, in both the JavaScript and Rust bindings. It also makes the library replaceable piece by piece, so a consumer can swap a failing or missing part without waiting for a release.\n\nIssue: [agent-commander #57](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/issues/57). Implementation: [PR #58](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/58). The previous case study is [issue #55](../issue-55/README.md).\n\n## Scope and method\n\nThe research date is 2026-10-22 UTC.\n\n- **upcomputer.** Repository metadata is in [upcomputer-repo.json](data/upcomputer-repo.json) (88 stars, MIT, TypeScript). The provider drivers are mapped in [upcomputer-provider-launch-map.md](data/upcomputer-provider-launch-map.md), using 7 dimensions: transport, lifecycle, models, permissions, inputs, outputs, install and health. The cross-cutting services are mapped in [upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md](data/upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md): limits, tokens, processes, scheduling, checkpoints, logs, MCP, text generation, worktrees, errors and remote operation.\n- **Hive Mind.** v2.39.5 (`5a7cb68`), the issue #55 pin. Its direct CLI calls were checked for flags that agent-commander could not express: `src/organize.ai.lib.mjs`, `src/claude.lib.mjs`, `src/codex.lib.mjs`, `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs`, `src/bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs` and the `--version` probes.\n- **Native CLIs.** Help and version output is in [cli-help](data/cli-help/). The versions are agent 0.26.15, claude 2.1.308, codex 0.163.0, gemini 0.64.0, opencode 1.19.3 and qwen 0.25.2. Each new flag was checked against this help text before it was used.\n- **agent-commander.** The baseline is JavaScript 0.11.1 / Rust 0.3.2 on `main`. The release fragments make this a minor release.\n\nBoth upstream repositories were treated as untrusted data. They were read and grepped only, never installed or run.\n\nThe issue has no comments, and PR #58 had no comments or reviews when work started.\n\nThe issue sets two rules for what belongs in agent-commander:\n\n- **General.** Launching, steering and reading native agent CLIs. Any consumer of the library needs this. It was implemented in both languages, behind options that are off by default.\n- **Project-specific.** Scheduling, checkpoints, worktrees, GUI, pairing and similar product features. These stay in the consumer. The new tool overrides make sure a consumer can still rebuild any general part that is missing or broken.\n\n## Every issue requirement and its execution plan\n\n| Requirement from the issue                                                         | Solution and plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Delivered evidence                                                                                                                                       |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| R1. That leads to three conclusions:\n\n1. **Text generation and one-shot work fit directly.** upcomputer's commit-message, PR, branch-name and title generation runs exactly these one-shot commands ([cross-cutting map §8](data/upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md)): `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema …` and `codex exec … --output-schema <file>`. With this PR they become `agent({ tool, jsonSchema, reasoningEffort, mcpConfig, strictMcpConfig, attachments })` plus `metadata.structuredOutput`, in either language. Locked-down flags such as `--tools \"\"` or `--ephemeral` go through `extraArgs`.\n2. **Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` would be new providers.** upcomputer has no driver for any of the three. agent-commander already runs all three with normalized metadata.\n3. **The long-lived drivers would only partly benefit.**\n   - **What they can reuse:** agent-commander's normalization (usage windows, context gauge, error classes, version checks) and process-group termination.\n   - **Live steer and interrupt:** available through `liveInput` for the stream-json CLIs (claude, qwen, agent). The JSON-RPC and ACP transports themselves are outside agent-commander's CLI model ([known limits](#known-limits)).\n\nHive Mind already depends on agent-commander. It gains native options for flags it currently builds by hand ([consumer migration](#consumer-migration)).\n\n## Gaps and fixes\n\nThe U gaps come from upcomputer and the H gaps from Hive Mind.                                                |\n\n### Left to the consumer\n\nThese were classified as product features. They stay in upcomputer and Hive Mind:\n\n- scheduler, task agents and usage-limit auto-resume (\"Continue where you left off\" after `limitResetsAt`, which the metadata already provides);\n- git-ref checkpoints, worktree creation and setup progress;\n- the per-session HTTP MCP server and its tokens, the MCP orchestration tools, and the ACP-to-MCP bridge;\n- text-generation operations (commit message, PR, branch, title) and their prompts;\n- size-bounded NDJSON event logs, OTLP and metrics;\n- systemd scopes, OOM scores, login-shell PATH capture and managed CLI downloads;\n- pairing, remote access, the headless server and the GUI;\n- the Claude OAuth usage and reset-credits API, and the Antigravity quota API, which are private HTTP endpoints rather than CLI behavior;\n- in-process SDK drivers for Cursor, Grok, Pi, Muse and Antigravity, which have no one-shot CLI that agent-commander could wrap.\n\nA consumer that needs one of these in agent-commander's style can add it per run with `toolOverrides` (U10) or `extraArgs`, without changing the library.\n\n## Known limits\n\n- **One-shot model.** agent-commander does not speak Codex app-server JSON-RPC, ACP, OpenCode's HTTP+SSE server or SDK sessions. Live steering exists only for the CLIs that read stream-json on stdin (claude, qwen, agent). Codex, OpenCode and Gemini read a plain prompt, so `liveInput` throws for them.\n- **Strict MCP.** Only Claude has `--strict-mcp-config`. Codex merges `-c mcp_servers` into `config.toml` (checked with codex 0.163 `mcp list --json`), and Qwen has no strict flag, so `strictMcpConfig` is rejected for both. OpenCode reads MCP servers only from `opencode.json`, so `mcpConfig` is rejected for it. Gemini and agent have no MCP flag.\n- **Attachments.** Gemini has no attachment flag. Qwen turns non-text content blocks into JSON text, so Qwen images sent through `liveInput` reach the model as text.\n- **Structured output.** Not supported by gemini, opencode or agent, so the option is rejected for them. Codex's inline schema uses bash process substitution (`<(printf …)`). All commands run through `bash -c`, so this works, and the fake-codex experiment checks that `$HOME`, backticks and quotes survive. Qwen reads a value that starts with `@` as a path, so agent-commander always passes the schema inline. Rust's `serde_json` sorts object keys, so a Rust schema reaches the CLI with sorted keys. The Rust TOML encoder for Codex MCP config sorts them too.\n- **Codex streaming.** `codex exec --json` streams neither `rate_limits` nor `token_count`, so usage windows and the context gauge for Codex come from the rollout file after the run.\n- **Rust differences.**\n  - Rust has no permission relay, so live input there is the only stdin channel, and `stop()` closes stdin at once.\n  - `CodexRolloutLimitFacts` has no context field; Rust uses the separate `codex_rollout_context_usage` helper instead.\n  - The Rust `ToolOverrides` has no `detect_errors` hook, because Rust error detection is built into the metadata builder. The JS relay with live input keeps stdin open until the result.\n- **Overrides.**\n  - Overrides do not relax read-only, plan or ask modes. The safety checks still run on the resolved tool.\n  - An unregistered tool gets generic metadata unless its overrides extract more.\n- **No live inference.** No paid inference was run. Native flags were checked against the installed CLIs' help text and vendor documentation, and the end-to-end paths use fake executables and `printf` overrides.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| These are the flags each option maps to.                                                                                                                        |\n| upcomputer source (read only)                                                                                                | The facts in both [maps](data/), with file and line references.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |\n| Hive Mind v2.39.5 source (read only)                                                                                          | `src/organize.ai.lib.mjs` lines 39–62 (schema and effort flags), `src/claude.lib.mjs` line 342 (strict MCP), `src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` line 98 (Codex effort through `extraArgs`), and the `--version` probes.                                                                                                                         |\n\n## Existing components and libraries\n\nThe following were considered before writing new code:\n\n- **Claude Agent SDK** (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`), which upcomputer uses. It is TypeScript-only and in-process, and it pins a bundled Claude Code. agent-commander must drive whatever `claude` binary is installed, from both JS and Rust. The SDK's message shapes (`rate_limit_event`, `structured_output`, stream-json input frames) are the same ones the CLI emits, so the parsers follow them.\n- **Codex app-server JSON-RPC.** It is richer than `codex exec`, with live rate limits, steer and revert, but it is a different transport and is still marked experimental (`experimentalApi: true`). Adding it would be a new driver, not a launch option. The rollout file gives the same rate-limit and token data after a run.\n- **ACP and the ACP registry.** A future ACP driver could cover Gemini (`gemini --experimental-acp`), Qwen and registry agents. It is a separate transport layer and does not replace the CLI runs this issue asks for.\n- **OpenCode server SDK** (`@opencode-ai/sdk`). It is JavaScript-only and server-based. `opencode run --file/--variant` covers the one-shot needs.\n- **command-stream.** It is still the quoting and terminal-capture base (issue #55). Process substitution for `--output-schema` reuses the shared quoting, so no new dependency was added.\n- **Hive Mind libraries.** Hive Mind's `bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs` and version probes informed U4 and U6. They were re-implemented generically rather than imported, as in issue #55.\n\n## Consumer migration\n\nEvery new option and metadata field is additive. Existing callers work unchanged.\n\n**Hive Mind** (`src/agent-commander.lib.mjs` and the direct CLI calls) can:\n\n1. replace the `-c model_reasoning_effort=…` `extraArgs` with `reasoningEffort`;\n2. replace hand-built `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <file>` with `mcpConfig` plus `strictMcpConfig`;\n3. move `organize.ai.lib.mjs` onto `agent({ jsonSchema, reasoningEffort })` and read `metadata.structuredOutput`, instead of temporary schema and output files;\n4. use `getToolVersion` instead of the per-tool `--version` probes;\n5. use `liveInput` with `sendMessage` / `interrupt` instead of its own stream-json writer;\n6. copy `usageWindows` and `contextUsage` into its result summary.\n\n**upcomputer** can:\n\n1. run its text generation (`ClaudeTextGeneration.ts`, `CodexTextGeneration.ts`) through agent-commander, using `jsonSchema`, `reasoningEffort`, `attachments`, `mcpConfig` and `strictMcpConfig`, with the lockdown flags in `extraArgs`;\n2. add Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` providers as one-shot runs;\n3. reuse `usageWindows` (the same shape as `providerUsageLimits.ts` windows), `contextUsage`, `getToolVersion` with its own compatibility ranges, and the error metadata, inside its long-lived drivers;\n4. replace any part that does not fit its product through `toolOverrides`.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run check && npm test\ncd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features && cargo doc --no-deps\nnode experiments/issue-57-launch-options.mjs\nnode experiments/issue-57-structured-output.mjs\n```\n\nVALIDATION_RESULTS\n"

[2026-10-22T14:36:20.580Z] [INFO]     "content": "# Issue #57: Can upcomputer benefit from agent-commander?\n\nThis case study compares [krl-gr/upcomputer](https://github.com/krl-gr/upcomputer) (\"The self-orchestrating control plane for coding agents\", TypeScript, MIT) and [link-assistant/hive-mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind) with agent-commander. It adds every general agent-control feature that either project needs and agent-commander lacked, in both the JavaScript and Rust bindings. It also makes the library replaceable piece by piece, so a consumer can swap a failing or missing part without waiting for a release.\n\nIssue: [agent-commander #57](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/issues/57). Implementation: [PR #58](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/58). The provider drivers are mapped in [upcomputer-provider-launch-map.md](data/upcomputer-provider-launch-map.md), using 7 dimensions: transport, lifecycle, models, permissions, inputs, outputs, install and health. The cross-cutting services are mapped in [upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md](data/upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md): limits, tokens, processes, scheduling, checkpoints, logs, MCP, text generation, worktrees, errors and remote operation.\n- **Hive Mind.** v2.39.5 (`5a7cb68`), the issue #55 pin. Each new flag was checked against this help text before it was used.\n- **agent-commander.** The baseline is JavaScript 0.11.1 / Rust 0.3.2 on `main`. The release fragments make this a minor release.\n\nBoth upstream repositories were treated as untrusted data. They were read and grepped only, never installed or run.\n\nThe issue has no comments, and PR #58 had no comments or reviews when work started.\n\nThe issue sets two rules for what belongs in agent-commander:\n\n- **General.** Launching, steering and reading native agent CLIs. Any consumer of the library needs this. It was implemented in both languages, behind options that are off by default.\n- **Project-specific.** Scheduling, checkpoints, worktrees, GUI, pairing and similar product features. These stay in the consumer. The new tool overrides make sure a consumer can still rebuild any general part that is missing or broken.\n\n## Every issue requirement and its execution plan\n\n| Requirement from the issue                                                         | Solution and plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Delivered evidence                                                                                                                                       |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| R1. That leads to three conclusions:\n\n1. **Text generation and one-shot work fit directly.** upcomputer's commit-message, PR, branch-name and title generation runs exactly these one-shot commands ([cross-cutting map §8](data/upcomputer-cross-cutting-map.md)): `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema …` and `codex exec … --output-schema <file>`. With this PR they become `agent({ tool, jsonSchema, reasoningEffort, mcpConfig, strictMcpConfig, attachments })` plus `metadata.structuredOutput`, in either language. Locked-down flags such as `--tools \"\"` or `--ephemeral` go through `extraArgs`.\n2. **Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` would be new providers.** upcomputer has no driver for any of the three. agent-commander already runs all three with normalized metadata.\n3. **The long-lived drivers would only partly benefit.**\n   - **What they can reuse:** agent-commander's normalization (usage windows, context gauge, error classes, version checks) and process-group termination.\n   - **Live steer and interrupt:** available through `liveInput` for the stream-json CLIs (claude, qwen, agent). The JSON-RPC and ACP transports themselves are outside agent-commander's CLI model ([known limits](#known-limits)).\n\nHive Mind already depends on agent-commander. It gains native options for flags it currently builds by hand ([consumer migration](#consumer-migration)).\n\n## Gaps and fixes\n\nThe U gaps come from upcomputer and the H gaps from Hive Mind. They stay in upcomputer and Hive Mind:\n\n- scheduler, task agents and usage-limit auto-resume (\"Continue where you left off\" after `limitResetsAt`, which the metadata already provides);\n- git-ref checkpoints, worktree creation and setup progress;\n- the per-session HTTP MCP server and its tokens, the MCP orchestration tools, and the ACP-to-MCP bridge;\n- text-generation operations (commit message, PR, branch, title) and their prompts;\n- size-bounded NDJSON event logs, OTLP and metrics;\n- systemd scopes, OOM scores, login-shell PATH capture and managed CLI downloads;\n- pairing, remote access, the headless server and the GUI;\n- the Claude OAuth usage and reset-credits API, and the Antigravity quota API, which are private HTTP endpoints rather than CLI behavior;\n- in-process SDK drivers for Cursor, Grok, Pi, Muse and Antigravity, which have no one-shot CLI that agent-commander could wrap.\n\nA consumer that needs one of these in agent-commander's style can add it per run with `toolOverrides` (U10) or `extraArgs`, without changing the library.\n\n## Known limits\n\n- **One-shot model.** agent-commander does not speak Codex app-server JSON-RPC, ACP, OpenCode's HTTP+SSE server or SDK sessions. Live steering exists only for the CLIs that read stream-json on stdin (claude, qwen, agent). Codex, OpenCode and Gemini read a plain prompt, so `liveInput` throws for them.\n- **Strict MCP.** Only Claude has `--strict-mcp-config`. Codex merges `-c mcp_servers` into `config.toml` (checked with codex 0.163 `mcp list --json`), and Qwen has no strict flag, so `strictMcpConfig` is rejected for both. OpenCode reads MCP servers only from `opencode.json`, so `mcpConfig` is rejected for it. Gemini and agent have no MCP flag.\n- **Attachments.** Gemini has no attachment flag. Qwen turns non-text content blocks into JSON text, so Qwen images sent through `liveInput` reach the model as text.\n- **Structured output.** Not supported by gemini, opencode or agent, so the option is rejected for them. Codex's inline schema uses bash process substitution (`<(printf …)`). All commands run through `bash -c`, so this works, and the fake-codex experiment checks that `$HOME`, backticks and quotes survive. Qwen reads a value that starts with `@` as a path, so agent-commander always passes the schema inline. Rust's `serde_json` sorts object keys, so a Rust schema reaches the CLI with sorted keys. The Rust TOML encoder for Codex MCP config sorts them too.\n- **Codex streaming.** `codex exec --json` streams neither `rate_limits` nor `token_count`, so usage windows and the context gauge for Codex come from the rollout file after the run.\n- **Rust differences.**\n  - Rust has no permission relay, so live input there is the only stdin channel, and `stop()` closes stdin at once.\n  - `CodexRolloutLimitFacts` has no context field; Rust uses the separate `codex_rollout_context_usage` helper instead.\n  - The Rust `ToolOverrides` has no `detect_errors` hook, because Rust error detection is built into the metadata builder. The JS relay with live input keeps stdin open until the result.\n- **Overrides.**\n  - Overrides do not relax read-only, plan or ask modes. The safety checks still run on the resolved tool.\n  - An unregistered tool gets generic metadata unless its overrides extract more.\n- **No live inference.** No paid inference was run. Native flags were checked against the installed CLIs' help text and vendor documentation, and the end-to-end paths use fake executables and `printf` overrides.\n\n## Primary-source research\n\n| Source                                                                                                                       | Fact used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | The SDK's message shapes (`rate_limit_event`, `structured_output`, stream-json input frames) are the same ones the CLI emits, so the parsers follow them.\n- **Codex app-server JSON-RPC.** It is richer than `codex exec`, with live rate limits, steer and revert, but it is a different transport and is still marked experimental (`experimentalApi: true`). Process substitution for `--output-schema` reuses the shared quoting, so no new dependency was added.\n- **Hive Mind libraries.** Hive Mind's `bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs` and version probes informed U4 and U6. [2026-10-22T14:37:39.848Z] [INFO]         "content": "> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n\n# Get structured output from agents\n\n> Return validated JSON from agent workflows using JSON Schema, Zod, or Pydantic. Get type-safe, structured data after multi-turn tool use.\n\nStructured outputs let you define the exact shape of data you want back from an agent. The agent can use any tools it needs to complete the task, and you still get validated JSON matching your schema at the end. Define a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/about) for the structure you need, and the SDK validates the output against it, re-prompting on mismatch. If validation does not succeed within the retry limit, the result is an error instead of structured data; see [Error handling](#error-handling).\n\nFor full type safety, use [Zod](#type-safe-schemas-with-zod-and-pydantic) (TypeScript) or [Pydantic](#type-safe-schemas-with-zod-and-pydantic) (Python) to define your schema and get strongly typed objects back.\n\n## Why structured outputs?\n\nAgents return free-form text by default, which works for chat but not when you need to use the output programmatically. Structured outputs give you typed data you can pass directly to your application logic, database, or UI components.\n\nConsider a recipe app where an agent searches the web and brings back recipes. Without structured outputs, you get free-form text that you'd need to parse yourself. With structured outputs, you define the shape you want and get typed data you can use directly in your app.\n\n> **Without structured outputs**\n>\n> ```text theme={null}\n> Here's a classic chocolate chip cookie recipe!\n>\n> **Chocolate Chip Cookies**\n> Prep time: 15 minutes | Cook time: 10 minutes\n>\n> Ingredients:\n> - 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour\n> - 1 cup butter, softened\n> ...\n> ```\n>\n> To use this in your app, you'd need to parse out the title, convert \"15 minutes\" to a number, separate ingredients from instructions, and handle inconsistent formatting across responses.\n\n> **With structured outputs**\n>\n> ```jsonc theme={null}\n> {\n>   \"name\": \"Chocolate Chip Cookies\",\n>   \"prep_time_minutes\": 15,\n>   \"cook_time_minutes\": 10,\n>   \"ingredients\": [\n>     { \"item\": \"all-purpose flour\", \"amount\": 2.25, \"unit\": \"cups\" },\n>     { \"item\": \"butter, softened\", \"amount\": 1, \"unit\": \"cup\" }\n>     // ...\n>   ],\n>   \"steps\": [\"Preheat oven to 375°F\", \"Cream butter and sugar\" /* ... */]\n> }\n> ```\n>\n> Typed data you can use directly in your UI.\n\n## Quick start\n\nTo use structured outputs, define a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/about) describing the shape of data you want, then pass it to `query()` via the `outputFormat` option (TypeScript) or `output_format` option (Python). When the agent finishes, the result message includes a `structured_output` field with validated data matching your schema.\n\nBefore running the examples on this page, install the Claude Agent SDK by following the [quickstart](/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart#setup). The example below asks the agent to research Anthropic and return the company name, year founded, and headquarters as structured output.\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\n// Define the shape of data you want back\nconst schema = {\n  type: \"object\",\n  properties: {\n    company_name: { type: \"string\" },\n    founded_year: { type: \"number\" },\n    headquarters: { type: \"string\" }\n  },\n  required: [\"company_name\"]\n};\n\ntry {\n  for await (const message of query({\n    prompt: \"Research Anthropic and provide key company information\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: schema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    // The result message contains structured_output with validated data\n    if (message.type === \"result\" && message.subtype === \"success\" && message.structured_output) {\n      console.log(message.structured_output);\n      // { company_name: \"Anthropic\", founded_year: 2021, headquarters: \"San Francisco, CA\" }\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result, such as\n  // error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n  console.error(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\n# Define the shape of data you want back\nschema = {\n    \"type\": \"object\",\n    \"properties\": {\n        \"company_name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n        \"founded_year\": {\"type\": \"number\"},\n        \"headquarters\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n    },\n    \"required\": [\"company_name\"],\n}\n\n\nasync def main():\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Research Anthropic and provide key company information\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": schema}\n            ),\n        ):\n            # The result message contains structured_output with validated data\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output:\n                print(message.structured_output)\n                # {'company_name': 'Anthropic', 'founded_year': 2021, 'headquarters': 'San Francisco, CA'}\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, such as\n        # error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Type-safe schemas with Zod and Pydantic\n\nInstead of writing JSON Schema by hand, you can use [Zod](https://zod.dev/) (TypeScript) or [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/) (Python) to define your schema. These libraries generate the JSON Schema for you and let you parse the response into a fully-typed object you can use throughout your codebase with autocomplete and type checking.\n\nThe example below defines a schema for a feature implementation plan with a summary, list of steps (each with complexity level), and potential risks. The agent plans the feature and returns a typed `FeaturePlan` object. You can then access properties like `plan.summary` and iterate over `plan.steps` with full type safety.\n\nThe SDK validates schemas with JSON Schema draft-07, so schemas that declare a newer version are rejected. Zod targets draft 2020-12 by default, so pass `target: \"draft-7\"` when converting your schema.\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\n// Define schema with Zod\nconst FeaturePlan = z.object({\n  feature_name: z.string(),\n  summary: z.string(),\n  steps: z.array(\n    z.object({\n      step_number: z.number(),\n      description: z.string(),\n      estimated_complexity: z.enum([\"low\", \"medium\", \"high\"])\n    })\n  ),\n  risks: z.array(z.string())\n});\n\ntype FeaturePlan = z.infer<typeof FeaturePlan>;\n\n// Convert to JSON Schema using the draft-07 target the SDK expects\nconst schema = z.toJSONSchema(FeaturePlan, { target: \"draft-7\" });\n\n// Use in query\ntry {\n  for await (const message of query({\n    prompt:\n      \"Plan how to add dark mode support to a React app. Break it into implementation steps.\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: schema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    if (message.type === \"result\" && message.subtype === \"success\" && message.structured_output) {\n      // Validate and get fully typed result\n      const parsed = FeaturePlan.safeParse(message.structured_output);\n      if (parsed.success) {\n        const plan: FeaturePlan = parsed.data;\n        console.log(`Feature: ${plan.feature_name}`);\n        console.log(`Summary: ${plan.summary}`);\n        plan.steps.forEach((step) => {\n          console.log(`${step.step_number}. [${step.estimated_complexity}] ${step.description}`);\n        });\n      }\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result, such as\n  // error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n  console.error(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\n\nclass Step(BaseModel):\n    step_number: int\n    description: str\n    estimated_complexity: str  # 'low', 'medium', 'high'\n\n\nclass FeaturePlan(BaseModel):\n    feature_name: str\n    summary: str\n    steps: list[Step]\n    risks: list[str]\n\n\nasync def main():\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Plan how to add dark mode support to a React app. Break it into implementation steps.\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\n                    \"type\": \"json_schema\",\n                    \"schema\": FeaturePlan.model_json_schema(),\n                }\n            ),\n        ):\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output:\n                # Validate and get fully typed result\n                plan = FeaturePlan.model_validate(message.structured_output)\n                print(f\"Feature: {plan.feature_name}\")\n                print(f\"Summary: {plan.summary}\")\n                for step in plan.steps:\n                    print(\n                        f\"{step.step_number}. [{step.estimated_complexity}] {step.description}\"\n                    )\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, such as\n        # error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Output format configuration\n\nThe `outputFormat` (TypeScript) or `output_format` (Python) option accepts an object with:\n\n* `type`: Set to `\"json_schema\"` for structured outputs\n* `schema`: A [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/about) object defining your output structure. You can generate this from a Zod schema with `z.toJSONSchema(schema, { target: \"draft-7\" })` or a Pydantic model with `.model_json_schema()`\n\nThe SDK supports standard JSON Schema features including all basic types (object, array, string, number, boolean, null), `enum`, `const`, `required`, nested objects, and `$ref` definitions. For the full list of supported features and limitations, see [JSON Schema limitations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs#json-schema-limitations).\n\nA schema that isn't valid JSON Schema fails the run at startup with an error naming the problem. Before v2.1.205, an invalid schema was silently ignored and the agent returned unstructured text.\n\nThe `format` keyword, such as `\"format\": \"email\"`, is accepted as an annotation and isn't enforced by the SDK's validator. Before v2.1.205, any schema containing `format` was treated as invalid.\n\n## Example: TODO tracking agent\n\nThis example demonstrates how structured outputs work with multi-step tool use. The agent needs to find TODO comments in the codebase, then look up git blame information for each one. It autonomously decides which tools to use (Grep to search, Bash to run git commands) and combines the results into a single structured response.\n\nThe schema includes optional fields (`author` and `date`) since git blame information might not be available for all files. The agent fills in what it can find and omits the rest.\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\n// Define structure for TODO extraction\nconst todoSchema = {\n  type: \"object\",\n  properties: {\n    todos: {\n      type: \"array\",\n      items: {\n        type: \"object\",\n        properties: {\n          text: { type: \"string\" },\n          file: { type: \"string\" },\n          line: { type: \"number\" },\n          author: { type: \"string\" },\n          date: { type: \"string\" }\n        },\n        required: [\"text\", \"file\", \"line\"]\n      }\n    },\n    total_count: { type: \"number\" }\n  },\n  required: [\"todos\", \"total_count\"]\n};\n\n// Agent uses Grep to find TODOs, Bash to get git blame info\ntry {\n  for await (const message of query({\n    prompt: \"Find all TODO comments in this codebase and identify who added them\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: todoSchema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    if (message.type === \"result\" && message.subtype === \"success\" && message.structured_output) {\n      const data = message.structured_output as { total_count: number; todos: Array<{ file: string; line: number; text: string; author?: string; date?: string }> };\n      console.log(`Found ${data.total_count} TODOs`);\n      data.todos.forEach((todo) => {\n        console.log(`${todo.file}:${todo.line} - ${todo.text}`);\n        if (todo.author) {\n          console.log(`  Added by ${todo.author} on ${todo.date}`);\n        }\n      });\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result, such as\n  // error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n  console.error(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\n# Define structure for TODO extraction\ntodo_schema = {\n    \"type\": \"object\",\n    \"properties\": {\n        \"todos\": {\n            \"type\": \"array\",\n            \"items\": {\n                \"type\": \"object\",\n                \"properties\": {\n                    \"text\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                    \"file\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                    \"line\": {\"type\": \"number\"},\n                    \"author\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                    \"date\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                },\n                \"required\": [\"text\", \"file\", \"line\"],\n            },\n        },\n        \"total_count\": {\"type\": \"number\"},\n    },\n    \"required\": [\"todos\", \"total_count\"],\n}\n\n\nasync def main():\n    # Agent uses Grep to find TODOs, Bash to get git blame info\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Find all TODO comments in this codebase and identify who added them\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": todo_schema}\n            ),\n        ):\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output:\n                data = message.structured_output\n                print(f\"Found {data['total_count']} TODOs\")\n                for todo in data[\"todos\"]:\n                    print(f\"{todo['file']}:{todo['line']} - {todo['text']}\")\n                    if \"author\" in todo:\n                        print(f\"  Added by {todo['author']} on {todo['date']}\")\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, such as\n        # error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Recognize the StructuredOutput tool call\n\nWhen you set `outputFormat` in TypeScript or `output_format` in Python, your message stream carries a tool call named `StructuredOutput` that you never defined. Claude Code adds this tool to the session, and the agent calls it to return its answer. The [system init message](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdksystemmessage) lists it in the `tools` array, and each call arrives as two blocks:\n\n* A `tool_use` block named `StructuredOutput`, whose input is the object the agent produced for your schema\n* A `tool_result` block reading `Structured output provided successfully`\n\nWhen that object doesn't match your schema, the `tool_result` carries `is_error: true` instead and the agent calls `StructuredOutput` again, so your stream can hold several calls for one query. Read the validated data from `structured_output` on the result message rather than from a `tool_use` block, and see [Error handling](#error-handling) for the result you get when no attempt succeeds.\n\nIf your application shows or logs tool calls, skip the ones named `StructuredOutput` so the mechanism doesn't appear as a step the agent chose. A `tool_result` block carries no tool name, only the `tool_use_id` of the call it answers, so match that against the `id` of each call you skipped.\n\n## Error handling\n\nStructured output generation can fail when the agent cannot produce valid JSON matching your schema. This typically happens when the schema is too complex for the task, the task itself is ambiguous, or the agent hits its retry limit trying to fix validation errors. It can also happen without any validation failure: a [model fallback](/docs/en/model-config#automatic-model-fallback) can retract an already-completed output mid-stream, and if no retry replaces it the run ends with the same error. Check the `errors` list on the error result message to tell the two causes apart before debugging your schema.\n\nWhen an error occurs, the result message has a `subtype` indicating what went wrong:\n\n| Subtype | Meaning |\n| - | - |\n| `success` | Output was generated and validated successfully |\n| `error_max_structured_output_retries` | No valid output remained after multiple attempts (validation failures, or a model-fallback retraction with no successful retry) |\n\nA result can also end with subtype `success` but no `structured_output` value, for example when the run completes without the agent producing a structured output. Treat that case as a failure as well. The troubleshooting entry [structured\\_output is None but the result says success](/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#structured_output-is-none-but-the-result-says-success) covers this case. The example below treats a result as successful only when the `subtype` is `success` and `structured_output` is present, and handles every other result as a failure:\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\nconst contactSchema = {\n  type: \"object\",\n  properties: {\n    name: { type: \"string\" },\n    email: { type: \"string\" }\n  },\n  required: [\"name\"]\n};\n\ntry {\n  for await (const msg of query({\n    prompt: \"Extract contact info from the document\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: contactSchema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    if (msg.type === \"result\") {\n      if (msg.subtype === \"success\" && msg.structured_output) {\n        // Use the validated output\n        console.log(msg.structured_output);\n      } else if (msg.subtype === \"error_max_structured_output_retries\") {\n        console.error(\"Could not produce valid output\");\n      } else {\n        console.error(\"Run ended without a structured output\");\n      }\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result. If the\n  // failure was an error result, the error subtype branches above have\n  // already run; connection or process failures yield no result message.\n  console.log(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\ncontact_schema = {\n    \"type\": \"object\",\n    \"properties\": {\n        \"name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n        \"email\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n    },\n    \"required\": [\"name\"],\n}\n\n\nasync def main():\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Extract contact info from the document\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": contact_schema}\n            ),\n        ):\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage):\n                if message.subtype == \"success\" and message.structured_output:\n                    # Use the validated output\n                    print(message.structured_output)\n                elif message.subtype == \"error_max_structured_output_retries\":\n                    print(\"Could not produce valid output\")\n                else:\n                    print(\"Run ended without a structured output\")\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result. If the\n        # failure was an error result, the error subtype branches above have\n        # already run; connection or process failures yield no result message.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n**Tips for avoiding errors:**\n\n* **Keep schemas focused.** Deeply nested schemas with many required fields are harder to satisfy. Start simple and add complexity as needed.\n* **Match schema to task.** If the task might not have all the information your schema requires, make those fields optional.\n* **Use clear prompts.** Ambiguous prompts make it harder for the agent to know what output to produce.\n\n## Related resources\n\n* [JSON Schema documentation](https://json-schema.org/): learn JSON Schema syntax for defining complex schemas with nested objects, arrays, enums, and validation constraints\n* [API Structured Outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs): use structured outputs with the Claude API directly for single-turn requests without tool use\n* [Custom tools](/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools): give your agent custom tools to call during execution before returning structured output\n"

Get type-safe, structured data after multi-turn tool use.\n\nStructured outputs let you define the exact shape of data you want back from an agent. The agent can use any tools it needs to complete the task, and you still get validated JSON matching your schema at the end. Define a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/about) for the structure you need, and the SDK validates the output against it, re-prompting on mismatch. If validation does not succeed within the retry limit, the result is an error instead of structured data; see [Error handling](#error-handling).\n\nFor full type safety, use [Zod](#type-safe-schemas-with-zod-and-pydantic) (TypeScript) or [Pydantic](#type-safe-schemas-with-zod-and-pydantic) (Python) to define your schema and get strongly typed objects back.\n\n## Why structured outputs?\n\nAgents return free-form text by default, which works for chat but not when you need to use the output programmatically. Structured outputs give you typed data you can pass directly to your application logic, database, or UI components.\n\nConsider a recipe app where an agent searches the web and brings back recipes. Without structured outputs, you get free-form text that you'd need to parse yourself. With structured outputs, you define the shape you want and get typed data you can use directly in your app.\n\n> **Without structured outputs**\n>\n> ```text theme={null}\n> Here's a classic chocolate chip cookie recipe!\n>\n> **Chocolate Chip Cookies**\n> Prep time: 15 minutes | Cook time: 10 minutes\n>\n> Ingredients:\n> - 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour\n> - 1 cup butter, softened\n> ...\n> ```\n>\n> To use this in your app, you'd need to parse out the title, convert \"15 minutes\" to a number, separate ingredients from instructions, and handle inconsistent formatting across responses.\n\n> **With structured outputs**\n>\n> ```jsonc theme={null}\n> {\n>   \"name\": \"Chocolate Chip Cookies\",\n>   \"prep_time_minutes\": 15,\n>   \"cook_time_minutes\": 10,\n>   \"ingredients\": [\n>     { \"item\": \"all-purpose flour\", \"amount\": 2.25, \"unit\": \"cups\" },\n>     { \"item\": \"butter, softened\", \"amount\": 1, \"unit\": \"cup\" }\n>     // ...\n>   ],\n>   \"steps\": [\"Preheat oven to 375°F\", \"Cream butter and sugar\" /* ... */]\n> }\n> ```\n>\n> Typed data you can use directly in your UI.\n\n## Quick start\n\nTo use structured outputs, define a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/about) describing the shape of data you want, then pass it to `query()` via the `outputFormat` option (TypeScript) or `output_format` option (Python). When the agent finishes, the result message includes a `structured_output` field with validated data matching your schema.\n\nBefore running the examples on this page, install the Claude Agent SDK by following the [quickstart](/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart#setup). The example below asks the agent to research Anthropic and return the company name, year founded, and headquarters as structured output.\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\n// Define the shape of data you want back\nconst schema = {\n  type: \"object\",\n  properties: {\n    company_name: { type: \"string\" },\n    founded_year: { type: \"number\" },\n    headquarters: { type: \"string\" }\n  },\n  required: [\"company_name\"]\n};\n\ntry {\n  for await (const message of query({\n    prompt: \"Research Anthropic and provide key company information\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: schema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    // The result message contains structured_output with validated data\n    if (message.type === \"result\" && message.subtype === \"success\" && message.structured_output) {\n      console.log(message.structured_output);\n      // { company_name: \"Anthropic\", founded_year: 2021, headquarters: \"San Francisco, CA\" }\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result, such as\n  // error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n  console.error(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\n# Define the shape of data you want back\nschema = {\n    \"type\": \"object\",\n    \"properties\": {\n        \"company_name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n        \"founded_year\": {\"type\": \"number\"},\n        \"headquarters\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n    },\n    \"required\": [\"company_name\"],\n}\n\n\nasync def main():\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Research Anthropic and provide key company information\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": schema}\n            ),\n        ):\n            # The result message contains structured_output with validated data\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output:\n                print(message.structured_output)\n                # {'company_name': 'Anthropic', 'founded_year': 2021, 'headquarters': 'San Francisco, CA'}\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, such as\n        # error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Type-safe schemas with Zod and Pydantic\n\nInstead of writing JSON Schema by hand, you can use [Zod](https://zod.dev/) (TypeScript) or [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/) (Python) to define your schema. These libraries generate the JSON Schema for you and let you parse the response into a fully-typed object you can use throughout your codebase with autocomplete and type checking.\n\nThe example below defines a schema for a feature implementation plan with a summary, list of steps (each with complexity level), and potential risks. The agent plans the feature and returns a typed `FeaturePlan` object. You can then access properties like `plan.summary` and iterate over `plan.steps` with full type safety.\n\nThe SDK validates schemas with JSON Schema draft-07, so schemas that declare a newer version are rejected. Zod targets draft 2020-12 by default, so pass `target: \"draft-7\"` when converting your schema.\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { z } from \"zod\";\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\n// Define schema with Zod\nconst FeaturePlan = z.object({\n  feature_name: z.string(),\n  summary: z.string(),\n  steps: z.array(\n    z.object({\n      step_number: z.number(),\n      description: z.string(),\n      estimated_complexity: z.enum([\"low\", \"medium\", \"high\"])\n    })\n  ),\n  risks: z.array(z.string())\n});\n\ntype FeaturePlan = z.infer<typeof FeaturePlan>;\n\n// Convert to JSON Schema using the draft-07 target the SDK expects\nconst schema = z.toJSONSchema(FeaturePlan, { target: \"draft-7\" });\n\n// Use in query\ntry {\n  for await (const message of query({\n    prompt:\n      \"Plan how to add dark mode support to a React app. Break it into implementation steps.\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: schema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    if (message.type === \"result\" && message.subtype === \"success\" && message.structured_output) {\n      // Validate and get fully typed result\n      const parsed = FeaturePlan.safeParse(message.structured_output);\n      if (parsed.success) {\n        const plan: FeaturePlan = parsed.data;\n        console.log(`Feature: ${plan.feature_name}`);\n        console.log(`Summary: ${plan.summary}`);\n        plan.steps.forEach((step) => {\n          console.log(`${step.step_number}. [${step.estimated_complexity}] ${step.description}`);\n        });\n      }\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result, such as\n  // error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n  console.error(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\n\nclass Step(BaseModel):\n    step_number: int\n    description: str\n    estimated_complexity: str  # 'low', 'medium', 'high'\n\n\nclass FeaturePlan(BaseModel):\n    feature_name: str\n    summary: str\n    steps: list[Step]\n    risks: list[str]\n\n\nasync def main():\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Plan how to add dark mode support to a React app. Break it into implementation steps.\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\n                    \"type\": \"json_schema\",\n                    \"schema\": FeaturePlan.model_json_schema(),\n                }\n            ),\n        ):\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output:\n                # Validate and get fully typed result\n                plan = FeaturePlan.model_validate(message.structured_output)\n                print(f\"Feature: {plan.feature_name}\")\n                print(f\"Summary: {plan.summary}\")\n                for step in plan.steps:\n                    print(\n                        f\"{step.step_number}. [{step.estimated_complexity}] {step.description}\"\n                    )\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, such as\n        # error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Output format configuration\n\nThe `outputFormat` (TypeScript) or `output_format` (Python) option accepts an object with:\n\n* `type`: Set to `\"json_schema\"` for structured outputs\n* `schema`: A [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/about) object defining your output structure. You can generate this from a Zod schema with `z.toJSONSchema(schema, { target: \"draft-7\" })` or a Pydantic model with `.model_json_schema()`\n\nThe SDK supports standard JSON Schema features including all basic types (object, array, string, number, boolean, null), `enum`, `const`, `required`, nested objects, and `$ref` definitions. For the full list of supported features and limitations, see [JSON Schema limitations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs#json-schema-limitations).\n\nA schema that isn't valid JSON Schema fails the run at startup with an error naming the problem. Before v2.1.205, an invalid schema was silently ignored and the agent returned unstructured text.\n\nThe `format` keyword, such as `\"format\": \"email\"`, is accepted as an annotation and isn't enforced by the SDK's validator. Before v2.1.205, any schema containing `format` was treated as invalid.\n\n## Example: TODO tracking agent\n\nThis example demonstrates how structured outputs work with multi-step tool use. The agent needs to find TODO comments in the codebase, then look up git blame information for each one. It autonomously decides which tools to use (Grep to search, Bash to run git commands) and combines the results into a single structured response.\n\nThe schema includes optional fields (`author` and `date`) since git blame information might not be available for all files. The agent fills in what it can find and omits the rest.\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\n// Define structure for TODO extraction\nconst todoSchema = {\n  type: \"object\",\n  properties: {\n    todos: {\n      type: \"array\",\n      items: {\n        type: \"object\",\n        properties: {\n          text: { type: \"string\" },\n          file: { type: \"string\" },\n          line: { type: \"number\" },\n          author: { type: \"string\" },\n          date: { type: \"string\" }\n        },\n        required: [\"text\", \"file\", \"line\"]\n      }\n    },\n    total_count: { type: \"number\" }\n  },\n  required: [\"todos\", \"total_count\"]\n};\n\n// Agent uses Grep to find TODOs, Bash to get git blame info\ntry {\n  for await (const message of query({\n    prompt: \"Find all TODO comments in this codebase and identify who added them\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: todoSchema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    if (message.type === \"result\" && message.subtype === \"success\" && message.structured_output) {\n      const data = message.structured_output as { total_count: number; todos: Array<{ file: string; line: number; text: string; author?: string; date?: string }> };\n      console.log(`Found ${data.total_count} TODOs`);\n      data.todos.forEach((todo) => {\n        console.log(`${todo.file}:${todo.line} - ${todo.text}`);\n        if (todo.author) {\n          console.log(`  Added by ${todo.author} on ${todo.date}`);\n        }\n      });\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result, such as\n  // error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n  console.error(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\n# Define structure for TODO extraction\ntodo_schema = {\n    \"type\": \"object\",\n    \"properties\": {\n        \"todos\": {\n            \"type\": \"array\",\n            \"items\": {\n                \"type\": \"object\",\n                \"properties\": {\n                    \"text\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                    \"file\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                    \"line\": {\"type\": \"number\"},\n                    \"author\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                    \"date\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n                },\n                \"required\": [\"text\", \"file\", \"line\"],\n            },\n        },\n        \"total_count\": {\"type\": \"number\"},\n    },\n    \"required\": [\"todos\", \"total_count\"],\n}\n\n\nasync def main():\n    # Agent uses Grep to find TODOs, Bash to get git blame info\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Find all TODO comments in this codebase and identify who added them\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": todo_schema}\n            ),\n        ):\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage) and message.structured_output:\n                data = message.structured_output\n                print(f\"Found {data['total_count']} TODOs\")\n                for todo in data[\"todos\"]:\n                    print(f\"{todo['file']}:{todo['line']} - {todo['text']}\")\n                    if \"author\" in todo:\n                        print(f\"  Added by {todo['author']} on {todo['date']}\")\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result, such as\n        # error_max_structured_output_retries; see the Error handling section.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Recognize the StructuredOutput tool call\n\nWhen you set `outputFormat` in TypeScript or `output_format` in Python, your message stream carries a tool call named `StructuredOutput` that you never defined. Claude Code adds this tool to the session, and the agent calls it to return its answer. The [system init message](/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#sdksystemmessage) lists it in the `tools` array, and each call arrives as two blocks:\n\n* A `tool_use` block named `StructuredOutput`, whose input is the object the agent produced for your schema\n* A `tool_result` block reading `Structured output provided successfully`\n\nWhen that object doesn't match your schema, the `tool_result` carries `is_error: true` instead and the agent calls `StructuredOutput` again, so your stream can hold several calls for one query. Read the validated data from `structured_output` on the result message rather than from a `tool_use` block, and see [Error handling](#error-handling) for the result you get when no attempt succeeds.\n\nIf your application shows or logs tool calls, skip the ones named `StructuredOutput` so the mechanism doesn't appear as a step the agent chose. A `tool_result` block carries no tool name, only the `tool_use_id` of the call it answers, so match that against the `id` of each call you skipped.\n\n## Error handling\n\nStructured output generation can fail when the agent cannot produce valid JSON matching your schema. This typically happens when the schema is too complex for the task, the task itself is ambiguous, or the agent hits its retry limit trying to fix validation errors. It can also happen without any validation failure: a [model fallback](/docs/en/model-config#automatic-model-fallback) can retract an already-completed output mid-stream, and if no retry replaces it the run ends with the same error. Check the `errors` list on the error result message to tell the two causes apart before debugging your schema.\n\nWhen an error occurs, the result message has a `subtype` indicating what went wrong:\n\n| Subtype | Meaning |\n| - | - |\n| `success` | Output was generated and validated successfully |\n| `error_max_structured_output_retries` | No valid output remained after multiple attempts (validation failures, or a model-fallback retraction with no successful retry) |\n\nA result can also end with subtype `success` but no `structured_output` value, for example when the run completes without the agent producing a structured output. Treat that case as a failure as well. The troubleshooting entry [structured\\_output is None but the result says success](/docs/en/agent-sdk/troubleshooting#structured_output-is-none-but-the-result-says-success) covers this case. The example below treats a result as successful only when the `subtype` is `success` and `structured_output` is present, and handles every other result as a failure:\n\n```typescript TypeScript theme={null}\nimport { query } from \"@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk\";\n\nconst contactSchema = {\n  type: \"object\",\n  properties: {\n    name: { type: \"string\" },\n    email: { type: \"string\" }\n  },\n  required: [\"name\"]\n};\n\ntry {\n  for await (const msg of query({\n    prompt: \"Extract contact info from the document\",\n    options: {\n      outputFormat: {\n        type: \"json_schema\",\n        schema: contactSchema\n      }\n    }\n  })) {\n    if (msg.type === \"result\") {\n      if (msg.subtype === \"success\" && msg.structured_output) {\n        // Use the validated output\n        console.log(msg.structured_output);\n      } else if (msg.subtype === \"error_max_structured_output_retries\") {\n        console.error(\"Could not produce valid output\");\n      } else {\n        console.error(\"Run ended without a structured output\");\n      }\n    }\n  }\n} catch (error) {\n  // A single-shot query() throws after yielding an error result. If the\n  // failure was an error result, the error subtype branches above have\n  // already run; connection or process failures yield no result message.\n  console.log(`Session ended with an error: ${error}`);\n}\n```\n\n```python Python theme={null}\nimport asyncio\nfrom claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage\n\ncontact_schema = {\n    \"type\": \"object\",\n    \"properties\": {\n        \"name\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n        \"email\": {\"type\": \"string\"},\n    },\n    \"required\": [\"name\"],\n}\n\n\nasync def main():\n    try:\n        async for message in query(\n            prompt=\"Extract contact info from the document\",\n            options=ClaudeAgentOptions(\n                output_format={\"type\": \"json_schema\", \"schema\": contact_schema}\n            ),\n        ):\n            if isinstance(message, ResultMessage):\n                if message.subtype == \"success\" and message.structured_output:\n                    # Use the validated output\n                    print(message.structured_output)\n                elif message.subtype == \"error_max_structured_output_retries\":\n                    print(\"Could not produce valid output\")\n                else:\n                    print(\"Run ended without a structured output\")\n    except Exception as error:\n        # A single-shot query() raises after yielding an error result. If the\n        # failure was an error result, the error subtype branches above have\n        # already run; connection or process failures yield no result message.\n        print(f\"Session ended with an error: {error}\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n**Tips for avoiding errors:**\n\n* **Keep schemas focused.** Deeply nested schemas with many required fields are harder to satisfy. Start simple and add complexity as needed.\n* **Match schema to task.** If the task might not have all the information your schema requires, make those fields optional.\n* **Use clear prompts.** Ambiguous prompts make it harder for the agent to know what output to produce.\n\n## Related resources\n\n* [JSON Schema documentation](https://json-schema.org/): learn JSON Schema syntax for defining complex schemas with nested objects, arrays, enums, and validation constraints\n* [API Structured Outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs): use structured outputs with the Claude API directly for single-turn requests without tool use\n* [Custom tools](/docs/en/agent-sdk/custom-tools): give your agent custom tools to call during execution before returning structured output\n",

Finally, it makes each part of a tool replaceable per run, so a project can swap a failing or missing part without forking the library.\n\n**Short answer:** yes for one-shot runs, and partly for long-lived sessions.\n\n- **Text generation fits directly.** upcomputer's text generation runs the same `claude -p --json-schema` and `codex exec --output-schema` commands that agent-commander can now express.\n- **New providers.** Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` would be new providers for upcomputer.\n- **Long-lived drivers reuse the normalization only.** Its SDK, JSON-RPC, ACP and HTTP drivers can reuse the normalized usage windows, context gauge, version probe and error metadata. Their transports stay outside agent-commander's CLI model.\n\nThe full analysis is in the [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/blob/issue-57-78ec18ab83ff/docs/case-studies/issue-57/README.md).\n\n### New features\n\n**Launch options.** Each maps to the tool's native flag and is rejected, naming the tools that support it, when the tool has none:\n\n| Option (JS / Rust / CLI) | claude | codex | opencode | qwen | gemini |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `reasoningEffort` / `reasoning_effort` / `--reasoning-effort` | `--effort` | `-c model_reasoning_effort=` | `--variant` | – | – |\n| `mcpConfig` / `mcp_config` / `--mcp-config` | `--mcp-config` | `-c mcp_servers={…}` | – | `--mcp-config` | – |\n| `strictMcpConfig` / `--strict-mcp-config` | `--strict-mcp-config` | – | – | – | – |\n| `additionalDirectories` / `--add-dir` | `--add-dir` | `--add-dir` | – | `--include-directories` | `--include-directories` |\n| `attachments` / `--attach` | – | `--image` | `run --file` | – | – |\n| `jsonSchema` / `json_schema` / `--json-schema` | `--json-schema` | `--output-schema <(…)` | – | `--json-schema` | – |\n\n**New result metadata:**\n\n- `usageWindows`: session, weekly and other subscription windows. They come from Claude `rate_limit_event` and Codex `rate_limits`, or from the Codex rollout file.\n- `contextUsage`: the context-window gauge.\n- `structuredOutput`: the schema-shaped answer.\n\n**Live input.** `liveInput` adds `sendMessage(text, { images })`, `interrupt()` and `endInput()` to steer a running claude, qwen or agent turn.\n\n**Version probe.** `getToolVersion`, `parseToolVersion`, `compareVersions` and `buildVersionCommand`.\n\n**Tool overrides.** `toolOverrides` (JS) and `ToolOverrides` (Rust) replace any of these for one run, or drive a tool that is not registered:\n\n- the command builder and the output parser;\n- the session-id, usage or error extractors;\n- the executable and the capability flags.\n\n`escapeArg` / `escape_arg` are exported for override builders.\n\n**Out of scope.** Project-specific features stay in the consumers: scheduler, checkpoints, worktrees, the per-session MCP server, logs, pairing and remote access, GUI, private usage APIs and SDK-only drivers. The case study explains why each was excluded.\n\n### Commits\n\n| Feature | JavaScript | Rust |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Effort, MCP and add-dir | 257cf4a | 1f9c84f |\n| Version probe | 6dec642 | 6dec642 |\n| Usage windows | 60773ae | 60773ae |\n| Live input | a6ee043 | 6017aef |\n| Context usage | 4a3589d | 4a3589d |\n| Attachments | 36c349f | 36c349f |\n| Tool overrides | f847dcb | 8489e12 |\n| Structured output | 30e0fa2 | a8f1175 |\n\nDocumentation is in `10d678f`, `5b5b843` and `8b9aee0`, and the case study in `9a5de09`.\n\n## Tests\n\n- **JavaScript.** New test files:\n  - `context-usage`\n  - `launch-options`\n  - `live-input`\n  - `structured-output`\n  - `tool-overrides`\n  - `tool-version`\n  - `usage-windows`\n\n  407 tests pass.
