Their transports stay outside agent-commander's CLI model.\n\nThe full analysis is in the [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/blob/issue-57-78ec18ab83ff/docs/case-studies/issue-57/README.md).\n\n### New features\n\n**Launch options.** Each maps to the tool's native flag and is rejected, naming the tools that support it, when the tool has none:\n\n| Option (JS / Rust / CLI) | claude | codex | opencode | qwen | gemini |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `reasoningEffort` / `reasoning_effort` / `--reasoning-effort` | `--effort` | `-c model_reasoning_effort=` | `--variant` | – | – |\n| `mcpConfig` / `mcp_config` / `--mcp-config` | `--mcp-config` | `-c mcp_servers={…}` | – | `--mcp-config` | – |\n| `strictMcpConfig` / `--strict-mcp-config` | `--strict-mcp-config` | – | – | – | – |\n| `additionalDirectories` / `--add-dir` | `--add-dir` | `--add-dir` | – | `--include-directories` | `--include-directories` |\n| `attachments` / `--attach` | – | `--image` | `run --file` | – | – |\n| `jsonSchema` / `json_schema` / `--json-schema` | `--json-schema` | `--output-schema <(…)` | – | `--json-schema` | – |\n\n**New result metadata:**\n\n- `usageWindows`: session, weekly and other subscription windows. They come from Claude `rate_limit_event` and Codex `rate_limits`, or from the Codex rollout file.\n- `contextUsage`: the context-window gauge.\n- `structuredOutput`: the schema-shaped answer.\n\n**Live input.** `liveInput` adds `sendMessage(text, { images })`, `interrupt()` and `endInput()` to steer a running claude, qwen or agent turn.\n\n**Version probe.** `getToolVersion`, `parseToolVersion`, `compareVersions` and `buildVersionCommand`.\n\n**Tool overrides.** `toolOverrides` (JS) and `ToolOverrides` (Rust) replace any of these for one run, or drive a tool that is not registered:\n\n- the command builder and the output parser;\n- the session-id, usage or error extractors;\n- the executable and the capability flags.\n\n`escapeArg` / `escape_arg` are exported for override builders.\n\n**Out of scope.** Project-specific features stay in the consumers: scheduler, checkpoints, worktrees, the per-session MCP server, logs, pairing and remote access, GUI, private usage APIs and SDK-only drivers. The case study explains why each was excluded.\n\n### Commits\n\n| Feature | JavaScript | Rust |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Effort, MCP and add-dir | 257cf4a | 1f9c84f |\n| Version probe | 6dec642 | 6dec642 |\n| Usage windows | 60773ae | 60773ae |\n| Live input | a6ee043 | 6017aef |\n| Context usage | 4a3589d | 4a3589d |\n| Attachments | 36c349f | 36c349f |\n| Tool overrides | f847dcb | 8489e12 |\n| Structured output | 30e0fa2 | a8f1175 |\n\nDocumentation is in `10d678f`, `5b5b843` and `8b9aee0`, and the case study in `9a5de09`.\n\n## Tests\n\n- **JavaScript.** New test files:\n  - `context-usage`\n  - `launch-options`\n  - `live-input`\n  - `structured-output`\n  - `tool-overrides`\n  - `tool-version`\n  - `usage-windows`\n\n  407 tests pass. Summary\n\nThis PR answers issue #57: can [krl-gr/upcomputer](https://github.com/krl-gr/upcomputer) benefit from agent-commander? It also adds every general agent-control feature that upcomputer and [Hive Mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind) need and agent-commander lacked, in **both JavaScript and Rust**. Finally, it makes each part of a tool replaceable per run, so a project can swap a failing or missing part without forking the library.\n\n**Short answer:** yes for one-shot runs, and partly for long-lived sessions.\n\n- **Text generation fits directly.** upcomputer's text generation runs the same `claude -p --json-schema` and `codex exec --output-schema` commands that agent-commander can now express.\n- **New providers.** Gemini, Qwen and `@link-assistant/agent` would be new providers for upcomputer.\n- **Long-lived drivers reuse the normalization only.** Its SDK, JSON-RPC, ACP and HTTP drivers can reuse the normalized usage windows, context gauge, version probe and error metadata. Their transports stay outside agent-commander's CLI model.\n\nThe full analysis is in the [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/blob/issue-57-78ec18ab83ff/docs/case-studies/issue-57/README.md).\n\n### New features\n\n**Launch options.** Each maps to the tool's native flag and is rejected, naming the tools that support it, when the tool has none:\n\n| Option (JS / Rust / CLI) | claude | codex | opencode | qwen | gemini |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `reasoningEffort` / `reasoning_effort` / `--reasoning-effort` | `--effort` | `-c model_reasoning_effort=` | `--variant` | – | – |\n| `mcpConfig` / `mcp_config` / `--mcp-config` | `--mcp-config` | `-c mcp_servers={…}` | – | `--mcp-config` | – |\n| `strictMcpConfig` / `--strict-mcp-config` | `--strict-mcp-config` | – | – | – | – |\n| `additionalDirectories` / `--add-dir` | `--add-dir` | `--add-dir` | – | `--include-directories` | `--include-directories` |\n| `attachments` / `--attach` | – | `--image` | `run --file` | – | – |\n| `jsonSchema` / `json_schema` / `--json-schema` | `--json-schema` | `--output-schema <(…)` | – | `--json-schema` | – |\n\n**New result metadata:**\n\n- `usageWindows`: session, weekly and other subscription windows. They come from Claude `rate_limit_event` and Codex `rate_limits`, or from the Codex rollout file.\n- `contextUsage`: the context-window gauge.\n- `structuredOutput`: the schema-shaped answer.\n\n**Live input.** `liveInput` adds `sendMessage(text, { images })`, `interrupt()` and `endInput()` to steer a running claude, qwen or agent turn.\n\n**Version probe.** `getToolVersion`, `parseToolVersion`, `compareVersions` and `buildVersionCommand`.\n\n**Tool overrides.** `toolOverrides` (JS) and `ToolOverrides` (Rust) replace any of these for one run, or drive a tool that is not registered:\n\n- the command builder and the output parser;\n- the session-id, usage or error extractors;\n- the executable and the capability flags.\n\n`escapeArg` / `escape_arg` are exported for override builders.\n\n**Out of scope.** Project-specific features stay in the consumers: scheduler, checkpoints, worktrees, the per-session MCP server, logs, pairing and remote access, GUI, private usage APIs and SDK-only drivers. The case study explains why each was excluded.\n\n### Commits\n\n| Feature | JavaScript | Rust |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Effort, MCP and add-dir | 257cf4a | 1f9c84f |\n| Version probe | 6dec642 | 6dec642 |\n| Usage windows | 60773ae | 60773ae |\n| Live input | a6ee043 | 6017aef |\n| Context usage | 4a3589d | 4a3589d |\n| Attachments | 36c349f | 36c349f |\n| Tool overrides | f847dcb | 8489e12 |\n| Structured output | 30e0fa2 | a8f1175 |\n\nDocumentation is in `10d678f`, `5b5b843` and `8b9aee0`, and the case study in `9a5de09`.\n\nWindows CI fixes:\n\n- `9574417` limits the new Rust tests that spawn processes to Unix, like the existing executor tests. On Windows runners `bash` is the WSL launcher without a distribution.\n- `9139f9e` gives each TUI capture test its own 30 s budget. Before, six serial ConPTY captures shared one budget and timed out at 35–41 s on node and bun (normally 13–18 s). Main's JS CI also fails on Windows (run 39782822431: deno timeout in `command-stream.test.mjs`).\n\n## Tests\n\n- **JavaScript.** New test files:\n  - `context-usage`\n  - `launch-options`\n  - `live-input`\n  - `structured-output`\n  - `tool-overrides`\n  - `tool-version`\n  - `usage-windows`\n\n  417 tests pass (the TUI capture tests now run once per client). ESLint reports 0 errors and the same 30 warnings as `main`; Prettier and the duplication check pass.\n- **Rust.** New test files, mirroring the JavaScript ones:\n  - `command_builder_modes`\n  - `context_usage`\n  - `launch_options`\n  - `live_input`\n  - `structured_output`\n  - `tool_overrides`\n  - `tool_version`\n  - `usage_windows`\n\n  403 tests pass. `fmt`, pedantic `clippy -D warnings`, the file-size check and `cargo doc` pass.\n- **Experiments.**\n  - `experiments/issue-57-launch-options.mjs` prints each tool's native command and the rejections.\n  - `experiments/issue-57-structured-output.mjs` runs a fake `codex` that reads the `--output-schema` process substitution back intact.\n- **Examples.** `examples/tool-overrides.mjs` and `rust/examples/tool_overrides.rs`.\n- **No paid inference was run.** The flags were checked against the installed CLIs' help text (saved in `docs/case-studies/issue-57/data/cli-help`) and vendor documentation.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```bash\ncd js && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm test\ncd ../rust && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test --all-features\nnode ../experiments/issue-57-launch-options.mjs\n```\n\n## Release\n\n- `js/.changeset/upcomputer-agent-control.md` (minor).\n-
